sections.title: Key concepts

title: Energy Flow and the 10% Rule
subtitle: The Living World: Ecosystems

sections.title: Energy Flow and the 10% Rule
traps: Applying the 10% rule to matter/nutrients — nutrients recycle, energy does not; the 10% rule is energy-only; confusing these on FRQ loses full credit

title: Biogeochemical Cycles — Carbon, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Water

overview: The Living World: Ecosystems 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion, ocean buffering
fixation (N₂ → NH₃), nitrification, denitrification pathways
no atmospheric reservoir; slow weathering release

traps: Confusing nitrogen fixation with nitrification — fixation converts N₂ gas to usable NH₃ (only bacteria do this); nitrification converts NH₃ to NO₃⁻

terms.def: tropical rainforest, temperate deciduous, grassland, desert, tundra

objectives: Competitive exclusion principle and niche partitioning as its resolution

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: what's possible vs. what's achieved
fitness effects on each partner

traps: Confusing fundamental (potential) with realized (actual) niche — competitive exclusion shrinks the realized niche; AP asks which is wider and why

title: Ecosystem Services — What Nature Provides
subtitle: The Living World: Ecosystems

objectives: NPP = GPP - respiration; units in g C/m²/yr or kcal/m²/yr

Comparing productivity across biomes using data tables

sections.title: Primary and Secondary Productivity Calculations
traps: Using GPP instead of NPP for available energy — consumers can only use NPP (what's left after plant respiration); AP math FRQ always requires NPP as the starting value

terms.def: high endemism + high threat

objectives: Adaptive radiation and why island/isolated environments accelerate it
Extinction vs. speciation rate determining net biodiversity

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: allopatric vs. sympatric

title: Island Biogeography — A Model for Habitat Patches

terms.def: larger islands have lower extinction rates
closer islands have higher immigration rates

title: Threats to Biodiversity — HIPPO
subtitle: The Living World: Biodiversity
overview: The Living World: Biodiversity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

Overexploitation, pollution, climate change as additional drivers

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: competitive, predatory, and disease mechanisms

title: Keystone Species and Trophic Cascades
subtitle: The Living World: Biodiversity
overview: The Living World: Biodiversity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Sea otter / sea urchin / kelp as the canonical AP case study

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: disproportionate impact relative to biomass
top predator removal increases herbivore, decreases vegetation

traps: Confusing keystone with apex predator — a keystone species has outsized community impact but isn't necessarily the top predator; starfish and sea otters are classic AP keystone examples

title: Conservation Strategies — Protected Areas and Corridors
subtitle: The Living World: Biodiversity
overview: The Living World: Biodiversity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Habitat corridors allowing gene flow between fragmented populations
Minimum viable population and extinction vortex

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: one large vs. several small reserves

traps: Assuming larger reserves are always better — AP tests nuances: multiple small reserves may cover more habitat types; edge effects reduce effective interior area of large reserves

title: Invasive Species — Mechanisms and Case Studies
subtitle: The Living World: Biodiversity
overview: The Living World: Biodiversity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Economic and ecological costs of invasive species

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: enemy release, novel weapons, phenotypic plasticity
zebra mussels, kudzu, cane toads, Asian carp

traps: Saying invasives succeed 'because they have no predators' — that's enemy release hypothesis, one explanation; AP may ask for multiple mechanisms or ask you to evaluate evidence

title: Endangered Species and International Agreements
subtitle: The Living World: Biodiversity
overview: The Living World: Biodiversity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Captive breeding and reintroduction programs — success factors

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: criteria for critically endangered vs. vulnerable
trade restrictions for threatened species

traps: Confusing CITES (trade) with ESA (domestic US protection) — AP tests which treaty applies to international vs. domestic species protection scenarios

title: Population Dynamics — Growth Models
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Per capita growth rate changes with density under logistic model

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: unlimited resources, r = biotic potential
K as carrying capacity, growth slows near K

traps: Using exponential model when logistic applies — AP gives data showing slowing growth and asks which model fits; must recognize S-curve features in data, not just graphs

title: Population Density and Distribution Patterns
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Clumped, uniform, and random distribution — causes of each
Density-dependent vs. density-independent limiting factors

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: mark-recapture, transects, quadrats

traps: Confusing density-dependent (disease, competition, predation — intensity increases with density) with density-independent (weather, natural disasters — occur regardless of density)

title: Age Structure Diagrams — Predicting the Future
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: How current age structure predicts future growth momentum

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: growing, stable, declining populations
proportion of working-age to non-working-age population

traps: Reading age pyramids as snapshots not predictors — a country with many young people will CONTINUE growing even if fertility drops to replacement level immediately (population momentum)

title: Human Population Growth — Demographic Transition
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Total fertility rate (TFR) vs. replacement fertility (2.1)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: high birth+death → falling death → falling birth → stable
education, urbanization, women's rights

traps: Applying demographic transition uniformly to all countries — different countries are in different stages; AP gives TFR and death rate data and asks which stage and what policy would be effective

title: Survivorship Curves — Who Dies When
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Type I (late loss — humans, elephants), Type II (constant — birds), Type III (early loss — fish, plants)
Connecting curve type to life history strategy (r vs. K selection)
Survivorship data interpretation from tables

sections.title: Survivorship Curves — Who Dies When
traps: Memorizing examples without understanding mechanism — AP asks WHY fish are Type III (massive egg production, minimal parental care, most die young) not just that they are Type III

title: Resource Consumption and Ecological Footprint
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Per capita resource consumption differences between developed and developing nations

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: land area required to support a lifestyle
Impact = Population × Affluence × Technology

traps: Blaming only population size for environmental impact — AP tests IPAT; a small wealthy population can have more impact than a large poor population due to affluence factor

title: Sustainable Yield and Fisheries Management
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: ITQs and catch limits as management tools

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: harvesting at K/2 for fastest regrowth
individual incentive vs. collective optimum

traps: Thinking MSY means harvest as much as possible — MSY is at K/2 where population growth rate is maximum; overfishing past MSY depletes the population

title: Human Population Policies and Ethics
subtitle: Populations
overview: Populations 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Pro-natalist vs. anti-natalist policies — when each is used
Education and access to family planning as most effective interventions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: demographic consequences (sex ratio, aging)

traps: Evaluating policies only on effectiveness without ethical dimensions — AP FRQ often asks for both effectiveness AND tradeoffs/consequences; China's policy reduced growth but created aging crisis

title: Plate Tectonics and Earth's Interior
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Convection in mantle driving plate movement
Earthquakes and volcanoes concentrated at plate boundaries

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: divergent, convergent, transform — landforms at each

traps: Confusing subduction (oceanic under continental or oceanic under oceanic) with collision (continental-continental) — AP asks which plate boundary creates which feature

title: The Rock Cycle and Soil Formation
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Weathering (physical and chemical) as soil formation mechanism

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: formation and interconversion
O, A, B, C layers and what each contains

traps: Describing soil only by texture, not horizon — AP FRQ asks about which horizon is most fertile (A horizon) and why (accumulated organic matter from decomposition)

title: The Atmosphere — Structure and Composition
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Troposphere contains weather; stratosphere contains ozone layer

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: properties of each
CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, H₂O vapor — relative forcing

traps: Treating ozone depletion and greenhouse effect as the same problem — ozone depletion is in the stratosphere from CFCs; greenhouse effect is in the troposphere from CO₂/CH₄; they're distinct

title: Solar Radiation, Albedo, and Earth's Energy Budget
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Latitude effects on solar angle and energy intensity

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fraction of solar radiation reflected; ice-albedo feedback
shortwave in, longwave out, greenhouse retention

traps: Confusing albedo with emissivity — albedo is about incoming shortwave; greenhouse effect involves outgoing longwave; ice-albedo feedback links melting ice to more warming

title: Global Wind Patterns and Ocean Currents
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Coriolis effect deflecting winds and ocean currents

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: rising/falling air creating wind belts
density-driven global ocean conveyor

traps: Not connecting wind patterns to precipitation — air rises at equator (wet) and descends at 30° (desert belt); AP gives a location's latitude and asks about likely climate

title: El Niño/La Niña and Climate Variability
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: ENSO impacts on global precipitation patterns

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: weakened trade winds, warm water moves east, drought in Australia/Indonesia
strengthened trade winds, opposite effects of El Niño

traps: Confusing which region experiences drought vs. flooding — El Niño brings drought to western Pacific (Australia) and flooding to South America's west coast; AP tests specific regional effects

title: Water Systems — Hydrological Cycle and Freshwater
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Water Systems — Hydrological Cycle and Freshwater for the Earth Systems and Resources unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration
confined vs. unconfined; groundwater depletion
all water draining to a single outlet

traps: Ignoring groundwater when discussing freshwater — aquifers hold 30x more freshwater than all surface water; AP tests Ogallala Aquifer depletion as a case study

title: Natural Disasters — Frequency, Magnitude, Prediction
subtitle: Earth Systems and Resources
overview: Earth Systems and Resources 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Natural Disasters — Frequency, Magnitude, Prediction for the Earth Systems and Resources unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Richter scale logarithmic nature, P and S waves
viscosity and silica content predicting explosiveness
formation conditions (warm water, moisture, low wind shear)

title: Agriculture — Green Revolution and Its Consequences
subtitle: Land and Water Use

Subsistence vs. industrial agriculture tradeoffs

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: food production increase; costs: soil degradation, water use, chemical runoff

title: Soil Degradation — Erosion, Salinization, Desertification
subtitle: Land and Water Use
overview: Land and Water Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Soil Degradation — Erosion, Salinization, Desertification for the Land and Water Use unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: rates accelerated by tillage and removal of cover

terms.term: Salinization from irrigation in arid regions
terms.def: salt accumulation
land degradation at dry-land margins from overuse

traps: Confusing salinization (salt buildup from irrigation) with acidification (pH drop from industrial pollution or acid rain) — they have different causes and remediation strategies

title: Sustainable Agriculture — Conservation Practices
subtitle: Land and Water Use
overview: Land and Water Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Sustainable Agriculture — Conservation Practices for the Land and Water Use unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: physical erosion control
biological and chemical soil conservation
minimizing pesticide use

title: Forestry — Logging Methods and Their Impacts
subtitle: Land and Water Use
overview: Land and Water Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Forestry — Logging Methods and Their Impacts for the Land and Water Use unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: extent of disturbance and recovery
biodiversity and carbon storage differences
agriculture, logging, urbanization

title: Mining — Extraction Methods and Remediation
subtitle: Land and Water Use

title: Fisheries and Aquaculture
subtitle: Land and Water Use
overview: Land and Water Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Fisheries and Aquaculture for the Land and Water Use unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: declining catch per unit effort, smaller fish
non-target species in commercial fishing nets
disease, escaped species, nutrient pollution

title: Urban Land Use and Sprawl
subtitle: Land and Water Use
overview: Land and Water Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

diversion leading to ecosystem collapse

title: Fossil Fuels — Formation, Extraction, Environmental Costs
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption

objectives: EROI (Energy Return on Energy Investment) declining for fossil fuels

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: relative carbon content and emissions per unit energy
surface mining, fracking, deep-sea drilling — environmental risks of each

title: Nuclear Energy — Fission, Waste, and Risk
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption
overview: Energy Resources and Consumption 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: U-235 splits releasing neutrons and energy
half-life and long-term storage challenges
what went wrong and why containment matters

traps: Treating nuclear as either zero-risk or too dangerous without nuance — AP FRQ asks for specific advantages (no CO₂ emissions, high energy density) AND disadvantages (waste storage, accident risk)

objectives: Intermittency problem and storage solutions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: semiconductor converting photons to electrons
orientation, thermal mass, glazing

traps: Ignoring lifecycle environmental costs of solar — manufacturing solar panels requires mining rare earth elements and produces toxic waste; AP tests full lifecycle analysis

title: Wind, Hydro, and Geothermal Energy
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption
overview: Energy Resources and Consumption 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Wind, Hydro, and Geothermal Energy for the Energy Resources and Consumption unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: capacity factor (~30%), bird/bat mortality, visual impact
reliable but habitat disruption, altered sediment flow
limited to tectonically active regions, H₂S emissions

traps: Treating all renewables as equally applicable everywhere — hydroelectric requires significant elevation drop and water flow; geothermal requires volcanic activity; AP tests location-specific feasibility

title: Biofuels and Biomass Energy
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: EROI for corn ethanol is near 1
food vs. fuel vs. forest

traps: Assuming biofuels are carbon-neutral — only if regrowth absorbs all CO₂ emitted; corn ethanol lifecycle often produces more GHG than gasoline when land use change is included

title: Energy Conservation and Efficiency
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: using waste heat to increase overall efficiency
insulation, HVAC, lighting efficiency improvements

traps: Confusing efficiency with conservation — efficiency means getting more output per unit energy input; conservation means using less total energy; AP asks for both strategies

subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption

Electricity grid vs. transportation sector energy sources
Energy security and geopolitical implications of fossil fuel dependence

sections.title: The Energy Mix — Global and US Patterns

title: Energy Policy — Economics, Subsidies, and Incentives
subtitle: Energy Resources and Consumption
overview: Energy Resources and Consumption 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Fossil fuel subsidies vs. renewable energy incentives
Cost-benefit analysis of energy transition

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: mechanisms and tradeoffs

title: Air Pollutants — Primary and Secondary
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: EPA six criteria pollutants and their health effects

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: emitted directly (SO₂, NOx, CO, particulates, VOCs)
formed in atmosphere (ozone, PAN, H₂SO₄, HNO₃)

traps: Confusing ground-level ozone (bad, tropospheric pollutant) with stratospheric ozone (good, UV shield) — AP explicitly tests this distinction; the same molecule has opposite effects at different altitudes

title: Photochemical Smog Formation
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: NOx + VOCs + sunlight → ozone + PAN (photochemical smog)
Temperature inversion trapping pollutants near surface

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: cars + sunlight + topography creating smog

traps: Confusing photochemical smog (ozone-based, sunny cities) with industrial/London smog (sulfurous, foggy, cold) — different chemistry, different conditions, different health effects

title: Acid Deposition — Chemistry and Ecological Damage
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ → H₂SO₄; NOx + H₂O → HNO₃

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: aluminum mobilization at pH < 5
acid rain affecting regions far from sources

traps: Treating acid rain as only a local problem — emissions in Ohio create acid rain in New England due to prevailing westerly winds; AP tests transboundary pollution and international policy

title: Stratospheric Ozone Depletion
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Montreal Protocol as policy success story

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂; ClO + O → Cl + O₂ (Cl regenerated)
polar stratospheric clouds concentrating Cl

traps: Saying CFCs 'destroy' ozone as a one-time reaction — each Cl atom catalytically destroys ~100,000 ozone molecules before being removed; the catalytic cycle is the critical AP concept

title: Indoor Air Pollution
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: VOCs from building materials and cleaning products
Developing world indoor air pollution from biomass combustion

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: natural radioactive gas from uranium decay, lung cancer risk

traps: Overlooking indoor air quality as an AP topic — AP specifically tests radon (enter through foundation cracks, accumulates in basements) and its mechanism of harm (alpha particle emission in lungs)

title: The Clean Air Act and Pollution Reduction
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: NAAQS standards for six criteria pollutants
Best available control technology (BACT) requirements
Cap-and-trade for SO₂ under 1990 CAA Amendments

sections.title: The Clean Air Act and Pollution Reduction
traps: Treating regulation as binary (yes/no) — AP tests HOW regulations work; cap-and-trade sets total emissions cap, issues permits, allows trading so cheapest reductions happen first

title: Noise and Light Pollution
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Noise and Light Pollution for the Atmospheric Pollution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: disrupted communication, navigation, reproduction
disrupted circadian rhythms, sea turtle disorientation
shielding lights, reducing unnecessary illumination

traps: Treating noise/light pollution as trivial AP topics — they appear in FRQ expecting mechanistic explanations; sea turtles navigate by moon over ocean, artificial lights cause disorientation

title: Climate Change and Atmospheric Pollution Linkages
subtitle: Atmospheric Pollution
overview: Atmospheric Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Black carbon (soot) both absorbs radiation AND causes health problems
Ozone as both pollutant (troposphere) and greenhouse gas

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: improving air quality AND reducing warming

traps: Separating air pollution from climate policy — methane reduction prevents climate change AND reduces ground-level ozone; AP tests these co-benefits

title: Water Pollution — Point vs. Nonpoint Sources
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Water Pollution — Point vs. Nonpoint Sources for the Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: specific location (pipe, drain) — easier to regulate
diffuse (agricultural runoff, urban stormwater) — harder to control
discharge permits for point sources

traps: Applying point source regulations to nonpoint problems — a farmer's field has no single discharge point; AP tests why nonpoint source pollution is harder to regulate and what strategies address it

title: Eutrophication — Nutrient Pollution Mechanisms
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Nitrogen and phosphorus runoff → algal bloom → decomposition → oxygen depletion

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Gulf of Mexico as primary AP case study
adding phosphorus to freshwater triggers growth

traps: Confusing which nutrient limits which system — phosphorus usually limits freshwater systems; nitrogen usually limits marine/coastal systems; AP asks about the specific system in the scenario

title: Toxic Pollutants and Biomagnification
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Bioaccumulation in individual organisms vs. biomagnification across food web

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: concentration increases at higher trophic levels
fat-soluble or non-metabolizable, concentrate in fatty tissue

traps: Confusing bioaccumulation (within one organism over time) with biomagnification (increasing concentration across trophic levels) — AP explicitly distinguishes these two processes

title: Solid Waste — Types, Disposal, Reduction
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Solid Waste — Types, Disposal, Reduction for the Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: food (most by weight), paper, plastics
liner, leachate collection, methane capture
reduce, reuse, recycle, recover, dispose

traps: Treating recycling as the top priority — the waste hierarchy puts REDUCTION first; AP FRQ asks to rank strategies and explain why source reduction is more effective than recycling

title: Hazardous Waste — Classification and Superfund
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Hazardous Waste — Classification and Superfund for the Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, toxicity
polluter-pays principle, National Priorities List
contaminated industrial sites and redevelopment challenges

traps: Assuming all industrial waste is regulated the same — RCRA governs current hazardous waste; CERCLA (Superfund) addresses historical abandoned sites; AP tests which law applies to which scenario

title: Oil Spills — Impacts and Remediation
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Oil Spills — Impacts and Remediation for the Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: coating seabirds, smothering benthic organisms
PAH compounds affecting fish reproduction
hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria as cleanup tool

traps: Focusing only on visible oil effects — long-term chronic effects from PAH compounds and dispersant toxicity persist for decades; AP tests both acute and long-term impacts of spills

title: Soil Contamination and Remediation
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: In-situ vs. ex-situ remediation tradeoffs

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: lead, arsenic, cadmium from mining/industry
plants (hyperaccumulators) extracting metals from soil

traps: Describing phytoremediation without mechanism — plants must be harvested AND disposed of properly to actually remove metals from the site; if left to decompose, metals return to soil

title: Environmental Justice — Pollution Burden Distribution
subtitle: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution
overview: Aquatic and Terrestrial Pollution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Disproportionate pollution exposure in low-income and minority communities
Locally unwanted land uses (LULUs) and siting decisions
EJ movement and EPA environmental justice policies

sections.title: Environmental Justice — Pollution Burden Distribution
traps: Treating environmental justice as separate from environmental science — AP FRQ integrates EJ with pollution topics; must connect which communities bear the greatest burden from specific pollutants

title: The Greenhouse Effect and Climate Science
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, H₂O as greenhouse gases — relative warming potential

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: shortwave in, longwave absorbed by GHGs, re-radiated toward Earth
ice cores, temperature records, sea level rise, Arctic sea ice

traps: Explaining climate change vaguely — AP FRQ requires molecular mechanism: greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation because their bonds vibrate at IR frequencies

title: Climate Feedbacks — Amplifying and Dampening
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Climate Feedbacks — Amplifying and Dampening for the Global Change unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ice-albedo, water vapor amplification, permafrost methane
blackbody radiation, cloud albedo effects
threshold beyond which feedbacks become self-sustaining

traps: Calling all climate feedbacks positive (amplifying) — negative feedbacks also exist; AP tests that more outgoing radiation as temperature rises is a stabilizing (negative) feedback

title: Climate Change Impacts — Ecological and Human
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Climate Change Impacts — Ecological and Human for the Global Change unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: earlier spring events disrupting predator-prey timing
thermal expansion + ice melt; coastal flooding
thermal stress expelling zooxanthellae

traps: Listing impacts without connecting to mechanism — coral bleaching: warmer water stresses zooxanthellae (symbiotic algae), coral expels them (bleaches), loses food source and may die if prolonged

title: Ocean Acidification
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: pH drop dissolving calcium carbonate shells of marine organisms
Pteropods, oysters, corals as most vulnerable organisms

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: chemistry of acidification

traps: Confusing ocean acidification with general ocean pollution — caused specifically by dissolved CO₂ from atmosphere; pH has dropped from 8.2 to 8.1 (30% more acidic); AP tests the chemistry

title: Mitigation Strategies — Reducing Emissions
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Renewable energy transition, electrification of transportation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: geological sequestration
reforestation, soil carbon, methane capture from landfills

traps: Treating mitigation as only energy-sector solutions — AP tests agriculture (methane, N₂O from fertilizer), land use change, and waste sector contributions to total GHG inventory

title: Adaptation Strategies — Living With Climate Change
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Sea walls, managed retreat, living shorelines for coastal flooding
Heat-resilient crops and shifting agricultural zones
Early warning systems and disaster preparedness

sections.title: Adaptation Strategies — Living With Climate Change
traps: Confusing mitigation (preventing emissions) with adaptation (adjusting to changes) — AP FRQ distinguishes and asks which strategy addresses a specific scenario

title: International Climate Policy — UNFCCC, Paris Agreement
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Carbon markets and international emissions trading

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: NDCs, 1.5°C and 2°C targets, review mechanism
developed vs. developing nations

traps: Treating the Paris Agreement as legally binding — it's a voluntary pledge system (NDCs); lack of enforcement mechanism is a key weakness; AP asks about both structure and limitations

title: Ozone Recovery and Environmental Policy Lessons
subtitle: Global Change
overview: Global Change 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Using Montreal Protocol as model for climate policy discussions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: phaseout of CFCs leading to measurable ozone recovery
HCFCs → HFCs (some still potent GHGs)

traps: Treating ozone recovery as complete — the ozone hole still forms annually but is smaller than peak; full recovery projected for 2060s; AP tests that HFC replacements became a new climate problem

title: Coulomb's Law and Superposition — Vector Calculus
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Electric force as vector; superposition principle
Force on charge from continuous distribution by integration
Electric field E = F/q₀ as a vector field

sections.title: Coulomb's Law and Superposition — Vector Calculus
traps: Adding force magnitudes without considering direction — must resolve into components and add; AP C gives charge distributions and expects component integration

title: Electric Field from Continuous Charge Distributions
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Linear (λ), surface (σ), volume (ρ) charge densities
Field of infinite line charge, ring, disk by integration

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: building field from infinitesimal elements

traps: Not exploiting symmetry to simplify integrations — for a ring of charge, perpendicular components cancel; only axial component survives; setting up dE correctly then identifying cancellations is key

title: Gauss's Law — Derivation and Applications
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Applying to spherical, cylindrical, planar symmetry
Field inside and outside conductor; field between plates

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Gauss's law and its derivation

traps: Choosing non-symmetric Gaussian surfaces — Gauss's law always holds, but only simplifies when E is uniform and perpendicular on the surface; AP C tests whether you choose the right surface shape

title: Electric Potential from Field — Integration
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: V = -∫E·dr from reference point (usually infinity)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: V = k∫dq/r (scalar, easier than field)
finding field from potential gradient

traps: Integrating E to get V in the wrong direction — must go from the field point to infinity (or chosen reference), not along field lines; AP C gives a charge distribution and expects both E and V derivations

title: Conductors in Electrostatic Equilibrium
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: E = 0 inside conductor; charges on outer surface only
Induced charges on conductor in external field
Charge distribution on non-spherical conductors — surface charge density proportional to curvature

sections.title: Conductors in Electrostatic Equilibrium
traps: Not accounting for induced charges on nearby conductors — when a charge is brought near a grounded conductor, induced surface charges redistribute; AP C FRQ often includes this induced-charge scenario

title: Capacitance and Energy Storage
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: C = Q/V; C = ε₀A/d; C = 4πε₀R for isolated sphere
Energy U = ½CV² = Q²/2C; energy density u = ½ε₀E²
Capacitors in series and parallel; dielectric effects

sections.title: Capacitance and Energy Storage
traps: Forgetting to recalculate V or Q when connecting capacitors — AP C gives charged and uncharged capacitors connected; must conserve total charge, then find new V across the combined capacitance

title: Dielectrics and Polarization
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Bound surface charges from polarization

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: C_new = κC₀; E reduced to E₀/κ inside
why κ > 1

traps: Confusing the effect of dielectric when battery-connected vs. disconnected — with battery (V constant): C increases, Q increases, U increases; without battery (Q constant): V decreases, C increases, U decreases

title: Electrostatic Boundary Conditions and Uniqueness Theorem
subtitle: Electrostatics
overview: Electrostatics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Electrostatic Boundary Conditions and Uniqueness Theorem for the Electrostatics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: tangential component continuous, normal component has discontinuity
solution determined by boundary conditions alone

title: Two-Way Tables and Association in Categorical Data
subtitle: Exploring Two-Variable Data
overview: Exploring Two-Variable Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Marginal, joint, and conditional distributions from two-way tables

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: conditional distributions differ across categories
direction of association reverses when data is combined

traps: Using marginal frequencies instead of conditional frequencies to assess association — must compare conditional distributions (row or column percentages); AP gives a two-way table and asks whether variables are associated

title: Causation, Correlation, and Confounding
subtitle: Exploring Two-Variable Data
overview: Exploring Two-Variable Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why randomized experiments can establish causation but observational studies can't

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: causation, common cause, coincidence
associated with both X and Y

traps: Describing a confounding variable as one that 'affects the outcome' — it must also be associated with the explanatory variable; AP FRQ asks to 'identify and explain' a potential confounding variable, requiring both parts

title: Sampling Methods — Which to Use and Why
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Sampling Methods — Which to Use and Why for the Collecting Data unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: every individual equally likely to be chosen
divide into strata, SRS within each
divide into groups, randomly select entire groups; systematic sampling

traps: Confusing stratified with cluster sampling — stratified takes a few from EACH group; cluster sampling takes ALL from SOME groups; AP gives a sampling description and asks to identify the method

title: Sampling Bias and Its Sources
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Wording effects in survey questions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: mechanisms of each
self-selected samples overrepresent extreme opinions

traps: Calling any sampling error 'bias' — bias is SYSTEMATIC error in one direction; random sampling error is expected and decreases with sample size; AP tests whether a described error is bias or random variation

title: Experimental Design — The Three Principles
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Control group vs. placebo group (not the same)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: why each is necessary
single-blind and double-blind designs

traps: Confusing control group with placebo group — control group receives no treatment; placebo group receives an inert treatment; both are controls, but AP distinguishes why placebos are used (to account for psychological effects)

title: Blocking in Experiments
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why blocking reduces variability and increases sensitivity to treatment effects

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: grouping similar experimental units before randomization
simplest block design (pairing individuals or before/after)

traps: Describing blocking as 'randomly dividing into groups' — blocking is NOT random; you group similar units first, then randomize within blocks; AP asks to identify what constitutes an appropriate blocking variable

title: Causation in Experiments
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Random assignment allows causal conclusions (unlike random sampling)
Four conditions for establishing causation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: random sample allows generalization; random assignment allows causation

traps: Claiming random sampling establishes causation — random SAMPLING allows generalization to the population; random ASSIGNMENT allows causal conclusions; AP tests this two-condition distinction for scope of inference

title: Ethics in Data Collection
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Informed consent, anonymity vs. confidentiality, IRB oversight
Ethical issues in observational vs. experimental research
Data privacy and protection

sections.title: Ethics in Data Collection
traps: Confusing anonymity (researcher doesn't know identity) with confidentiality (researcher knows but won't disclose) — AP occasionally tests these distinctions and why they matter for bias and participant protection

title: Simulation in Statistics
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Designing a simulation to model a probability problem
Assigning digits/outcomes to represent probabilities
Running repetitions and computing empirical probability from results

sections.title: Simulation in Statistics
traps: Assigning multiple digits to the same outcome without justifying the proportion — if P(success) = 0.3, must assign exactly 30 of 100 equally-likely outcomes; AP FRQ asks to describe simulation design clearly and precisely

title: Survey Design and Question Wording
subtitle: Collecting Data
overview: Collecting Data 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Loaded questions, leading questions, and double-barreled questions
Order effects in survey items
Pilot testing and question validation

sections.title: Survey Design and Question Wording
traps: Not identifying the specific type of bias in a survey question — AP asks to identify AND explain the source; saying 'it's biased' without naming the mechanism (e.g., response bias from question wording) loses points

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Probability Rules — Addition and Multiplication
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B); simplifies if mutually exclusive
P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B|A); simplifies if independent

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: P(Aᶜ) = 1 - P(A)

traps: Applying the simplified multiplication rule P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B) without checking independence — must first verify independence; AP gives probabilities and tests whether events are independent before using the product rule

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Conditional Probability and Independence
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Testing independence from a two-way table

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: conditional probability formula
P(A|B) = P(A); knowing B doesn't change probability of A

traps: Confusing mutually exclusive with independent — mutually exclusive events (P(A and B)=0) are NOT independent (unless P(A)=0); if two events can't occur together, knowing one occurred tells you something about the other

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Discrete Random Variables — Expected Value and Variance
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Var(X) = Σ[(x-μ)²·P(X=x)]; SD(X) = √Var(X)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: probability-weighted average
E(aX+b) = aE(X)+b; Var(aX+b) = a²Var(X)

traps: Adding standard deviations instead of variances — Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) for independent X, Y; SD(X+Y) ≠ SD(X) + SD(Y); must add variances first, then take square root

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Binomial Distribution
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: P(X=k) = C(n,k)pᵏ(1-p)^(n-k)
μ = np; σ = √(np(1-p)); normal approximation when np≥10 and n(1-p)≥10

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: BINS (Binary, Independent, fixed N, same p)

traps: Using binomial when independence assumption is violated — sampling without replacement from small populations violates independence; must check whether n is less than 10% of population for independence to hold approximately

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Geometric Distribution
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: E(X) = 1/p; Var(X) = (1-p)/p²

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: number of trials until first success
geometric has no fixed n

traps: Confusing binomial (count of successes in fixed n trials) with geometric (number of trials until first success) — AP gives a scenario and tests which distribution applies; the presence or absence of a fixed number of trials is the key distinction

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Continuous Probability Distributions
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: P(X=a) = 0 for continuous distributions; only intervals have nonzero probability

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: f(x) = 1/(b-a) on [a,b]
F(x) = P(X≤x) = cumulative area

traps: Computing P(X=2.5) as nonzero for a continuous distribution — for continuous distributions, single values have probability zero; must compute P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = area; AP gives an interval and expects area calculation

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Normal Distribution Calculations
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Standardizing to Z and using z-table or calculator normalcdf
Finding values from percentiles using invNorm

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: X+Y still normal if X, Y normal

traps: Not recognizing that a sum of normal random variables is also normal — AP gives the means and variances of two normal RVs and asks for probabilities about their sum; must compute new mean = μ₁+μ₂ and variance = σ₁²+σ₂² first

unitName: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
title: Law of Large Numbers and Simulation
subtitle: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
overview: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Using simulation to estimate probabilities empirically

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: sample proportion approaches true probability as n grows
past outcomes don't change future probabilities in independent trials

traps: Confusing LLN (proportion converges) with the gambler's fallacy (each trial has changed probability to 'balance out') — individual trials are independent; LLN is about long-run averages, not any specific next outcome

title: Sampling Distribution of p̂
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: p̂ is the sample proportion; its sampling distribution is approximately normal for large n

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: μ_p̂ = p; spread: σ_p̂ = √(p(1-p)/n)
np ≥ 10 and n(1-p) ≥ 10 for normality

traps: Using the formula σ_p̂ = √(p̂(1-p̂)/n) with the observed p̂ instead of the true p — when the true p is known (null hypothesis), use p; only substitute p̂ when p is unknown (confidence intervals)

title: Sampling Distribution of x̄
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: μ_x̄ = μ; σ_x̄ = σ/√n (standard error)
Population must be normal OR n large for x̄ to be normal

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: x̄ is approximately normal for n ≥ 30 regardless of population shape

traps: Applying CLT to small samples from skewed populations — CLT requires n ≥ 30 (approximately) for non-normal populations; if n=10 and population is skewed, x̄ is NOT approximately normal

title: Central Limit Theorem — The Key Insight
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: CLT applies to means, not individual observations
Population distribution vs. sampling distribution of x̄

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: averaging many random values concentrates the distribution

traps: Applying CLT to individual observations — CLT describes the distribution of SAMPLE MEANS, not individual data values; P(X > 5) for one randomly chosen value uses the original distribution, not the normal approximation

title: Sampling Distributions for Differences
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Independence assumption required between samples

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: center = p₁-p₂; variance = p₁(1-p₁)/n₁ + p₂(1-p₂)/n₂
center = μ₁-μ₂; variance = σ₁²/n₁ + σ₂²/n₂

traps: Adding standard errors instead of variances when combining two sampling distributions — must add VARIANCES and then take the square root; SE(x̄₁ - x̄₂) = √(σ₁²/n₁ + σ₂²/n₂)

title: Bias and Variability of Estimators
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Bias-variance tradeoff in statistical estimation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: E(estimator) = parameter
smaller standard error = more precise estimator

traps: Confusing bias (systematic error) with variability (precision) — an estimator can be unbiased but imprecise (high variance) or precise but biased; AP asks to describe an estimator in terms of BOTH properties

title: Effect of Sample Size on Sampling Distributions
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Doubling n reduces SE by factor of √2, not 2
Sampling distribution narrowing as n increases visualized

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: smaller standard error (SE = σ/√n)

traps: Saying 'larger sample gives smaller standard deviation' — larger sample reduces the STANDARD ERROR (of the mean), not the population standard deviation or individual observation variability; AP tests this language precision

title: t-Distribution vs. z-Distribution
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: t-distribution approaches z as degrees of freedom → ∞

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: heavier tails, used when σ unknown; degrees of freedom = n-1
t* > z* for same confidence level (heavier tails require wider interval)

traps: Using z* instead of t* when σ is unknown — whenever population standard deviation is unknown (almost always in practice), must use t*; AP tests when each distribution is appropriate

title: Conditions for Inference — The Three Checks
subtitle: Sampling Distributions
overview: Sampling Distributions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Conditions for Inference — The Three Checks for the Sampling Distributions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: data from random sample or randomized experiment
n≥30 or normal population or no strong skew
population ≥ 10n (10% condition)

traps: Skipping condition checks and going straight to calculations — AP FRQ requires explicitly stating, checking, and verifying all three conditions; missing any condition check typically costs 1 point on the scoring rubric

title: Confidence Intervals for One Proportion
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: CI: p̂ ± z*(√(p̂(1-p̂)/n)); using p̂ (not p) in SE for CI
Margin of error, confidence level, sample size relationships

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 'We are 95% confident the true proportion is in...'

traps: Saying 'there is a 95% probability the true proportion is in this interval' — the true proportion is FIXED (not random); the interval either contains it or not; correct language is 'we are 95% confident'

title: Significance Tests for One Proportion
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: H₀: p = p₀ vs. Hₐ: p ≠ p₀ (two-sided) or one-sided

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: z = (p̂ - p₀)/√(p₀(1-p₀)/n); using p₀ in SE for tests
probability of getting this result or more extreme IF H₀ true

traps: Using p̂ in the standard error for hypothesis tests — for hypothesis tests, use p₀ (null hypothesis value) in the SE formula; p̂ is used only for confidence intervals; this distinction appears on almost every AP stats FRQ

title: Two-Sample Proportion Tests and Intervals
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Large sample conditions for each sample must be checked separately

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: use pooled proportion p_c in SE
use separate p̂₁ and p̂₂ in SE (no pooling)

traps: Using pooled proportion for confidence intervals — pooling only happens in hypothesis tests when H₀: p₁=p₂; for CIs (no assumption of equal proportions), use unpooled standard error with p̂₁ and p̂₂ separately

title: Type I and Type II Errors and Power
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Power = 1 - β; increases with larger n, larger effect size, larger α

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: rejecting true H₀; probability = α (significance level)
failing to reject false H₀; probability = β

traps: Confusing Type I and II error in context — AP gives a specific scenario and asks which type of error is described; Type I = falsely concluding there's an effect; Type II = missing a real effect

title: P-value Interpretation — The Most Tested Concept
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Small p-value = evidence against H₀; NOT probability H₀ is true
Significance level α as the threshold for rejection

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: probability of observed statistic OR MORE EXTREME, given H₀ is true

traps: Saying 'the p-value is the probability H₀ is true' — this is false; p-value is P(data at least this extreme | H₀ is true); AP FRQ requires the conditional statement structure in the interpretation

title: Confidence Interval as a Range of Plausible Values
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: CI informs us about plausible parameter values, not just significance

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.term: Confidence level as long-run capture rate
terms.def: 95% of CIs contain the true value

terms.term: Connection between CI and two-sided test
terms.def: parameter outside CI ↔ reject H₀

traps: Interpreting confidence level as probability for ONE interval — once an interval is computed, the true parameter either is or isn't in it; the 95% refers to the METHOD over many samples, not this specific interval

title: Conditions for Proportion Inference
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Conditions for Proportion Inference for the Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: random sample
np₀ ≥ 10 and n(1-p₀) ≥ 10 (using p₀ for tests)
n ≤ 10% of population

traps: Using p̂ instead of p₀ in the normal condition check for hypothesis tests — must use the NULL hypothesis value p₀ when checking np₀ ≥ 10; this differs from the CI check which uses p̂

title: Selecting the Right Test — One vs. Two Sample
subtitle: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
overview: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Selecting the Right Test — One vs. Two Sample for the Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: comparing one group to a known standard
comparing two independent groups
two measurements on same subject → one-sample on differences

traps: Using two-sample test for matched pairs data — matched pairs are NOT independent samples; must compute differences first, then apply one-sample t-test to the differences; AP gives the design and tests whether you identify it correctly

title: One-Sample t-Test and t-Interval
subtitle: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
overview: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Using t-table or calculator; df = n-1 for one sample

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: test statistic with degrees of freedom n-1

traps: Using z-procedures when σ is unknown — whenever you use s (sample standard deviation) instead of σ, use t-procedures; almost all real-world problems require t

title: Two-Sample t-Procedures
subtitle: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
overview: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Checking conditions separately for each sample

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: df calculated by calculator (Welch) or conservative df = min(n₁,n₂)-1
(x̄₁ - x̄₂) ± t*(SE)

traps: Using the pooled t-test instead of Welch's for two-sample tests — AP Statistics uses Welch's two-sample t (not pooled) by default; pooled is only valid if variances are known to be equal (rarely appropriate)

title: Matched Pairs t-Procedures
subtitle: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means

title: Chi-Square Test of Independence

title: Chi-Square Test for Homogeneity

title: Expected Counts and the Chi-Square Distribution

terms.def: alliance-based colonialism dependent on indigenous knowledge and labor
French integrated with indigenous peoples rather than replacing them

traps: Treating all European colonialism as identical — AP tests DIFFERENCES in colonial models: French depended on indigenous intermediaries and intermarried (métis); Spanish imposed replacement colonialism; British plantation model imported African labor; these distinctions explain different demographic outcomes and resistance patterns

title: The Enlightenment and Atlantic Revolutions
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: How Enlightenment ideas traveled through print culture to Atlantic world

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: natural rights, social contract, right to revolution
separation of powers as guard against tyranny

traps: Treating the Enlightenment as the single cause of Atlantic revolutions — AP tests MATERIAL causes alongside ideological: American Revolution driven by taxation without representation (economic) + Enlightenment ideas; Haitian Revolution driven by slavery's brutality (material) + French revolutionary ideals; ideas alone rarely cause revolutions

title: American and French Revolutions — Outcomes Compared
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Both inspired by Enlightenment but produced opposite outcomes — why?

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: conservative revolution preserving property rights, creating republican government
radical revolution destroying aristocracy, ending in Napoleon's authoritarianism

traps: Treating these revolutions as equally radical — AP tests that the American Revolution was CONSERVATIVE (preserving British legal traditions, protecting property including enslaved people); the French was radical (abolishing aristocracy, universal male citizenship); this distinction explains why America stabilized quickly and France cycled through regimes

title: Haitian Revolution — The Exception That Tests the Rule
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Only successful slave revolution in history — Toussaint L'Ouverture's leadership
French abolition of slavery (1794) creating the condition for Black soldiers fighting FOR France
Haiti inspiring fear in slaveholder societies worldwide, restricting its diplomatic recognition

sections.title: Haitian Revolution — The Exception That Tests the Rule
traps: Presenting Haiti as simply 'inspired by the French Revolution' — AP tests the IRONY: France's Revolution proclaimed universal rights but maintained slavery; Haiti forced the question of whether those rights applied to enslaved Africans; Napoleon's decision to reinstate slavery triggered the final uprising; causation runs from French contradiction, not French inspiration

title: Latin American Independence — Creole Revolutions
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Creoles (American-born Spaniards) leading revolutions, not indigenous or mestizo populations
Napoleon's invasion of Spain (1808) removing the legitimating authority colonial loyalty depended on

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.term: Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín
terms.def: military campaigns connecting South America

traps: Assuming Latin American revolutions were socially radical like Haiti — AP tests that they were CREOLE revolutions preserving the racial hierarchy; indigenous and African populations rarely benefited; independence transferred power from peninsulares to creoles, not to the majority populations; this explains persistent inequality after independence

title: Industrial Revolution — Britain First, Why?
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Enclosure movement creating mobile landless labor force available for factory work
Patent system protecting inventors; capital markets funding investment

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Britain's natural resources concentrated near navigable water

traps: Listing only coal and geography as causes — AP tests SOCIAL CONDITIONS: the enclosure movement is the hidden cause that created a dispossessed labor force willing to work in factories; without landless workers desperate for wages, machinery without operators changes nothing; demographic and property law changes enabled industrialization as much as resources

title: Social Effects of Industrialization
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Social Effects of Industrialization for the Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Manchester growing from 25,000 to 300,000 in 50 years
factory discipline, child labor, 14-hour days
factory owners, managers, professionals creating new social layer

traps: Focusing only on negative effects — AP tests that industrialization created the MIDDLE CLASS as a genuinely new social group with new values (thrift, hard work, separate spheres for women); responses to industrialization (socialism, labor unions, reform movements) are as important as the conditions they responded to

title: Nationalism — Unification and Fragmentation
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Nationalism — Unification and Fragmentation for the Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Bismarck using 'blood and iron' — wars against Denmark, Austria, France
Cavour's diplomacy + Garibaldi's military campaign
Greek independence, Balkan crises

traps: Treating nationalism as always a unifying force — AP tests that nationalism was SIMULTANEOUSLY fragmenting (breaking apart Ottoman and Habsburg empires) and consolidating (unifying Germany and Italy); which function it performed depended on whether the group was a majority or minority within an existing political unit

title: Abolitionism and the End of the Slave Trade
subtitle: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Revolutions (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Haitian Revolution making slaveholders fear abolition; American South defending slavery as 'positive good'
British navy patrolling Atlantic after 1807 — enforcement gap between law and practice

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: evangelical Christianity + Enlightenment rights rhetoric + economic argument (free labor more productive)

traps: Crediting abolitionism solely to moral progress — AP tests ECONOMIC arguments: British industrialists argued free laborers consumed more goods (creating markets); Caribbean planters were losing competitiveness; moral arguments were effective because they aligned with economic interests of industrial capitalism; purely moral explanations are incomplete for AP

title: New Imperialism — Causes and the Scramble for Africa
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master New Imperialism — Causes and the Scramble for Africa for the Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: need for raw materials, markets for manufactured goods, investment outlets
nationalism and prestige driving competition between European powers
quinine (malaria prevention), steam power, repeating rifles enabling interior conquest

traps: Using 'economic greed' as the sole cause — AP tests the interaction of causes: a country could profit from trade without colonization; the political competition between European powers (fear of being left behind) drove the PACE and COMPREHENSIVENESS of colonization beyond what pure economics required; technology enabled what competition demanded

title: Imperialism in Asia — India and China Compared
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Imperialism in Asia — India and China Compared for the Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: direct colonial rule after 1857 Sepoy Mutiny; railways, English education, legal system
'semicolonial' — unequal treaties, extraterritoriality, treaty ports without formal annexation
resisting colonization through Meiji industrialization — the exception proving the rule

traps: Treating China and India as experiencing identical imperialism — AP tests the distinction: India was COLONIZED (direct rule, British governor-general); China was SEMI-COLONIZED (kept nominal sovereignty but lost economic and legal autonomy); this distinction matters for explaining nationalist responses — Indian Congress vs. Chinese Qing weakness

title: Responses to Imperialism — Accommodation and Resistance
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Responses to Imperialism — Accommodation and Resistance for the Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: selective Westernization as strategy to avoid colonization
educated elite using British legal framework to demand rights
xenophobic popular resistance to foreign presence in China

traps: Categorizing responses as simply 'resistant' or 'collaborative' — AP tests the SPECTRUM: Meiji Japan selectively adopted Western institutions (technology, military) while rejecting Western political control; Indian educated elites used British education against British rule; these sophisticated responses require analyzing what was adopted and what was rejected, and why

title: Economic Imperialism — Export Economies and Dependency
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Economic Imperialism — Export Economies and Dependency for the Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: colonies forced into single cash crops (cotton in Egypt, rubber in Congo)
railroads running from interior to coast, not between cities
Indian textile industry destroyed by cheap British manufactured cloth

traps: Treating colonial economic development as beneficial modernization — AP tests DE-INDUSTRIALIZATION: India had sophisticated textile manufacturing before British rule; British tariffs protecting Lancashire mills while flooding Indian markets destroyed it; the infrastructure argument (railroads benefited India) ignores that it was designed for extraction, not internal development

title: Migration in the Industrial Age
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Indian and Chinese contract labor (indenture) replacing enslaved labor in Caribbean and Pacific

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 50+ million to Americas (1850-1914) fleeing poverty and persecution
rural to urban across industrializing regions

traps: Treating all migration as voluntary — AP tests coercion spectrum: chattel slavery → indenture → contract labor → 'voluntary' migration driven by economic desperation; indentured workers technically consented but were often deceived about conditions; AP asks you to analyze the DEGREE of coercion across different labor migration systems

title: Social Darwinism and Racism as Imperial Ideology
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Herbert Spencer applying evolutionary theory to justify racial hierarchy ('survival of the fittest' society)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Kipling's poem presenting imperialism as civilizing mission
skull measurements, IQ testing used to legitimize subjugation

traps: Treating racist ideology as simply hypocritical cover for economic interests — AP tests that elites GENUINELY believed Social Darwinist claims; ideology shaped policy (separate education, restrictions on intermarriage); the economic and ideological motivations reinforced each other rather than one being real and the other fake

title: Women's Rights Movements in the 19th Century
subtitle: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900)
overview: Consequences of Industrialization (c. 1750–c. 1900) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Industrialization creating middle-class women with time and literacy for activism

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Declaration of Sentiments using Declaration of Independence language — deliberate rhetorical strategy
suffrage movement (political rights) vs. socialist feminism (economic equality)

traps: Treating women's rights as a purely Western phenomenon — AP tests that women organized across colonized world simultaneously; Indian women's organizations, Egyptian feminist union emerged in this period; the suffrage question was complicated by colonial women demanding rights that colonial men denied them, creating tensions within nationalist movements

title: Causes of World War I — MAIN and the Alliance System
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Alliance system converting local conflict into continental war (Austria-Serbia → world war)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Serbian nationalism threatening Austro-Hungarian multi-ethnic empire
competition over colonies creating tensions between European powers

traps: Memorizing MAIN as four equal causes — AP tests the INTERACTION: militarism made war seem winnable; alliances made it spread; imperialism created the rivalries; nationalism provided the trigger (assassination); the alliance system is the MECHANISM that turned a regional crisis into world war; treating them as separate misses the causal chain

title: World War I — Total War and Its Effects
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master World War I — Total War and Its Effects for the Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: military stalemate created by industrial weapons outpacing military tactics
women in factories, rationing, propaganda
Ottoman deportation and massacre of Armenian Christians (1915-1923)

traps: Focusing only on the Western Front — AP tests GLOBAL dimensions: colonial soldiers from India, Africa, Southeast Asia fought for European powers; the war in the Middle East created the modern map through Sykes-Picot Agreement; the Armenian Genocide established the template for 20th century genocides; WWI was genuinely world-spanning

title: The Russian Revolution — Two Revolutions, One Year
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Russian Revolution — Two Revolutions, One Year for the Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: tsarist regime collapsed under war pressure and food shortages
Bolsheviks seizing power promising 'Peace, Land, Bread'
vanguard party, immediate revolution in agrarian society

traps: Treating the Russian Revolution as inevitable — AP tests CONTINGENCY: the February Revolution was spontaneous and Tsar Nicholas could have survived with minimal reform; the Bolsheviks succeeded because they made specific promises (land to peasants, end to war) that the Provisional Government refused to make; outcomes depended on decisions, not historical laws

title: Rise of Fascism — Italy and Germany
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Hitler's legal rise to power through elections, then consolidation through emergency laws

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: hyperinflation (Germany), unemployment, perceived national humiliation enabling extremist appeal
ultranationalism, racial hierarchy, anti-Marxist

traps: Treating fascism as pure economic desperation — AP tests that the MIDDLE CLASS was fascism's core support, not the unemployed poor (who voted communist); fear of communist revolution drove middle-class professionals to fascist parties; economic crisis explains the opening but class anxiety explains which option people chose

title: World War II — Global Scope and the Holocaust
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master World War II — Global Scope and the Holocaust for the Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Japan's imperial expansion in Asia preceding European war by years
systematic genocide of 6 million Jews plus Roma, disabled, political opponents
ideologically incompatible powers (US democracy, Soviet communism) unified by common enemy

traps: Treating the Holocaust as separate from the war — AP tests that the Holocaust was ENABLED by wartime conditions: the chaos of occupation, the use of war as cover, the involvement of collaborators across occupied Europe; genocide studies show that most perpetrators were ordinary people following orders in conditions of dehumanization — Hannah Arendt's 'banality of evil'

title: Atomic Bombs and the End of Total War
subtitle: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present)
overview: Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Atomic Bombs and the End of Total War for the Global Conflict (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: unprecedented government-science collaboration driven by fear Germany would get the bomb first
immediate deaths 130,000-226,000; debate over whether invasion alternative would have cost more
mutual assured destruction preventing direct great-power conflict
