traps: Treating the atomic bomb decision as obviously right or wrong — AP tests HISTORICAL CONTEXT: in August 1945, Japan had not offered unconditional surrender; Battle of Okinawa suggested invasion would cost 250,000+ American casualties; Truman decided with this information, not hindsight; AP wants analysis of decision-making context, not moral verdict

title: The Cold War — Origins and Ideology
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Cold War — Origins and Ideology for the Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: capitalism/democracy vs. communism/one-party state
Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO as US strategy
security buffer, spreading communist revolution as defensive

traps: Presenting the Cold War as entirely American vs. Soviet — AP tests that BOTH sides had legitimate security concerns: Soviets lost 27 million in WWII and wanted buffer states; Americans feared communist expansion; treating one side as entirely aggressive misses the security dilemma dynamic that AP rewards in SAQ and LEQ responses

title: Decolonization — Africa and Asia
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Decolonization — Africa and Asia for the Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: partition creating India and Pakistan along religious lines, causing 1 million deaths
mostly peaceful transfer but with notable violent exceptions (Algeria, Kenya)
violence as psychologically necessary for colonial liberation

traps: Treating decolonization as a gift from European powers — AP tests that it was FORCED by independence movements, post-WWII weakness of European states, and Cold War pressure (US and USSR both officially anti-colonial); Britain and France did not voluntarily relinquish empire; the pace and nature of independence was determined by the strength of resistance movements

title: Non-Aligned Movement and the Third World
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Third World as a political identity, not just economic description

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Asian and African nations refusing to choose between US and Soviet blocs
leaders using Cold War competition to extract aid from both sides

traps: Treating non-alignment as weakness or fence-sitting — AP tests it as a STRATEGIC CHOICE that gave developing nations leverage: by threatening to align with the other side, non-aligned nations extracted aid, weapons, and political recognition from both superpowers; Nasser got the Aswan Dam funded by the USSR after the US withdrew; this was sophisticated power politics

title: China's Communist Revolution and Mao
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master China's Communist Revolution and Mao for the Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: peasant-based revolution (not urban proletariat)
collectivization causing 15-45 million deaths from famine
Red Guards attacking 'bourgeois' culture, intellectuals sent to re-education camps

traps: Treating Mao's policies as simply evil or misguided — AP tests that the Great Leap Forward was based on ideological beliefs about the superiority of will over expertise; local officials falsified grain production data and people starved while grain was exported; the famine resulted from ideology + political incentives to lie + information suppression — a systemic failure, not just individual cruelty

title: Cold War Proxy Conflicts — Korea, Vietnam, Angola
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Proxy wars drawing Third World nations into superpower competition regardless of local causes

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: UN intervention freezing conflict at 38th parallel; still technically ongoing
US escalation based on domino theory; Tet Offensive turning American public opinion

traps: Treating proxy wars as caused by Cold War competition — AP tests LOCAL CAUSES: the Vietnamese conflict had its own anti-colonial logic predating US involvement; the Korean War was a civil war with deep domestic roots; Cold War competition intensified these conflicts but didn't create them; conflating Cold War causes with local causes loses points on DBQ

title: End of the Cold War — Soviet Collapse
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gorbachev's glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) unintentionally unleashing nationalism

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Soviet command economy unable to compete with US consumer economy
Eastern European states choosing independence when Gorbachev refused to use military force

traps: Attributing Soviet collapse solely to US pressure (Reagan's military spending) — AP tests INTERNAL causes: Soviet economic stagnation, ethnic nationalism in republics, and Gorbachev's reform miscalculations were primary; US pressure was a contributing factor but the Soviet Union collapsed from internal contradictions; single-cause answers receive partial credit

title: Apartheid and Post-Colonial State Challenges
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Mandela's release (1990) and Truth and Reconciliation Commission as alternative to retribution

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: racial segregation institutionalized by law; ANC resistance; international sanctions
artificial borders, ethnic conflict, economic dependency on former colonial powers

traps: Treating decolonization as solving colonialism's problems — AP tests CONTINUITIES: colonial-era borders ignoring ethnic distribution caused post-independence conflicts (Rwanda, Nigeria); export economies built for European consumption persisted after independence; neo-colonialism through multinational corporations and debt replaced formal colonialism

title: Women and Decolonization — Promises and Limits
subtitle: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Women and Decolonization — Promises and Limits for the Cold War and Decolonization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Algeria (FLN), Vietnam, Kenya (Mau Mau)
nationalist leaders often reverting to patriarchal structures after gaining power
constitutions granting rights not translating to lived reality

traps: Treating women's participation in independence movements as leading automatically to equality — AP tests the PATTERN of post-independence rollback; Algerian women who fought the French were told to return to domestic roles after independence; this pattern appears across decolonization and AP tests whether students can identify the gap between revolutionary rhetoric and post-revolutionary practice

title: Economic Globalization — Free Trade and Its Critics
subtitle: Globalization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Globalization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Economic Globalization — Free Trade and Its Critics for the Globalization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: IMF and World Bank creating post-WWII economic order
IMF requiring privatization and austerity in exchange for loans
reducing tariffs expanding trade but increasing inequality within countries

traps: Treating globalization as purely beneficial or purely harmful — AP tests CONTESTED EFFECTS: GDP growth in developing nations but also increased inequality; Western consumers benefiting from cheap goods while factory workers in developing nations face unsafe conditions; a complete analysis identifies winners and losers at multiple scales (global, national, class)

title: Technology and Cultural Globalization
subtitle: Globalization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Globalization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Internet enabling instantaneous global communication and commerce
American cultural exports (film, music, fast food) creating 'McDonaldization' critique

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: local cultures blending with global influences rather than being replaced

traps: Treating cultural globalization as simple American domination — AP tests HYBRIDITY and RESISTANCE: Bollywood producing more films than Hollywood; K-pop as non-Western global cultural export; local food traditions persisting alongside McDonald's; the AP rewards nuanced analysis that acknowledges both homogenization pressures and local adaptation

title: Climate Change and Environmental Globalization
subtitle: Globalization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Globalization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Industrial emissions since 1850 driving atmospheric CO2 increase

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: individual rational behavior producing collective environmental harm
voluntary national commitments without enforcement mechanism

traps: Treating climate change as only a recent issue — AP tests HISTORICAL CAUSATION: industrial revolution beginning the carbon accumulation problem; deforestation for plantation agriculture (colonial period) contributing; the current crisis has a 200-year causal history that AP expects students to connect to earlier periods using continuity reasoning

title: Disease, Migration, and Global Health
subtitle: Globalization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Globalization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Disease, Migration, and Global Health for the Globalization (c. 1900–present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: WWI mobilization spreading disease globally, killing 50-100 million
from regional disease to global pandemic through migration and trade networks
WHO coordinating international response to pandemic threats

traps: Treating pandemics as natural disasters without historical context — AP tests the HUMAN causes: WWI troop movements spread the 1918 flu; global trade routes carried HIV; colonialism disrupting ecosystems created conditions for zoonotic disease emergence; connecting pandemic history to political/economic systems is the AP-level analysis that earns top scores

title: Continuity and Change in the 21st Century
subtitle: Globalization (c. 1900–present)
overview: Globalization (c. 1900–present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Terrorism and asymmetric warfare replacing state-on-state conflict
Rising China challenging US-led world order — echoes of earlier hegemonic transitions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: wealth gap within and between nations wider than at any time since 1900

traps: Treating the present as entirely unprecedented — AP tests HISTORICAL PARALLELS: US-China tension mirrors UK-Germany tension before WWI (Thucydides Trap); inequality patterns echo Gilded Age; terrorist tactics echo anarchist violence of early 20th century; connecting current events to historical patterns is exactly the synthesis skill AP World History tests in the LEQ

title: Pre-Columbian North America — Diversity of Cultures
subtitle: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607)
overview: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Pre-Columbian North America — Diversity of Cultures for the Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Great Plains nomadic hunters vs. Southwest pueblo farmers vs. Eastern Woodlands confederacies
political model influencing Founders debate (disputed but AP-tested)
Mississippi Valley mound builders, Pacific Northwest fishing cultures

traps: Treating all Native Americans as a single culture — AP tests REGIONAL DIVERSITY as its own skill; a DBQ on colonial encounter requires distinguishing between nations; the Iroquois Confederacy's sophisticated political structure specifically appears in comparison questions about democracy's origins

title: Spanish Colonialism — Conquest and the Encomienda
subtitle: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607)
overview: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Conquistadors using indigenous alliances to defeat empires (Aztec, Inca)
Encomienda system extracting indigenous labor for mining and agriculture

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: conversion as both religious goal and tool of social control

traps: Presenting Spanish colonialism as uniquely brutal compared to other Europeans — AP tests that ALL European colonial systems used coerced labor; Spanish colonialism was distinctive in its SCALE (silver mining), religious intensity, and racial hierarchy (casta system), not in its brutality relative to other powers

title: European Contact — Competing Colonial Models
subtitle: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607)
overview: Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master European Contact — Competing Colonial Models for the Period 1: Colonial Foundations (1491–1607) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: trading post empire along coasts
conquest and settlement empire
fur trade alliance network with indigenous peoples

traps: Memorizing facts about each country's colonies without explaining the MODEL differences — AP tests that colonial models reflected home country circumstances: France had fewer settlers and needed indigenous allies; Spain had large armies and sought precious metals; these structural differences explain different relationships with indigenous peoples, which is the AP-level question

title: Chesapeake vs. New England Colonies — Contrasting Societies
subtitle: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754)
overview: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Chesapeake vs. New England Colonies — Contrasting Societies for the Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: profit-driven tobacco economy, indentured servants → enslaved Africans, high mortality
Puritan religious community, family migration, lower mortality, town meeting governance
land grants for sponsoring migrants creating plantation aristocracy in Chesapeake

traps: Treating all colonial regions as similar — AP tests REGIONAL DIFFERENCES as a core skill; the Chesapeake/New England contrast appears in every APUSH exam in some form; key distinction: New England came for religious reasons and built community institutions; Chesapeake came for profit and built hierarchy — these origins explain vastly different political cultures lasting to Civil War

title: Slavery's Expansion — From Indentured Service to Racial Chattel
subtitle: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754)
overview: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Slavery's Expansion — From Indentured Service to Racial Chattel for the Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: poor white and Black servants uniting against planter elite
racial slavery laws distinguishing Black from white servants permanently

terms.term: Middle Passage and the African Diaspora
terms.def: cultural survival through religion, music, family networks

traps: Treating slavery as always the colonial labor system — AP tests the TRANSITION: Chesapeake initially used white indentured servants; racial slavery REPLACED indenture because Bacon's Rebellion showed the danger of armed poor whites; this causation (rebellion → racial slavery) is directly tested and requires understanding the planter class's political calculation

title: Colonial Self-Governance — Assemblies and Salutary Neglect
subtitle: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754)
overview: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Colonial assemblies developing habits of self-governance that made British control difficult to reassert

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: first representative assembly in colonial America (1619)
loose enforcement of trade laws allowing colonial economic development

traps: Treating the Revolution as sudden — AP tests LONG-TERM CAUSES rooted in colonial experience; 150 years of salutary neglect created self-governing institutions; when Britain tried to reassert control after 1763, colonists had decades of precedent for self-rule; the Revolution was a defense of existing rights, not a demand for new ones — this framing earns top scores

title: The Great Awakening — Religion and Democratic Culture
subtitle: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754)
overview: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Itinerant preachers challenging established church authority — religious democratization
George Whitefield using emotional preaching to reach common people
Great Awakening creating culture of questioning authority that feeds into revolutionary mentality

sections.title: The Great Awakening — Religion and Democratic Culture
traps: Treating Great Awakening as purely religious — AP tests its POLITICAL implications: ordinary people were told they could judge their own salvation without church hierarchy; this habit of questioning authority transferred to political sphere; the Awakening created the cultural CONDITIONS for revolutionary skepticism of inherited authority

title: Colonial Economy and Mercantilism
subtitle: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754)
overview: Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Colonial Economy and Mercantilism for the Period 2: Colonial America (1607–1754) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: requiring colonial trade to go through Britain, enriching British merchants
connecting New England, West Africa, Caribbean, Britain
merchants evading trade restrictions and developing anti-British sentiment

traps: Treating mercantilism as simply exploitative — AP tests that colonists initially ACCEPTED mercantilist logic and benefited from British military protection and trade access; resistance began when enforcement tightened AFTER the French and Indian War; the shift from compliance to resistance explains the revolutionary timeline

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: French and Indian War — The Empire's Overreach
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Britain's debt from the war requiring colonial taxation — the trigger for revolution

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Franklin's failed attempt at colonial unity
preventing western settlement, angering colonists who expected war's reward

traps: Starting American Revolution analysis in 1775 — AP tests that the war BEGAN with the French and Indian War (1754); British debt created the taxation problem; Proclamation of 1763 denied colonists their expected western lands; the Stamp Act was Britain's SOLUTION to a debt problem, not an unprovoked attack; framing causation from 1754 demonstrates historical thinking

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: Road to Revolution — Ideology and Escalation
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Road to Revolution — Ideology and Escalation for the Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: British vs. colonial argument about taxation
escalating conflict and propaganda
shifting argument from rights as Englishmen to natural rights — independence justified

traps: Treating the Revolution as a constitutional argument about taxes — AP tests the IDEOLOGICAL SHIFT: early resistance was about parliamentary authority (we have rights as British subjects); Paine's Common Sense shifted to natural rights (monarchy itself is illegitimate); this evolution explains why independence was possible — it required a new theoretical framework, not just a constitutional complaint

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: The Revolution — Who Fought and Who Didn't
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Revolution — Who Fought and Who Didn't for the Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 20% of population; disproportionately recent immigrants, Anglican clergy, wealthy merchants
many fought for British (Lord Dunmore's Proclamation offering freedom to enslaved people who fought)
Daughters of Liberty, camp followers, spies — contributing without citizenship

traps: Treating the Revolution as a unified American uprising — AP tests DIVISIONS: 1/5 were loyalists; enslaved Africans largely sided with Britain (rationally — Britain offered freedom); Native Americans overwhelmingly opposed American independence (frontier expansion threatened their lands); a complete analysis of the Revolution must address these non-revolutionary voices

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: Articles of Confederation — Weakness by Design
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Articles of Confederation — Weakness by Design for the Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Congress requesting money from states, states often refusing
states printing own currency causing inflation
Massachusetts debt crisis showing need for stronger central government

traps: Treating the Articles as simply failed — AP tests that weakness was DELIBERATE: revolutionary generation feared strong central government (just fought one); Articles reflected republican ideology; it was Shays' Rebellion and similar crises that CONVINCED founders that the opposite danger (too weak) was also real; the Constitution was a response to lived experience, not obvious from the start

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: The Constitution — Compromises and Debates
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Constitution — Compromises and Debates for the Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: enslaved people counted as 3/5 for representation — benefiting slaveholder states
bicameral legislature balancing large and small states
Hamilton/Madison arguing for ratification against Anti-Federalist fears of tyranny

traps: Treating constitutional compromises as morally neutral — AP tests that the three-fifths clause was a POLITICAL VICTORY for slaveholder states giving them disproportionate representation for a century; it was not a compromise between slavery and freedom but between slaveholder states with different interests; framing it as morally contested earns higher scores

unitName: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
title: Federalists vs. Democratic-Republicans — First Party System
subtitle: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800)
overview: Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Federalists vs. Democratic-Republicans — First Party System for the Period 3: Revolution and the New Nation (1754–1800) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: national bank, tariffs, manufacturing — favoring merchants and creditors
independent farmers as republican ideal — favoring debtors and South
Hamilton using federal force to assert national authority over western farmers

traps: Treating this as just Hamilton vs. Jefferson personally — AP tests STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES: Hamilton's program favored commercial Northeast; Jefferson's favored agrarian South and West; these were competing visions of America's economic future, not personal conflicts; the party split mapped almost perfectly onto economic interests, which is the AP-level causal analysis

title: Market Revolution — Transportation and Economic Change
subtitle: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848)
overview: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Market Revolution — Transportation and Economic Change for the Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: connecting Great Lakes to Atlantic, cutting shipping costs 90%
young women from farms working factory jobs — new industrial labor force
North manufacturing, South cotton, West grain — interdependent regional economies

traps: Treating Market Revolution as simply economic growth — AP tests its SOCIAL DISRUPTION: farm families moving to cities; women entering wage labor; time discipline replacing seasonal farming rhythms; these social changes fed reform movements (temperance, abolition) because they disrupted traditional community bonds and created new social problems

title: Jacksonian Democracy — Expansion and Exclusion
subtitle: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848)
overview: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Jacksonian Democracy — Expansion and Exclusion for the Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: property requirements removed, democratizing politics for white men
Trail of Tears forcing southeastern nations west
South Carolina claiming right to nullify federal tariff

traps: Treating Jacksonian Democracy as straightforwardly democratic — AP tests the CONTRADICTIONS: democracy expanded for white men while contracting for Native Americans, enslaved people, and women; Jackson presented Indian removal as humanitarian; the Nullification Crisis previews sectional conflict; Jacksonian era simultaneously democratized and excluded — this tension is what AP tests

title: Manifest Destiny — Ideology and Consequences
subtitle: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848)
overview: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Manifest Destiny — Ideology and Consequences for the Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: providential belief that Americans destined to expand to Pacific
disputed Texas border becoming cause for war, gaining California/Southwest
attempting to ban slavery in territory gained from Mexico — reopening sectional conflict

traps: Treating Manifest Destiny as just westward expansion — AP tests it as IDEOLOGY that shaped policy: the belief that expansion was divinely ordained removed moral hesitation about displacing Mexicans and Native Americans; the Wilmot Proviso is crucial because it shows that territorial expansion REIGNITED the slavery debate that Missouri Compromise had temporarily resolved

title: The Second Great Awakening and Reform Movements
subtitle: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848)
overview: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Second Great Awakening and Reform Movements for the Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: belief that humans could create a perfect society — motivating reform
Declaration of Sentiments applying natural rights to women
Garrison's immediate abolition vs. gradual emancipation debate

traps: Listing reforms without explaining their CONNECTION — AP tests that Second Great Awakening created the CULTURAL FOUNDATION for multiple reforms: if society could be perfected, then slavery was a sin requiring immediate action; temperance addressed alcohol's role in poverty; women's rights activists often began in abolition movement; reforms were interconnected, not separate

title: Immigration and Nativism — Irish and German Arrivals
subtitle: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848)
overview: Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Immigration and Nativism — Irish and German Arrivals for the Period 4: Expansion and Reform (1800–1848) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 1 million Irish arriving, concentrated in northeastern cities
anti-Catholic, anti-immigrant political movement
bringing liberal political traditions

traps: Treating nativism as simply prejudice — AP tests the ECONOMIC and CULTURAL logic: Irish immigrants competed with native workers for unskilled jobs (economic threat); Irish Catholicism challenged Protestant American identity (cultural threat); Know-Nothing Party succeeded because it addressed REAL anxieties, even through bigotry; understanding nativist appeal is necessary for historical causation

title: Causes of the Civil War — Slavery and Sectionalism
subtitle: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)
overview: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Causes of the Civil War — Slavery and Sectionalism for the Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: California free state, Fugitive Slave Act — each side getting something
popular sovereignty reopening slavery question, creating Bleeding Kansas
Supreme Court ruling enslaved people had no rights, Congress couldn't ban slavery in territories

traps: Treating slavery as 'one of many causes' alongside tariffs and states' rights — AP tests that slavery was the CENTRAL cause and states' rights / tariffs debates were fundamentally about slavery; Confederate states explicitly stated slavery as the cause in secession documents; the tariff explanation was developed AFTER the war as Lost Cause mythology; treating causes as equal earns partial credit

title: The Civil War — Military and Political Dimensions
subtitle: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)
overview: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Civil War — Military and Political Dimensions for the Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: war aim shifted from union preservation to slavery abolition
180,000 African Americans fighting for Union, changing war's meaning
Sherman's March targeting Confederate civilian infrastructure and morale

traps: Treating the Emancipation Proclamation as Lincoln's moral conversion — AP tests the POLITICAL CALCULATION: Proclamation freed enslaved people only in Confederate states (not border states) to avoid losing them; it was designed to weaken the Confederacy militarily and prevent British recognition; Lincoln's private moral views evolved, but the document itself was strategic, not primarily moral

title: Reconstruction — Radical Plans and Resistance
subtitle: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)
overview: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Reconstruction — Radical Plans and Resistance for the Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: birthright citizenship and equal protection — transformative constitutional change
federal agency providing education, labor contracts, legal assistance
replacing slavery with debt peonage, keeping Black southerners economically bound

traps: Treating Reconstruction as a failed experiment — AP tests that Reconstruction was a GENUINE ACHIEVEMENT undermined by Northern abandonment: the 14th and 15th Amendments were radical achievements; they failed not because they were wrong but because the federal government stopped enforcing them; the question is NOT why Reconstruction failed but why the North abandoned it (compromise of 1877, racial fatigue, economic interests)

title: The End of Reconstruction — Compromise and Redemption
subtitle: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)
overview: Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The End of Reconstruction — Compromise and Redemption for the Period 5: Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Hayes becomes president, federal troops leave South
white supremacists regaining control of southern state governments
criminal justice system creating new form of forced labor replacing slavery

traps: Treating 1877 as the end of Black political life in the South — AP tests that Black political participation continued in some areas until the 1890s; the systematic disenfranchisement through literacy tests, poll taxes, and terrorism intensified AFTER 1877; the 1877-1900 period saw gradual rather than sudden loss of rights, which is the accurate timeline AP expects

title: Industrialization — Railroads, Steel, and Big Business
subtitle: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898)
overview: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Industrialization — Railroads, Steel, and Big Business for the Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: connecting national markets, enabling industrial economy
controlling all stages of production from raw material to retail
monopoly through buying out all competitors in same industry

traps: Treating business integration as simply greedy — AP tests the ECONOMIC LOGIC: vertical integration reduced costs by eliminating middlemen; horizontal integration eliminated competition reducing price uncertainty; Carnegie and Rockefeller created modern business structures that lowered consumer prices even while they exploited workers; AP expects analysis of economic rationale alongside labor exploitation

title: Labor Movement — Knights of Labor to AFL
subtitle: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898)
overview: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Labor Movement — Knights of Labor to AFL for the Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: inclusive (women, Black workers, unskilled) but declined after Haymarket (1886)
exclusive skilled craft workers, focused on wages/hours not social transformation
federal government using injunction to break strike — government siding with capital

traps: Treating all labor organizations as equally radical — AP tests the SPECTRUM: Knights sought fundamental economic transformation; AFL accepted capitalism and wanted better terms within it; this distinction explains their different tactics and different responses from employers and government; the AFL's conservatism was a strategic choice that explains its survival

title: Populism — Farmers' Alliance and Political Challenge
subtitle: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898)
overview: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Populism — Farmers' Alliance and Political Challenge for the Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: southern farmers trapped in debt to merchants, unable to escape cotton monoculture
demanding railroad regulation, graduated income tax, direct election of senators
silver coinage inflating currency to help debtor farmers

traps: Treating Populism as a failure because Bryan lost in 1896 — AP tests that Populist platform was ADOPTED by Progressives over the next two decades; income tax (16th Amendment), direct Senate election (17th Amendment), railroad regulation (ICC strengthening) all happened; Populism failed electorally but succeeded intellectually — this is the continuity argument AP rewards

title: The West — Conquest, Settlement, and Myth
subtitle: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898)
overview: Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The West — Conquest, Settlement, and Myth for the Period 6: The Gilded Age (1865–1898) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Sioux religious revival expressing desperation; Wounded Knee massacre (1890)
breaking up tribal lands into individual allotments — destroying collective land ownership
American democracy produced by frontier experience — ideology shaping historical memory

traps: Treating westward expansion as settlement of empty land — AP tests Native American AGENCY and RESISTANCE: Ghost Dance was a rational response to cultural destruction; Wounded Knee was a massacre of unarmed people; the Dawes Act was designed to destroy the cultural basis of Native American identity; framing the West as 'empty' is the ideological perspective Turner promoted, not historical fact

unitName: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
title: Progressivism — Reform, Regulation, and Its Limits
subtitle: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
overview: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Progressivism — Reform, Regulation, and Its Limits for the Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: journalists exposing corporate abuses (Sinclair's The Jungle, Tarbell on Standard Oil)
Roosevelt's distinction between good trusts (efficient) and bad trusts (predatory)
Jim Crow ignored or enforced; women divided on suffrage approach

traps: Treating Progressivism as uniformly liberal — AP tests the EXCLUSIONS: most Progressives focused on white industrial workers; Woodrow Wilson re-segregated the federal workforce; many Progressive women accepted racial hierarchy; a top-score analysis acknowledges that Progressive reform was class and race selective, benefiting white workers while leaving Black Americans in Jim Crow

unitName: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
title: WWI and the American Home Front
subtitle: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
overview: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master WWI and the American Home Front for the Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: government propaganda normalizing speech suppression
imprisoning antiwar activists (Eugene Debs)
Black southerners moving north for factory jobs, escaping Jim Crow — 1 million by 1920

traps: Treating WWI's home front as primarily about patriotism — AP tests the REPRESSION: Espionage Act imprisoned people for opposing the draft; the government suppressed civil liberties with public support; this pattern (wartime civil liberties reduction) connects to WWII internment and Cold War McCarthyism; AP tests continuity of government wartime overreach across periods

unitName: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
title: The 1920s — Prosperity, Culture Wars, and Exclusion
subtitle: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
overview: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The 1920s — Prosperity, Culture Wars, and Exclusion for the Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Black cultural production asserting dignity and humanity (Hughes, Hurston)
Scopes Trial over evolution teaching
Emergency Quota Act (1921) and National Origins Act (1924) — nativist victory

traps: Treating the 1920s as uniformly prosperous — AP tests the UNDERSIDE: farmers never recovered from post-WWI prices; Black Americans faced lynching and the new KKK (4 million members by 1924); immigration restriction reflected racial ideology; the prosperity was real but narrowly distributed; the contrast between Jazz Age glamour and widespread exclusion is the AP-level analysis

unitName: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
title: The New Deal — Programs, Opposition, and Legacy
subtitle: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
overview: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The New Deal — Programs, Opposition, and Legacy for the Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: relief and recovery (CCC, FERA, bank holiday)
reform (Social Security, Wagner Act protecting unions)
Supreme Court striking down programs; Huey Long's 'Share Our Wealth'; conservative business opposition

traps: Treating the New Deal as solving the Depression — AP tests that the Depression did NOT end until WWII spending; New Deal reduced suffering and created lasting programs but GDP did not recover to 1929 levels until 1941; opposition from BOTH right (too radical) and left (too conservative) is equally important; AP asks about New Deal DEBATES as much as its programs

unitName: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
title: WWII — Mobilization, Internment, and the Double V
subtitle: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945)
overview: Period 7: The Progressive Era through New Deal (1890–1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Rosie the Riveter and women's industrial work — temporary shift in gender roles

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Korematsu ruling upholding it — wartime national security vs. civil liberties
Black soldiers fighting for victory abroad AND democracy at home

traps: Treating WWII as straightforwardly unifying for all Americans — AP tests the CONTRADICTIONS: government interning American citizens based on race while fighting racist Nazi Germany; Black soldiers fighting for democracy denied to them at home; women entering workforce then pushed back out after war; these contradictions fed the civil rights movement — WWII as accelerator of domestic change is the AP connection

title: The Cold War at Home — Containment and Conformity
subtitle: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980)
overview: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Cold War at Home — Containment and Conformity for the Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: containment becoming bipartisan consensus
Senate hearings targeting suspected communists — climate of fear
GI Bill creating white middle-class homeownership, excluding Black veterans

traps: Treating anticommunism as only about foreign policy — AP tests DOMESTIC EFFECTS: McCarthyism silenced labor activists, civil rights leaders, and intellectuals by labeling dissent as communist; the Cold War consensus limited debate on capitalism and racial equality; domestic anticommunism and foreign containment were two sides of the same ideological coin

title: Civil Rights Movement — Strategies and Achievements
subtitle: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980)
overview: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Civil Rights Movement — Strategies and Achievements for the Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: NAACP using courts (Brown v. Board 1954 overturning Plessy)
Montgomery Bus Boycott, sit-ins, Freedom Rides — filling jails to expose injustice
federal enforcement of 15th Amendment — transformative legislative achievement

traps: Treating the Civil Rights Movement as a simple morality play between good and evil — AP tests the STRATEGIC DEBATES within the movement: King's nonviolence vs. SNCC's more confrontational approach vs. Malcolm X's Black nationalism; the movement was contested internally; these debates explain different outcomes and AP rewards analysis of internal movement tensions

title: The Great Society and Its Critics
subtitle: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980)
overview: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Great Society and Its Critics for the Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: federal health insurance for elderly and poor

terms.term: Voting Rights Act and Civil Rights Act
terms.def: completing legal framework of equality
Barry Goldwater's 1964 campaign articulating modern conservatism

traps: Treating Great Society as uniformly successful or failed — AP tests UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES: welfare programs criticized for creating dependency; urban renewal destroying Black neighborhoods; the conservative backlash was ORGANIZED RESPONSE to Great Society expansion; understanding the rise of modern conservatism as a reaction to liberal overreach is crucial for explaining 1980 Reagan election

title: Vietnam and the 1960s Divisions
subtitle: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980)
overview: Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Vietnam and the 1960s Divisions for the Period 8: Postwar America (1945–1980) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Congress giving Johnson blank check for escalation based on disputed incident
military surprise undermining official optimism, turning public opinion
MLK assassination, RFK assassination, Democratic convention chaos

traps: Treating antiwar movement as the main story of 1960s — AP tests that the MAJORITY of Americans supported the war initially; the shift was gradual; the antiwar movement was opposed by a 'silent majority' (Nixon's term); 1968 fracturing of the New Deal coalition is the key political consequence — it explains how Nixon won and begins the conservative realignment story

title: The Reagan Revolution — Conservative Realignment
subtitle: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present)
overview: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Reagan Revolution — Conservative Realignment for the Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: tax cuts for wealthy producing investment and growth ('trickle-down')
reducing federal oversight of business as philosophical commitment
Reagan coalition uniting economic conservatives and religious right (Moral Majority)

traps: Treating Reaganism as simply pro-business — AP tests the COALITION: Reagan united economic libertarians (less regulation, lower taxes) with social conservatives (anti-abortion, school prayer) who had different but complementary goals; the New Right was a political coalition requiring analysis of MULTIPLE conservative traditions, not just economic policy

title: End of the Cold War and New World Order
subtitle: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present)
overview: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gorbachev's reforms unintentionally ending Soviet control of Eastern Europe

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: international coalition as model of 'New World Order' multilateralism
unilateralism vs. multilateralism after Soviet collapse

traps: Treating the Cold War's end as a simple American victory — AP tests COMPLEXITY: Soviet collapse had internal causes (economic stagnation, nationalism); claiming it was purely due to Reagan's military pressure ignores Gorbachev's role; the end of bipolarity created new instability (Yugoslavia, Somalia) that the US was unprepared for; triumphalism misses the AP-level analysis

title: America at the Turn of the Millennium — Continuity and Change
subtitle: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present)
overview: Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master America at the Turn of the Millennium — Continuity and Change for the Period 9: Contemporary America (1980–Present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: manufacturing moving overseas, creating Rust Belt unemployment
Patriot Act, Iraq War, debates about security vs. liberty
gap between wealthy and working class widening to Gilded Age levels

traps: Treating contemporary history as too recent to analyze historically — AP tests CONTINUITY: globalization echoes market revolution; war on terror's civil liberties debates echo WWI Espionage Act; rising inequality parallels Gilded Age; connecting contemporary issues to historical patterns using specific evidence is exactly the synthesis skill AP tests in the required LEQ

title: The Italian Renaissance — Humanism and Patronage
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Italian Renaissance — Humanism and Patronage for the Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: focus on classical learning, individual potential, secular achievement
Medici funding artists as political legitimacy strategy
Erasmus adapting Italian humanism to religious reform impulse

traps: Treating the Renaissance as a complete break from the Middle Ages — AP tests CONTINUITY: Renaissance scholars used medieval universities and Church patronage; most Renaissance art was religious; the shift was emphasis (individual achievement alongside God) not rupture; distinguishing genuine change from exaggerated discontinuity is a core AP European History skill

title: Protestant Reformation — Causes and Spread
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Printing press enabling rapid spread of Lutheran ideas across German states

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: indulgence abuse as trigger, but deeper theological dispute about salvation by faith alone
the elect chosen by God — work ethic as sign of grace (Weber thesis)

traps: Treating the Reformation as solely about Church corruption — AP tests that Luther's core dispute was THEOLOGICAL: his doctrine of justification by faith alone contradicted Catholic sacramental theology; corruption angered people but theology sustained the movement; Weber's thesis about Calvinism and capitalism is specifically tested in SAQ and DBQ contexts

title: Catholic Reformation and the Wars of Religion
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Catholic Reformation and the Wars of Religion for the Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: clarifying Catholic doctrine, reforming abuses WITHOUT theological compromise
education and missions as Catholic intellectual and global expansion strategy
beginning as religious conflict, ending as great power competition

traps: Treating the Thirty Years' War as purely religious — AP tests the TRANSITION: Peace of Westphalia (1648) established state sovereignty over religious affairs; the war's last phase was France (Catholic) fighting Habsburg (Catholic) for political reasons; the outcome was the modern state system where religion lost its power to override political interests — this is the AP-level interpretive point

title: The New Monarchies — Centralization and State Building
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The New Monarchies — Centralization and State Building for the Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Louis XIV ('L'état, c'est moi') and absolutism as ideology
palace as political instrument controlling nobility through ceremony and dependency
professional administrators bypassing noble power in French provinces

traps: Treating absolutism as simply tyranny — AP tests that absolutism was a RESPONSE to the disorder of religious wars; Louis XIV's success in controlling nobility was real and made France Europe's most powerful state; the limits of absolutism (nobles retained local power, Church retained authority) are equally important; AP tests that absolutism was more ideological than fully realized

title: The Scientific Revolution — New Ways of Knowing
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Scientific Revolution — New Ways of Knowing for the Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: heliocentric model challenging Church authority over natural knowledge
Bacon's induction, Descartes' deduction — reason over tradition
if Church was wrong about astronomy, what else? — undermining religious authority

traps: Treating the Scientific Revolution as defeating religion — AP tests the COMPLEXITY: most scientists remained devoutly religious; Newton spent more time on theology than physics; the conflict was about authority over natural knowledge, not existence of God; the long-term implication (secular reasoning applied to society) came later through the Enlightenment, not immediately from science

title: Exploration and Early Colonialism — European Perspectives
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Spanish and Portuguese dominance through papal Treaty of Tordesillas (1494)
Slave trade's origins in Portuguese African exploration
Columbian Exchange effects on European population and diet

sections.title: Exploration and Early Colonialism — European Perspectives
traps: Focusing only on European perspectives in exploration questions — AP European History tests European INTERNAL debates: Spanish 'Black Legend' vs. Las Casas defending indigenous rights; debates about colonialism were happening in Europe simultaneously with conquest; an AP-level answer addresses how colonialism shaped European politics and economy, not just the colonies themselves

title: The Commercial Revolution and Early Capitalism
subtitle: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648)
overview: Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Commercial Revolution and Early Capitalism for the Renaissance and Reformation (c. 1450–c. 1648) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: spreading investment risk enabling large-scale commercial ventures
stable currency and credit facilitating Dutch commercial dominance
Spanish silver inflating European prices, hurting fixed-income nobles

traps: Treating the Commercial Revolution as just 'more trade' — AP tests STRUCTURAL CHANGES: joint-stock companies were a new organizational form distributing risk; the shift from barter to credit-based commerce required new legal and financial institutions; the Price Revolution redistributed wealth from landlords (fixed rents) to merchants (flexible prices) — this class shift underlies later political conflicts

title: The Enlightenment — Philosophy and Its Political Applications
subtitle: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815)
overview: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Voltaire's religious skepticism and religious tolerance arguments
Philosophes using salons to spread ideas across European educated class

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: government deriving legitimacy from consent of governed

traps: Treating the Enlightenment as a unified movement — AP tests INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS: Voltaire favored enlightened despotism; Rousseau's general will was more democratic; Locke emphasized property rights; Montesquieu emphasized institutional checks; these different conclusions from similar premises explain why Enlightenment ideas produced different revolutionary outcomes in America, France, and Germany

title: The French Revolution — Phases and Radicalization
subtitle: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815)
overview: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The French Revolution — Phases and Radicalization for the Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: moderate phase
Committee of Public Safety executing 'enemies' including revolutionaries
conservative backlash executing Robespierre, ending the Terror

traps: Treating the Terror as Robespierre's personal cruelty — AP tests STRUCTURAL CAUSES: the Terror emerged from existential military threat (Austria, Prussia invading) combined with internal counter-revolution (Vendée uprising); emergency conditions produced emergency measures; Robespierre was an instrument of those conditions; AP expects analysis of structural causes, not individual villainy

title: Napoleon — Consolidation and Contradiction
subtitle: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815)
overview: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Napoleon — Consolidation and Contradiction for the Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: legal equality, property rights, religious tolerance — spreading revolutionary principles
blockade against Britain damaging European economies including France's allies
Napoleon's conquests inspiring nationalist resistance that eventually defeated him

traps: Treating Napoleon as either revolutionary hero or military dictator — AP tests BOTH: he preserved key Revolutionary achievements (legal equality, abolition of feudalism) while ending political liberty (press censorship, secret police); this contradiction defines his legacy; most importantly, the nationalism his conquests inspired became the force that destroyed his empire — this irony is the AP-level interpretive claim

title: Congress of Vienna — Conservatism and Balance of Power
subtitle: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815)
overview: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Congress of Vienna — Conservatism and Balance of Power for the Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: legitimacy (restoring old dynasties), balance of power, suppression of nationalism
great powers collectively managing conflicts to prevent revolutionary war
restoring Bourbon monarchies while unable to fully reverse constitutional gains

traps: Treating the Congress of Vienna as simply reactionary — AP tests its ACHIEVEMENTS: the Congress created a balance of power that kept Europe mostly at peace for 100 years until WWI; the Concert of Europe was an early international security system; Metternich was wrong about nationalism but right that great power cooperation prevented general war; the system's longevity shows its sophistication

title: The Industrial Revolution in Europe — Spread and Social Effects
subtitle: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815)
overview: Absolutism and Constitutionalism (c. 1648–c. 1815) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Belgium industrializing first after Britain — coal, geography, capital availability

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: network connecting European markets, driving steel demand
artisans losing independence to become factory wage workers

traps: Treating industrialization as identical across countries — AP tests NATIONAL VARIATIONS: German industrialization was STATE-DIRECTED (government building railways, protecting industry); French industrialization was slower, retaining more artisan production; these differences explain why German socialism was more statist and French anarchism was more artisan-focused; industrialization produced different politics in different national contexts

title: Ideological Responses to Industrialization
subtitle: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914)
overview: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Ideological Responses to Industrialization for the Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: free market, individual rights, limited government — representing middle-class interests
collective ownership, class consciousness — representing working-class interests
tradition, hierarchy, gradual change — representing landed aristocracy and clergy

traps: Treating these ideologies as fixed — AP tests EVOLUTION: liberalism began as radical (against aristocracy) and became conservative (defending capitalism against socialism) by century's end; socialism fragmented into reformist social democracy vs. revolutionary Marxism; AP expects understanding that ideological labels shifted meaning as the class struggle evolved throughout the 19th century

title: Revolutions of 1848 — The Springtime of Nations
subtitle: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914)
overview: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Revolutions of 1848 — The Springtime of Nations for the Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: economic depression (1847 crop failures), frustrated liberal nationalism, urban working-class hunger
Second Republic established then Louis-Napoleon elected, becoming Napoleon III by coup
revolutions in Vienna, Hungary, Italy all suppressed — conservatism survived

traps: Treating 1848 as simply failed revolutions — AP tests WHY they failed: middle-class liberals feared working-class radicalism more than conservatism; peasants given land reform had little more to gain; nationalist movements divided along ethnic lines; the failure revealed the SPLIT between liberal nationalism (middle class) and socialist labor demands (workers) that defined European politics for the next century

title: Nationalism and Unification — Germany and Italy
subtitle: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914)
overview: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: New German Empire threatening European balance of power — alarming Britain and France

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: manipulating events (Ems Dispatch) to provoke wars serving Prussian goals
Cavour's diplomatic manipulation + Garibaldi's military campaigns

traps: Crediting nationalism for unification — AP tests that ELITE MANIPULATION drove unification: Bismarck used nationalism as a tool, not as a sincere belief; he manipulated the Ems Dispatch to provoke France into declaring war, making Prussia the defensive party; Cavour similarly maneuvered Austria into appearing the aggressor; unification was achieved through calculated statecraft, not popular nationalist enthusiasm

title: The New Imperialism — Causes and Justifications
subtitle: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914)
overview: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The New Imperialism — Causes and Justifications for the Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: scientific racism legitimizing European domination of 'inferior races'
raw materials, markets, investment outlets
European powers partitioning Africa without African consultation

traps: Using only economic causes for imperialism — AP tests the NATIONALIST and PSYCHOLOGICAL dimensions: European public opinion supported imperialism as national prestige; the scramble was competitive (fear of rivals, not just profit); Social Darwinism provided genuine belief system, not just hypocrisy; a complete AP response balances economic, nationalist, and ideological causes with specific evidence

title: Science, Culture, and Modernity (1850–1914)
subtitle: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914)
overview: Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Science, Culture, and Modernity (1850–1914) for the Industrialization and its Effects (c. 1815–c. 1914) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: challenge to religious understanding of human origins and purpose
God is dead — traditional morality losing foundation, secular ethics needed
impressionism, expressionism rejecting realistic representation

traps: Treating intellectual history as separate from political history — AP tests CONNECTIONS: Darwin's ideas were applied to society (Social Darwinism) justifying imperialism and racism; Nietzsche's nihilism contributed to post-WWI disillusionment; modernist rejection of tradition in art paralleled political radicalism; AP rewards connecting cultural/intellectual developments to political and social contexts

unitName: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
title: Causes and Course of WWI
subtitle: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
overview: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Alliance system converting Balkan crisis into world war

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Germany's two-front war strategy requiring rapid French defeat
industrial warfare consuming millions

traps: Treating the alliance system as the sole cause — AP tests the INTERACTION: German militarism drove the arms race; imperialism created colonial rivalries; nationalism made compromise politically impossible; the alliance system was the MECHANISM but the underlying tensions explain why compromise failed; AP European History specifically tests the Fischer Controversy (German war guilt debate)

unitName: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
title: The Russian Revolution and Bolshevik State
subtitle: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
overview: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Russian Revolution and Bolshevik State for the The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.term: Lenin's adaptation of Marxism to Russian conditions
terms.def: peasant-based, vanguard party leadership
Reds vs. Whites + foreign intervention
tactical retreat to mixed economy to rebuild after civil war devastation

traps: Treating Bolshevik victory as inevitable — AP tests CONTINGENCY: the Bolsheviks were a small minority who succeeded through organizational discipline and specific promises; the Civil War nearly destroyed them; Lenin's NEP shows pragmatic retreat from communist purity; the question of whether Stalinism was the inevitable outcome of Leninism or a contingent result of Stalin's personality is a major AP European History interpretive debate

unitName: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
title: Rise of Fascism — Italy and Germany
subtitle: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
overview: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Rise of Fascism — Italy and Germany for the The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fascism achieving power through threat and legal appointment, not revolution
elections, then Enabling Act — destroying democracy from within
Versailles humiliation, economic depression, fear of communism

traps: Treating fascism as pure evil requiring no historical explanation — AP tests that fascism appealed to REAL INTERESTS: middle-class fear of communist expropriation; nationalist resentment of Versailles; desire for order after instability; explaining HOW fascism gained support (not excusing it) is the historical task; the structural explanation earns full credit; attributing it to Hitler's charisma alone earns partial credit

unitName: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
title: WWII — Causes, Course, and Consequences
subtitle: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945)
overview: The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master WWII — Causes, Course, and Consequences for the The World Wars and Interwar Period (c. 1914–c. 1945) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Britain/France accepting Hitler's demands hoping to avoid war — Munich (1938)
industrialized genocide requiring state bureaucracy, collaborators, and bystander complicity
US commitment to European reconstruction and security

traps: Treating appeasement as simply cowardly — AP tests the CONTEXT: British military was unprepared in 1938; British public opposed war; Chamberlain bought time that allowed rearmament; the question is whether more time helped Britain or Germany more — a defensible historical question; AP rewards contextualizing appeasement within Britain's actual military and political constraints, not just moral condemnation

title: Cold War Europe — Division and Integration
subtitle: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present)
overview: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Marshall Plan creating economic interdependence binding Western Europe to US

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.term: European Coal and Steel Community (1951) → EEC (1957)
terms.def: economic integration as peace strategy
Soviet-imposed communist governments, Comecon as economic counterpart to Marshall Plan

traps: Treating European integration as purely economic — AP tests the POLITICAL motivation: Monnet and Schuman designed integration to make war between France and Germany structurally impossible by entangling their economies; the ECSC was a peace project that used economics as the mechanism; understanding this original purpose explains subsequent integration logic and British reluctance (island nation less threatened by continental war)

title: Decolonization and European Identity
subtitle: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present)
overview: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Immigration from former colonies transforming European demographics and identity debates

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: France's most traumatic decolonization — 1 million European settlers displaced
Britain and France humiliated by US pressure — end of European great power status

traps: Treating decolonization as only an overseas story — AP tests the DOMESTIC effects: Algerian War nearly caused French civil war and ended the Fourth Republic (de Gaulle returning to power); Suez revealed European dependence on US; immigration from former colonies created multicultural societies that challenged European national identities; decolonization was a European political crisis, not just a colonial one

title: 1968 and Social Movements
subtitle: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present)
overview: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master 1968 and Social Movements for the Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present) unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: student-worker uprising nearly toppling de Gaulle — generational revolt against authority
Czechoslovakia's liberalization crushed by Soviet tanks
new social movements transforming European politics outside traditional left-right

traps: Treating 1968 as a revolutionary moment that failed — AP tests LONG-TERM EFFECTS: the counterculture transformed values (sexual liberation, environmental consciousness, distrust of authority) even without political revolution; de Gaulle survived but resigned the next year; the CULTURAL revolution succeeded even where the political one failed; this distinction between political and cultural change is the AP-level interpretive claim

title: End of Cold War and European Integration
subtitle: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present)
overview: Cold War and Contemporary Europe (c. 1945–Present) 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gorbachev refusing to use military force — Eastern European revolutions succeeding without Soviet suppression

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: trade union becoming opposition political force
creating European Union with single currency, citizenship

traps: Treating EU integration as automatic progress — AP tests NATIONAL RESISTANCE: Britain's Euroscepticism had deep roots (sovereignty, distinct legal tradition); French farmers opposing agricultural liberalization; German fears of surrendering the deutschmark; the EU succeeded in some areas (single market) and failed in others (common foreign policy); Brexit is the culmination of British resistance to integration that began at Maastricht

title: Scarcity, Opportunity Cost, and the PPC
subtitle: Basic Economic Concepts
overview: Basic Economic Concepts 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: PPC shows maximum combinations of two goods — points ON curve are efficient

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: value of next best alternative given up — the true cost of any decision
resources or technology shift the curve; allocation choices move along it

traps: Drawing a PPC shift when the question shows a movement — a MOVEMENT along the PPC occurs when you reallocate existing resources; the CURVE SHIFTS only when total productive capacity changes (more resources, better technology); AP multiple choice frequently tests this distinction with a scenario requiring you to identify whether the change is a shift or movement

title: Comparative Advantage and Trade
subtitle: Basic Economic Concepts
overview: Basic Economic Concepts 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Specialization and trade expanding consumption possibilities beyond the PPC

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: lower opportunity cost, not absolute production ability
mutually beneficial trade occurs between the two countries' opportunity costs

traps: Calculating comparative advantage using total output instead of opportunity cost — ALWAYS convert to opportunity cost (what you give up of one good to produce one more of the other); the country with the LOWER opportunity cost has comparative advantage; a common AP trap: one country has absolute advantage in both goods but each has comparative advantage in one — both still benefit from trade

unitName: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
title: GDP — Measuring National Output
subtitle: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
overview: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master GDP — Measuring National Output for the Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: GDP = C + I + G + NX — memorize and know what each includes/excludes
nominal uses current prices; real adjusts for inflation using base year prices
intermediate goods, non-market production, underground economy, income distribution

traps: Including intermediate goods in GDP calculations — GDP counts FINAL goods only to avoid double-counting; if you count steel AND the car made from it, you've counted the steel twice; AP free response frequently requires identifying what IS and IS NOT included in GDP; memorize the exclusions (used goods, financial transactions, transfer payments) as carefully as the inclusions

unitName: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
title: Unemployment — Types and Measurement
subtitle: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
overview: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Natural rate of unemployment = frictional + structural (NOT zero unemployment)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: between jobs (normal, unavoidable); structural: skills mismatch; cyclical: recession-caused

terms.term: Labor force participation rate vs. unemployment rate
terms.def: discouraged workers leaving labor force REDUCES the measured rate

traps: Treating full employment as zero unemployment — full employment means NO CYCLICAL unemployment, but frictional and structural persist; the natural rate (about 4-5%) IS full employment; AP tests that reducing frictional unemployment (better job-matching services) lowers the natural rate; reducing cyclical unemployment is the goal of stabilization policy — these are different policy targets

unitName: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
title: Inflation — Measurement and Effects
subtitle: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle
overview: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Inflation — Measurement and Effects for the Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fixed basket of goods measuring price level change for consumers
hurts lenders (paid back in less valuable dollars); helps borrowers
extreme inflation destroying the medium of exchange function of money (Germany 1923)

traps: Treating all inflation as equally bad — AP tests the DISTRIBUTIONAL effects: unexpected inflation transfers wealth from lenders to borrowers; anticipated inflation is built into interest rates and causes less disruption; deflation is ALSO harmful (delays purchases, increases real debt burden); the AP macro question is usually about unexpected inflation's effects on specific groups, requiring you to identify who holds assets vs. owes debts

title: Aggregate Demand — The AD Curve
subtitle: National Income and Price Determination
overview: National Income and Price Determination 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: AD = C + I + G + NX — same components as GDP but showing quantity demanded at each price level
