sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: wealth effect, interest rate effect, foreign purchases effect
changes in C, I, G, NX that are NOT caused by price level changes

traps: Confusing a movement along AD with a shift — price level changes MOVE you along the AD curve (same curve, different point); only NON-PRICE-LEVEL factors shift AD (consumer confidence, government spending, foreign income); this is the most common error on AP macro; in free response, always state whether you're showing a shift (draw new curve) or movement (show point moving on existing curve)

title: Aggregate Supply — Short Run and Long Run
subtitle: National Income and Price Determination
overview: National Income and Price Determination 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Aggregate Supply — Short Run and Long Run for the National Income and Price Determination unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: higher prices make production more profitable in short run (input costs sticky)

terms.term: LRAS is vertical at full employment
terms.def: in long run, all prices adjust, so output returns to natural level
input prices, supply shocks; LRAS shifts: changes in productive capacity

traps: Drawing SRAS when you mean LRAS — a key AP trap: 'supply-side policies' that increase LRAS (more workers, better technology) are different from expansionary fiscal policy that increases AD; AP free response specifically tests whether you correctly draw LRAS as vertical; a non-vertical LRAS costs you the graphing point; practice drawing the three-curve AS-AD model until vertical LRAS is automatic

title: The Multiplier Effect
subtitle: National Income and Price Determination
overview: National Income and Price Determination 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Spending multiplier = 1/(1-MPC) = 1/MPS — larger MPC means larger multiplier
Tax multiplier = -MPC/(1-MPC) — smaller than spending multiplier because first dollar of tax cut is partly saved
Balanced budget multiplier = 1 — equal increase in G and T increases GDP by the same amount

sections.title: The Multiplier Effect
traps: Using the spending multiplier for tax changes — the TAX MULTIPLIER is smaller in magnitude than the spending multiplier (MPC/MPS vs. 1/MPS) because the first round of a tax cut is partly saved; AP free response frequently asks you to calculate both and explain why they differ; the balanced budget multiplier (= 1) showing that equal G and T increases raise GDP is a classic multiple choice trap

title: Short-Run Equilibrium vs. Long-Run Self-Correction
subtitle: National Income and Price Determination
overview: National Income and Price Determination 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Short-Run Equilibrium vs. Long-Run Self-Correction for the National Income and Price Determination unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: equilibrium output below full employment — wages eventually fall, SRAS shifts right
output above potential — wages eventually rise, SRAS shifts left back to LRAS
without policy, the economy eventually returns to LRAS

traps: Forgetting to show the self-correction when asked about long-run outcomes — AP free response asking 'what happens in the long run' requires showing SRAS shifting to restore LRAS equilibrium; the sequence is: gap identified → wage adjustment → SRAS shifts → new long-run equilibrium at LRAS; missing any step of this sequence loses graphing and explanation points

title: Money — Functions, Supply, and Demand
subtitle: Financial Sector
overview: Financial Sector 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Money — Functions, Supply, and Demand for the Financial Sector unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account
M1 (cash + checking deposits); M2 (M1 + savings + money market)
transaction demand (rises with GDP) + asset demand (falls as interest rates rise)

traps: Treating the money market graph like a regular supply/demand model — the money SUPPLY is vertical (set by the Fed, not price-sensitive); money DEMAND slopes downward because higher interest rates make holding non-interest cash more costly; the equilibrium interest rate is where they meet; AP specifically tests shifting money supply right (lower interest rate) vs. left (higher rate) as the mechanism of monetary policy

title: Banking and Money Creation
subtitle: Financial Sector
overview: Financial Sector 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Required reserve ratio determining the money multiplier = 1/RRR

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: bank loans creating deposits creating more loans (the multiplier process)
the rate banks charge each other for overnight reserve loans — the Fed's key policy instrument

traps: Confusing the money multiplier with the spending multiplier — MONEY multiplier = 1/RRR (reserve ratio); SPENDING multiplier = 1/MPS (marginal propensity to save); AP tests both in the same exam; the money multiplier tells you the maximum new money from a deposit; in practice the actual increase is less because banks hold excess reserves and people hold cash outside the banking system — AP tests this 'leakage'

title: The Federal Reserve and Monetary Policy
subtitle: Financial Sector
overview: Financial Sector 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Federal Reserve and Monetary Policy for the Financial Sector unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: lower federal funds rate → increased investment → AD shifts right
raise federal funds rate → less investment → AD shifts left
open market operations (primary), discount rate, reserve requirements

traps: Stopping the monetary policy chain at 'lower interest rates' — AP free response requires the FULL chain: Fed buys bonds → bank reserves increase → federal funds rate falls → investment increases → AD shifts right → real GDP increases, unemployment falls, price level rises; each link in the chain is worth points; stopping at 'more money in economy' without tracing through interest rates to AD earns partial credit

title: Fiscal Policy — Government Spending and Taxation
subtitle: Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies
overview: Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Fiscal Policy — Government Spending and Taxation for the Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: increase G or decrease T → shifts AD right
decrease G or increase T → shifts AD left
government borrowing driving up interest rates, reducing private investment

traps: Ignoring crowding out in fiscal policy analysis — when the government borrows to fund spending, it COMPETES for loanable funds with private borrowers, raising interest rates and reducing investment; AP free response specifically asks about crowding out as a limitation of fiscal policy; a complete answer traces: deficit spending → increased demand for loanable funds → higher interest rates → reduced investment → partially offsets AD increase

title: Phillips Curve — Short Run and Long Run
subtitle: Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies
overview: Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Phillips Curve — Short Run and Long Run for the Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment
vertical at natural rate of unemployment (no long-run tradeoff)
both inflation and unemployment rising simultaneously

traps: Treating the Phillips curve as a permanent policy menu — AP tests that the short-run tradeoff is TEMPORARY; increasing AD to lower unemployment causes inflation, but workers adjust wage expectations, shifting SRPC upward; the long-run result is higher inflation at the SAME unemployment rate; stagflation (1970s) proved this — policy makers learned they couldn't permanently buy lower unemployment with higher inflation

unitName: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance
title: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
subtitle: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance
overview: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates for the Open Economy — International Trade and Finance unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: trade in goods/services + income + transfers (the 'real' economy flows)
investment flows — must balance with current account
determined by supply and demand for currencies

traps: Confusing appreciation with depreciation effects on trade — currency APPRECIATION makes exports more expensive (foreigners buy less) and imports cheaper (domestic consumers buy more) → worsens trade balance; DEPRECIATION does the opposite; AP traces this full chain; the common error is stopping at 'exchange rate changes' without connecting to how it affects the trade balance through relative prices

unitName: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance
title: Exchange Rate Policy and International Effects
subtitle: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance
overview: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Higher domestic interest rates attracting foreign capital → currency appreciates

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Fed raises rates → dollar appreciates → net exports fall → partially offsets AD expansion
tradeoffs in policy autonomy vs. stability

traps: Forgetting the exchange rate effect in monetary policy analysis — when the Fed raises interest rates, foreign investors demand dollars to invest → dollar APPRECIATES → US exports become more expensive → net exports FALL → this PARTIALLY OFFSETS the contractionary effect on domestic investment; AP free response awards a separate point for correctly tracing monetary policy through the exchange rate to net exports — most students miss this point

title: Scarcity, Opportunity Cost, and Marginal Analysis
subtitle: Basic Economic Concepts
overview: Basic Economic Concepts 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Scarcity, Opportunity Cost, and Marginal Analysis for the Basic Economic Concepts unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: decisions made at the margin, not totals — 'one more unit' thinking
already incurred, should NOT affect future decisions
choose an action when marginal benefit ≥ marginal cost

traps: Using total cost/benefit instead of marginal in optimization problems — AP micro tests MARGINAL thinking in almost every context; the optimal production level is where MC = MR (not total profit maximum); the optimal consumption is where MB = MC; sunk costs appearing in a scenario are a deliberate trap — always ask 'what changes going forward?' and ignore what's already spent

title: Supply, Demand, and Market Equilibrium
subtitle: Basic Economic Concepts
overview: Basic Economic Concepts 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Price ceiling below equilibrium → shortage; price floor above equilibrium → surplus

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: income, prices of related goods, expectations, tastes, number of buyers
input prices, technology, number of sellers, expectations

traps: Drawing the wrong direction for a supply shift caused by input price increases — higher input prices DECREASE supply (shift left) because it's more costly to produce; AP tests the direction of shifts with subtle scenarios; a useful check: if production becomes more costly or less profitable for any reason, supply decreases; if more profitable or less costly, supply increases

unitName: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
title: Elasticity — Price, Income, and Cross-Price
subtitle: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
overview: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: PED = %ΔQd / %ΔP — elastic demand (>1) means revenue falls when price rises

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: positive = normal good; negative = inferior good
positive = substitutes; negative = complements

traps: Calculating elasticity using absolute values without specifying direction — AP awards full credit when you correctly identify whether demand is elastic or inelastic AND connect it to total revenue; elastic demand: price ↑ → revenue ↓ (opposite direction); inelastic: price ↑ → revenue ↑ (same direction); the total revenue test is faster than calculation for multiple choice and AP expects you to use it

unitName: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
title: Consumer Surplus, Producer Surplus, and Efficiency
subtitle: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
overview: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Consumer Surplus, Producer Surplus, and Efficiency for the Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: area above price and below demand curve
area below price and above supply curve
loss of total surplus from quantity not produced at efficient level

traps: Drawing deadweight loss on the wrong side — DWL is the triangle BETWEEN the efficient quantity and the actual quantity; for a binding price ceiling (below equilibrium), the DWL triangle points right (toward higher quantities that would have been traded); for a price floor, same logic; for a tax, DWL is between the buyer price and seller price at the new quantity; incorrect DWL placement loses the graphing point

unitName: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
title: Government Interventions — Taxes, Subsidies, Price Controls
subtitle: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory
overview: Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Government Interventions — Taxes, Subsidies, Price Controls for the Supply and Demand — Consumer and Producer Theory unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: burden falls more on inelastic side (buyers or sellers)
wedge between buyer price and seller price equal to the tax amount
shifts supply right; benefits split between buyers and sellers based on elasticity

traps: Assuming tax burden falls on whoever the tax is imposed on — AP tests ECONOMIC incidence, not statutory incidence; if a tax is placed on sellers but demand is perfectly inelastic, buyers bear the full burden (price rises by full tax); tax incidence depends on relative elasticities, not who writes the check to the government; drawing the tax wedge correctly and identifying which side bears more burden is a standard AP free response task

unitName: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
title: Production and Costs in the Short Run
subtitle: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
overview: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Fixed costs (don't change with output) vs. variable costs (change with output)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: adding workers to fixed capital reduces each worker's additional output
when MP rises, MC falls; when MP falls, MC rises — they mirror each other

traps: Forgetting the inverse relationship between MP and MC — when marginal product of labor is RISING (early workers are more productive as they specialize), marginal cost is FALLING; when MP starts falling (diminishing returns), MC starts rising; the AP graph question almost always shows both curves and tests whether you understand they are mirror images through the production function

unitName: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
title: Perfect Competition — Short-Run and Long-Run Equilibrium
subtitle: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
overview: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Perfect Competition — Short-Run and Long-Run Equilibrium for the Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: perfectly competitive firm takes market price as given (horizontal demand curve)
produce where P = MR = MC
P = MC = ATC (zero economic profit, maximum efficiency)

traps: Confusing economic profit with accounting profit — AP tests ECONOMIC profit which subtracts implicit costs (opportunity cost of owner's time and capital); zero economic profit means normal profit (owner earning what they could elsewhere); a firm earning zero economic profit will STAY in the industry; only firms earning NEGATIVE economic profit (below normal return) will exit; this distinction drives long-run adjustment

unitName: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
title: Shutdown and Break-Even Decisions
subtitle: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
overview: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Shut down in short run if P < AVC (not covering variable costs)
Exit in long run if P < ATC (not covering all costs including fixed)
Firm continues operating in short run even at a loss as long as P ≥ AVC

sections.title: Shutdown and Break-Even Decisions
traps: Confusing short-run shutdown with long-run exit — in the SHORT RUN a firm should CONTINUE operating if P ≥ AVC because fixed costs are sunk; shutting down saves variable costs but loses revenue; in the LONG RUN all costs are variable, so exit if P < ATC; AP tests this distinction with 'should the firm shut down immediately or exit the industry?' — they require different cost comparisons

title: Monopoly — Market Power and Inefficiency
subtitle: Imperfect Competition
overview: Imperfect Competition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Monopolist faces downward-sloping demand — must lower price to sell more, making MR < P

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: MR = MC; then charge the price consumers will pay (from demand curve)
monopolist produces less than socially optimal quantity

traps: Drawing the monopoly profit-maximizing price on the MC curve instead of the demand curve — the monopolist produces where MR = MC (that's the QUANTITY), then charges the price from the DEMAND CURVE at that quantity (that's the PRICE); never read price from MC; this two-step process is tested in almost every AP micro free response involving monopoly; practice until it's automatic

title: Monopolistic Competition — Differentiation and Long Run
subtitle: Imperfect Competition
overview: Imperfect Competition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Product differentiation creating downward-sloping demand for each firm

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: can earn profit or loss; Long run: zero profit (like perfect competition)
tangent to ATC — excess capacity (not at minimum ATC)

traps: Forgetting to show excess capacity in monopolistic competition long-run graph — the tangency point where demand touches ATC is to the LEFT of minimum ATC; this means the firm is NOT producing at minimum average cost, creating 'excess capacity'; AP specifically tests this as the inefficiency of monopolistic competition; contrasting it with perfect competition (which produces at minimum ATC) is a standard comparison question

title: Oligopoly — Game Theory and Strategic Behavior
subtitle: Imperfect Competition
overview: Imperfect Competition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Oligopoly — Game Theory and Strategic Behavior for the Imperfect Competition unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: individually rational choices producing collectively bad outcomes
each player choosing best response given what others are doing
firms acting like a monopolist; price leadership as tacit collusion

traps: Treating game theory questions as just about the specific example — AP tests the GENERAL PRINCIPLE: in a prisoner's dilemma, the dominant strategy leads to a Nash equilibrium that is WORSE for both players than cooperation would be; applying this to pricing cartels, advertising, or arms races requires understanding that self-interest undermining collective interest is the core insight; firms will cheat on cartel agreements for the same reason prisoners defect

title: Labor Markets — MRP and Wage Determination
subtitle: Factor Markets
overview: Factor Markets 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: MRP = MP × Product price — the derived demand for labor
Firm hires labor until MRP = wage (MRC)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: single buyer of labor setting wage below competitive level

traps: Treating factor markets exactly like product markets — labor demand is DERIVED demand (derived from product demand); if product price rises, MRP rises, and the firm hires more labor at the same wage; AP tests the connection between product markets and factor markets: a tax on the firm's product reduces its MRP, shifting labor demand left; factor market analysis requires tracing through the product market first

unitName: Market Failure and the Role of Government
title: Externalities and Public Goods
subtitle: Market Failure and the Role of Government
overview: Market Failure and the Role of Government 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Externalities and Public Goods for the Market Failure and the Role of Government unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: social cost > private cost → market overproduces; Pigouvian tax corrects it
social benefit > private benefit → market underproduces; subsidy corrects it
non-excludable + non-rival → free rider problem → private market underprovides

traps: Drawing externality graphs without showing the social cost/benefit curve — AP free response requires drawing BOTH the private and social curves; for negative externality: supply (private cost) is below the true social cost curve; efficient output is where demand meets SOCIAL cost, which is LESS than market output; for positive externality: demand (private benefit) is below social benefit; draw both curves, mark the market quantity and efficient quantity, and shade the deadweight loss triangle

title: History and Perspectives of Psychology
subtitle: Scientific Foundations of Psychology
overview: Scientific Foundations of Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master History and Perspectives of Psychology for the Scientific Foundations of Psychology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: analyzing conscious experience through introspection
how mental processes help organisms adapt to environment
behavioral, cognitive, biological, psychodynamic, sociocultural, humanistic

traps: Treating psychological perspectives as competing truths where one is right — AP tests that each perspective is a LENS emphasizing different factors; a psychologist choosing a perspective is choosing what to study, not claiming the others are wrong; explaining behavior fully often requires multiple perspectives; AP multiple choice frequently gives a scenario and asks WHICH perspective best explains it

title: Research Methods — Experiments, Correlations, Statistics
subtitle: Scientific Foundations of Psychology
overview: Scientific Foundations of Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Research Methods — Experiments, Correlations, Statistics for the Scientific Foundations of Psychology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: independent variable manipulated, dependent variable measured, confounds controlled
relationship between variables — does NOT prove causation
results unlikely due to chance; effect size: how large the difference actually is

traps: Confusing correlation with causation — AP tests this distinction relentlessly; a positive correlation between ice cream sales and drowning doesn't mean ice cream causes drowning (lurking variable: summer); experimental design controls for this by random assignment; AP free response frequently asks you to identify why a study cannot demonstrate causation and how you would redesign it as a true experiment

title: Biological Bases of Behavior — The Neuron
subtitle: Scientific Foundations of Psychology
overview: Scientific Foundations of Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Biological Bases of Behavior — The Neuron for the Scientific Foundations of Psychology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: all-or-none, travels down axon to synaptic terminal
chemical messengers crossing the synapse (acetylcholine, dopamine, serotonin)
neurotransmitter reabsorbed by presynaptic neuron — SSRIs block this for serotonin

traps: Memorizing neurotransmitter lists without knowing their functions — AP tests SPECIFIC associations: dopamine → reward, Parkinson's, schizophrenia; serotonin → mood, anxiety, SSRIs; acetylcholine → memory, muscle movement, Alzheimer's; GABA → inhibition, anxiety; the free response frequently describes a symptom and asks which neurotransmitter system is involved; know the function AND the disorder associated with excess/deficit

title: The Brain — Structures and Functions
subtitle: Biological Bases of Behavior
overview: Biological Bases of Behavior 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Brain — Structures and Functions for the Biological Bases of Behavior unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: amygdala (emotion/fear), hippocampus (memory consolidation)
frontal (executive function, motor), parietal (somatosensory), temporal (auditory/language), occipital (visual)
reorganization after injury; critical periods for development

traps: Mixing up lobes and their functions — AP tests this with patient case studies; frontal lobe damage = impulse control and personality changes (Phineas Gage); temporal lobe damage = language comprehension issues (Wernicke's area); the AP question type is 'a patient shows symptom X — which brain area is most likely damaged?'; practice mapping symptoms to structures rather than memorizing the other direction

title: Genetics and Behavior — Nature vs. Nurture
subtitle: Biological Bases of Behavior
overview: Biological Bases of Behavior 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Genetics and Behavior — Nature vs. Nurture for the Biological Bases of Behavior unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: proportion of variation in a trait explained by genetic differences — applies to POPULATIONS, not individuals
identical twins raised apart showing similar traits → genetic influence
environmental factors influencing gene expression without changing DNA sequence

traps: Treating heritability as saying genetics determines individual outcomes — heritability of 80% for height doesn't mean 80% of YOUR height is genetic; it means 80% of height VARIATION in the population is explained by genes; a poor diet can prevent you from reaching genetic potential; AP tests that heritability is a population statistic, not a statement about any individual's development

title: Sensation — Thresholds and Transduction
subtitle: Sensation and Perception
overview: Sensation and Perception 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Sensation — Thresholds and Transduction for the Sensation and Perception unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: minimum stimulus detectable 50% of the time
minimum change detectable — Weber's Law: proportional to original stimulus
hits, misses, false alarms, correct rejections — sensitivity vs. response bias

traps: Confusing absolute threshold with difference threshold — ABSOLUTE: can you detect the stimulus at all? (light in a dark room); DIFFERENCE: can you detect that it CHANGED? (is this coffee sweeter?); Weber's Law applies only to the difference threshold; AP tests both with specific scenarios; signal detection theory is tested with the concept that sensitivity and criterion are SEPARATE — a surgeon and a nervous radiologist can have the same sensitivity but different false alarm rates

title: Perception — Top-Down Processing and Gestalt Principles
subtitle: Sensation and Perception
overview: Sensation and Perception 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Perception — Top-Down Processing and Gestalt Principles for the Sensation and Perception unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: prior knowledge and expectations influencing perception (reading in context)
building perception from sensory data without prior knowledge
figure-ground, proximity, similarity, continuity, closure — organizing perception

traps: Treating perception as passive recording of reality — AP tests that perception is CONSTRUCTIVE; top-down processing means your brain fills in gaps, sometimes creating errors (moon illusion, perceptual set); the key AP insight is that two people with different schemas or expectations can perceive the same stimulus differently; free response questions about perception almost always require explaining how context or expectation influenced the result

title: Classical Conditioning — Pavlov and Applications
subtitle: Learning and Cognition
overview: Learning and Cognition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: US → UR (unconditioned); CS + US → CS → CR (conditioned)
Extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalization, discrimination
Systematic desensitization using classical conditioning to treat phobias

sections.title: Classical Conditioning — Pavlov and Applications
traps: Identifying the CS when given a scenario — AP tests this with complex scenarios where you must identify which stimulus was originally neutral; the CS is the previously neutral stimulus that PREDICTS the US; in advertising, the product (originally neutral) is paired with attractive people (US for positive feelings) until the product alone (CS) causes desire (CR); always ask: what was neutral before conditioning began?

title: Operant Conditioning — Reinforcement and Punishment
subtitle: Learning and Cognition
overview: Learning and Cognition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Positive adds; negative removes; reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases behavior — 4 combinations

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: variable ratio produces highest response rate and greatest resistance to extinction
reinforcing successive approximations toward the target behavior

traps: Confusing negative reinforcement with punishment — NEGATIVE REINFORCEMENT increases behavior by removing something unpleasant (taking aspirin removes headache → you take aspirin more); PUNISHMENT decreases behavior; AP tests the 2x2 matrix: positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement, positive punishment, negative punishment; categorizing a scenario into one of these four correctly is a standard multiple choice task

title: Memory — Encoding, Storage, and Retrieval
subtitle: Learning and Cognition
overview: Learning and Cognition 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Memory — Encoding, Storage, and Retrieval for the Learning and Cognition unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: sensory → short-term/working → long-term memory
semantic (meaning) encoding most effective for long-term retention
context-dependent memory; mood-congruent memory; misinformation effect

traps: Treating forgetting as simple memory decay — AP tests MULTIPLE causes of forgetting: encoding failure (never stored properly), storage decay (trace fades), retrieval failure (can't access), interference (proactive: old info blocks new; retroactive: new info blocks old), and motivated forgetting; the misinformation effect (Loftus) is specifically tested — memory is RECONSTRUCTIVE, not like a video recording; eyewitness testimony is unreliable for this reason

title: Piaget's Cognitive Development Stages
subtitle: Developmental Psychology
overview: Developmental Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Schema, assimilation, accommodation — how children update understanding

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: object permanence; Preoperational (2-7): egocentric, no conservation
conservation, reversibility; Formal operational (12+): abstract reasoning

traps: Memorizing stages without understanding the TEST scenarios — AP gives a SPECIFIC child behavior and asks which stage; preoperational children fail conservation tasks (think a tall narrow glass has more water than a short wide one) BECAUSE they focus on one dimension (centration) and can't reverse the action mentally; knowing the stage name is not enough — you must know the specific cognitive limitation being tested

title: Social Development — Attachment and Identity
subtitle: Developmental Psychology
overview: Developmental Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Social Development — Attachment and Identity for the Developmental Psychology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: contact comfort more important than feeding for attachment
secure vs. insecure (anxious, avoidant) attachment styles
each with a psychosocial crisis (trust vs. mistrust, identity vs. role confusion)

traps: Confusing Erikson with Piaget or Kohlberg — Erikson is PSYCHOSOCIAL (emotional/social challenges across lifespan); Piaget is COGNITIVE (reasoning ability in childhood); Kohlberg is MORAL reasoning; AP presents a scenario and asks which theorist's framework best explains it; identify the domain: is it about thinking ability (Piaget), social/emotional challenge (Erikson), or moral judgment (Kohlberg)?

title: Motivation — Theories and Hunger
subtitle: Motivation, Emotion, and Personality
overview: Motivation, Emotion, and Personality 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Motivation — Theories and Hunger for the Motivation, Emotion, and Personality unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: physiological → safety → love → esteem → self-actualization
biological needs creating drives that motivate behavior to restore homeostasis
overjustification effect — rewarding intrinsically motivated behavior can reduce it

traps: Treating Maslow as a strict sequence everyone follows — AP tests the OVERJUSTIFICATION EFFECT as the most commonly tested motivation concept; if you reward a child who already loves reading (intrinsic motivation) with money, they may lose the intrinsic motivation; removing the reward leaves them less motivated than before; this counterintuitive result is AP's favorite motivation question

title: Emotion — Theories and Expression
subtitle: Motivation, Emotion, and Personality
overview: Motivation, Emotion, and Personality 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Emotion — Theories and Expression for the Motivation, Emotion, and Personality unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: physiological response first → then emotion (we are afraid because we run)
physiological and emotional response simultaneously, independently
arousal + cognitive label = emotion — same arousal can produce different emotions

traps: Confusing James-Lange with common sense — common sense says we see a bear, feel fear, then run; James-Lange reverses it: we see a bear, run, THEN feel fear (because we notice we're running); AP tests this by presenting a scenario and asking which theory it best illustrates; two-factor theory is tested with the Schachter-Singer adrenaline experiment — misattributing arousal to a situation produces stronger emotion

title: Psychological Disorders — Classification and Diagnosis
subtitle: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment
overview: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Psychological Disorders — Classification and Diagnosis for the Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: diagnostic criteria requiring impairment in functioning
GAD, phobias, panic disorder, OCD, PTSD — distinct presentations
major depressive disorder vs. bipolar I and II — episode type differences

traps: Confusing OCD with OCPD or confusing phobia with PTSD — AP tests SPECIFIC diagnostic criteria; OCD requires obsessions AND compulsions with insight that they're irrational; PTSD requires a traumatic event and includes flashbacks/avoidance; phobias are disproportionate fear of specific objects; major depression requires 5 of 9 symptoms for 2 weeks; free response often describes symptoms and asks you to identify the specific disorder with justification

title: Biomedical Treatments
subtitle: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment
overview: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Biomedical Treatments for the Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: SSRIs block serotonin reuptake; SNRIs add norepinephrine
block dopamine receptors — explaining both therapeutic effect and side effects
effective for severe depression when medication fails; how it works is unclear

traps: Explaining drug effects without connecting to neurotransmitters — AP free response requires the MECHANISM: SSRIs increase serotonin in the synapse by blocking reuptake (not by producing more serotonin); antipsychotics work by BLOCKING dopamine receptors (the dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia); always trace: drug action → neurotransmitter effect → symptom change; stopping at 'it increases serotonin' without explaining how earns partial credit

title: Psychological Therapies — CBT and Beyond
subtitle: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment
overview: Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Psychological Therapies — CBT and Beyond for the Clinical Psychology — Disorders and Treatment unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: identifying and challenging irrational thoughts; behavioral component changing reinforcement patterns
bringing unconscious conflicts to consciousness through free association and dream analysis
unconditional positive regard, empathy, genuineness — facilitating self-actualization

traps: Treating therapy types as interchangeable — AP tests MATCHING therapy to disorder: CBT is evidence-based for anxiety, depression, OCD; systematic desensitization (classical conditioning) for phobias; token economies (operant conditioning) for institutional settings; psychoanalysis for insight into unconscious patterns; free response gives a client description and asks which therapy would be most appropriate AND why based on theoretical principles

title: Social Influence — Conformity and Obedience
subtitle: Social Psychology
overview: Social Psychology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Social Influence — Conformity and Obedience for the Social Psychology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: people conform to obviously wrong group answers — normative social influence
65% administered maximum shocks — situational power over moral behavior
overestimating disposition, underestimating situation in explaining others' behavior

traps: Treating Milgram as about individual cruelty — AP tests the SITUATIONAL explanation: most people administered shocks not because they were sadistic but because of situational pressures (authority, incremental escalation, responsibility diffusion); the lesson is that ordinary people can do terrible things in the right situational context — this is the fundamental attribution error reversed; AP rewards recognizing the power of situations over dispositions

title: Constitutional Foundations — Compromises and Design
subtitle: Foundations of American Democracy
overview: Foundations of American Democracy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Constitutional Foundations — Compromises and Design for the Foundations of American Democracy unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: dividing sovereignty between national and state governments

terms.term: Separation of powers with checks and balances
terms.def: each branch limiting the others
Declaration, Constitution, Federalist 10, Federalist 51, Brutus 1

traps: Summarizing the Federalist Papers without using specific arguments — AP requires SPECIFIC arguments from specific documents: Federalist 10 argues large republic REDUCES faction influence (extended sphere argument); Federalist 51 argues ambition counteracting ambition through separated powers; Brutus 1 argues large republic makes representatives too distant and government too powerful; free response requires applying these specific arguments to modern scenarios

title: Federalism — Division and Evolution
subtitle: Foundations of American Democracy
overview: Foundations of American Democracy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Enumerated powers (Article I §8) vs. implied powers (necessary and proper clause)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: expanding federal power through implied powers and supremacy
federal grants-in-aid creating interdependence, blurring boundaries

traps: Treating federalism as a fixed division of power — AP tests that federalism is CONTESTED and EVOLVING; McCulloch expanded federal power; New Deal further expanded it; Reagan tried to reduce it; the current system (cooperative federalism) uses grants with conditions to influence state behavior without direct mandates; AP free response asks how specific events or court cases CHANGED the federal balance

title: Civil Liberties — First Amendment and Its Limits
subtitle: Foundations of American Democracy
overview: Foundations of American Democracy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Civil Liberties — First Amendment and Its Limits for the Foundations of American Democracy unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 14th Amendment applying Bill of Rights to states (Gitlow, McDonald)
speech, press, religion, assembly, petition — each with different judicial tests

terms.term: Schenck 'clear and present danger' → Brandenburg test
terms.def: imminent lawless action required for speech restriction

traps: Treating First Amendment as absolute — AP tests LIMITS: obscenity (Miller test), fighting words, imminent lawless incitement are NOT protected; prior restraint is almost never allowed (Near v. Minnesota) but national security exceptions exist; AP free response frequently presents a First Amendment scenario and asks you to apply the correct judicial test, not just state that free speech exists

title: Civil Rights — Equal Protection and Its Evolution
subtitle: Foundations of American Democracy
overview: Foundations of American Democracy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Strict scrutiny (race, national origin), intermediate scrutiny (sex), rational basis (economic)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: basis for civil rights litigation
Brown v. Board, Engel v. Vitale, Schenck, Tinker, Gideon, Miranda, Roe, McDonald, Citizens United

traps: Knowing the case holdings without knowing WHY they are required — AP specifically lists 15 required Supreme Court cases; you must know the CONSTITUTIONAL QUESTION, the HOLDING, and the REASONING; for free response, cases must be applied to new scenarios; Brown matters not just as a fact (segregation unconstitutional) but as reasoning (psychological harm + 14th Amendment equal protection); apply the reasoning, not just the outcome

title: Congress — Structure, Powers, and Lawmaking
subtitle: Interactions Among Branches of Government
overview: Interactions Among Branches of Government 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Congress — Structure, Powers, and Lawmaking for the Interactions Among Branches of Government unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: House represents population; Senate represents states — different constituencies
where most legislation lives and dies; chairs having gatekeeping power
Senate unlimited debate requiring 60 votes (cloture) to end — minority veto power

traps: Treating the filibuster as constitutional — it is a SENATE RULE, not in the Constitution; AP tests the distinction between constitutional requirements (Article I) and procedural rules (Senate standing rules); the filibuster can be changed by Senate rule change (nuclear option); AP frequently tests why Congress is 'inefficient' — the answer is procedural obstacles (filibuster, committee gatekeeping) plus electoral incentives, not constitutional design alone

title: The Presidency — Formal and Informal Powers
subtitle: Interactions Among Branches of Government
overview: Interactions Among Branches of Government 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Presidency — Formal and Informal Powers for the Interactions Among Branches of Government unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: veto, commander-in-chief, appointment, treaty, State of the Union
executive orders, signing statements, executive privilege, bully pulpit
requiring congressional notification within 48 hours — presidents have ignored it

traps: Treating executive orders as equivalent to laws — executive orders are ADMINISTRATIVE directives that can be overturned by the next president or struck down by courts; they are not laws requiring congressional passage; AP tests that presidents use executive orders precisely BECAUSE Congress won't act; the political debate about executive overreach is testable as a checks and balances question

title: The Federal Bureaucracy — Implementation and Accountability
subtitle: Interactions Among Branches of Government
overview: Interactions Among Branches of Government 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Federal Bureaucracy — Implementation and Accountability for the Interactions Among Branches of Government unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: bureaucratic agency + congressional committee + interest group forming mutually beneficial relationship
quasi-legislative (rules) and quasi-judicial (adjudication) functions
hearings, budget control, confirmation power limiting bureaucratic independence

traps: Treating the bureaucracy as simply implementing laws — AP tests DISCRETION: bureaucrats make policy choices through rule-making and enforcement priorities; the EPA choosing which industries to audit is a policy decision; the iron triangle shows that bureaucracies develop political allies that make them hard to control; AP free response asks how Congress or the President can control bureaucratic behavior — know specific oversight mechanisms

title: Federal Courts — Structure, Selection, and Judicial Review
subtitle: Interactions Among Branches of Government
overview: Interactions Among Branches of Government 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Federal Courts — Structure, Selection, and Judicial Review for the Interactions Among Branches of Government unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Marbury v. Madison establishing courts' power to strike down unconstitutional laws
presidential nomination + Senate confirmation — making courts politically contested
debate over appropriate scope of judicial power

traps: Treating judicial review as explicitly in the Constitution — it is NOT; Marshall CLAIMED this power in Marbury v. Madison; AP tests the political nature of judicial selection (presidents appointing ideologically compatible justices) and the legitimacy debate (unelected judges invalidating democratic laws); free response asks you to evaluate competing perspectives on judicial power using specific cases and arguments

title: Selective Incorporation — Applying Rights to States
subtitle: Civil Liberties and Civil Rights
overview: Civil Liberties and Civil Rights 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Selective Incorporation — Applying Rights to States for the Civil Liberties and Civil Rights unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Bill of Rights originally applied only to federal government
vehicle for incorporating rights against states
Second Amendment incorporated — states cannot ban handguns

traps: Assuming all rights are equally incorporated — NOT all Bill of Rights provisions are incorporated; the Third Amendment (quartering soldiers) has never been directly incorporated; AP tests which rights HAVE been incorporated through specific cases; the pattern is that fundamental rights get incorporated but some procedural rights (grand jury for state felonies) have not been; the free response may ask you to trace the incorporation of a specific right

title: Political Socialization and Public Opinion
subtitle: American Political Ideologies and Beliefs
overview: American Political Ideologies and Beliefs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Education, peers, media, religion as secondary socialization agents

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: party identification passed intergenerationally
sampling method determining validity (random sample vs. convenience sample)

traps: Treating public opinion as a fixed reflection of preferences — AP tests that opinion is CONSTRUCTED and MANIPULATED: question wording affects responses; polling methodology affects results; media framing shapes opinion; politicians use public opinion strategically while also responding to it; the relationship is interactive (politicians lead opinion AND follow it) rather than one-directional

title: Political Parties — Functions and Realignment
subtitle: Political Participation
overview: Political Participation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Two-party system reinforced by plurality voting (Duverger's Law) and ballot access laws

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: nomination, voter mobilization, organizing government, policy development
critical elections shifting party coalitions (1932, 1968)

traps: Treating party platforms as binding on elected officials — AP tests that the United States has WEAK parties compared to parliamentary systems; individual members vote against the party regularly; party identification is the strongest predictor of vote choice but doesn't control behavior; the difference between a party system that controls legislators (parliamentary) and one that loosely organizes them (US) is a key AP comparative government connection

title: Interest Groups and Campaign Finance
subtitle: Political Participation
overview: Political Participation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Interest Groups and Campaign Finance for the Political Participation unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Citizens United allowing unlimited independent expenditures
providing information and campaign contributions as primary influence mechanisms
iron triangles are stable; issue networks are fluid, open to more groups

traps: Treating all interest group activity as corruption — AP tests that interest groups perform LEGITIMATE democratic functions (aggregating preferences, providing information to legislators, mobilizing voters) alongside their problematic role in distorting policy toward concentrated interests; Citizens United is specifically tested: connecting spending to First Amendment (speech) and explaining why corporations can spend without disclosure limits

title: Elections and Voting Behavior
subtitle: Political Participation
overview: Political Participation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Elections and Voting Behavior for the Political Participation unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: winner-take-all in most states creating battleground state focus
name recognition, franking privilege, constituency service, fundraising
party ID strongest, then candidate image, then issues

traps: Treating voter choice as primarily about policy issues — AP tests that PARTY IDENTIFICATION is the strongest predictor of vote choice, not issue positions; most voters don't follow issues closely; candidate image (likability, leadership qualities) is second; specific issue positions matter primarily to high-information voters and swing voters; this evidence-based understanding of voting behavior requires applying political science research, not assumptions about rational voting

title: Comparative Method — Why We Compare
subtitle: Introduction to Comparative Politics
overview: Introduction to Comparative Politics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Comparative Method — Why We Compare for the Introduction to Comparative Politics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: describing what is vs. prescribing what should be
using variation across countries to test hypotheses about politics
UK, Mexico, Russia, China, Iran, Nigeria — chosen to represent variation

traps: Treating country examples as just facts to memorize — AP tests COMPARISON; every free response asks you to compare across countries; you must know WHY countries differ (historical path, institutions, culture, resources) not just that they do; the comparative method requires identifying variables: if two countries differ in outcome X and differ in feature Y, Y might explain X; think like a social scientist, not just a geography student

title: Democratic and Authoritarian Regimes
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Democratic and Authoritarian Regimes for the Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: competitive elections, civil liberties, rule of law, minority rights
concentrated power, limited pluralism, restricted civil liberties — hybrid regimes combining features
authoritarian with different control mechanisms

traps: Treating all authoritarian regimes as identical — AP tests VARIATIONS within authoritarianism: China uses single-party rule with collective leadership and ideological legitimacy; Russia uses competitive authoritarianism (elections exist but are manipulated); Iran is a theocratic republic (elected institutions exist under clerical veto); Nigeria oscillates between democratic and military rule; knowing the specific mechanism of control in each country is required for free response

title: The UK — Westminster Parliamentary System
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The UK — Westminster Parliamentary System for the Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: PM governing through parliamentary majority — no separation of powers
two-party dominance, strong party discipline
Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland gaining limited self-governance while sovereignty remains at Westminster

traps: Treating UK as a model of separation of powers — the UK has NO separation of powers in the American sense; the Prime Minister controls Parliament through the majority; this means faster policy implementation but also unchecked power; AP tests the CONTRAST with American separation of powers; the PM question 'why can the UK PM pass policy more easily than the US President' requires understanding fusion of powers, not separation

title: Mexico — Presidential System and Democratization
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Mexico — Presidential System and Democratization for the Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: corporatist control of business, labor, peasants under one party
IFE (independent electoral commission) enabling genuine competition
peaceful power transfer marking democratic consolidation

traps: Treating Mexico as a stable democracy like the UK — AP tests Mexico as a TRANSITIONAL DEMOCRACY still consolidating; drug cartel violence threatening rule of law; clientelism persisting; federalism weak due to PRI legacy; Mexico's democratization is the story of INSTITUTIONS being built (independent courts, electoral commission) against clientelist and corrupt traditions; the incomplete nature of consolidation is what AP tests

title: Russia — Competitive Authoritarianism
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Putin using legal mechanisms to eliminate competition while maintaining electoral facade
United Russia party as Putin's instrument, not an independent organization with its own agenda

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: economic elites either co-opted (Abramovich) or destroyed (Khodorkovsky)

traps: Treating Russia as simply reverting to Soviet communism — Russia is NOT communist; it has private property, market economy, and private media (censored but exists); it's a COMPETITIVE AUTHORITARIAN system where elections exist but aren't fair; Putin's power comes from oil revenues, security services, and media control, not ideology; AP tests this distinction between Soviet-style totalitarianism and Putin's authoritarian capitalism

title: China — Single-Party State
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Chinese Communist Party maintaining power through economic performance, nationalism, and repression

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: technically supreme but rubber-stamps party decisions
consolidating personal power beyond collective leadership norms — removing term limits

traps: Treating China's government structure as simply the CCP deciding everything — AP tests the INSTITUTIONS: the NPC formally passes laws, the State Council implements policy, the military reports to the party, not the government; Xi's consolidation of power is a change FROM the collective leadership model (post-Mao reform); understanding what changed under Xi requires knowing what the norm was before; AP tests both the formal structure and actual power dynamics

title: Iran — Theocratic Republic
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Iran — Theocratic Republic for the Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: elected president and parliament coexist with unelected supreme leader and guardian council
vetting candidates ensuring only approved figures compete in elections
reformists winning elections but being constrained by clerical institutions

traps: Treating Iran as simply a dictatorship — Iran has REAL electoral competition within the approved candidate pool; reformists like Khatami and Rouhani won elections and changed policy at the margins; the system is theocratic but not totalitarian; AP tests the tension between elected and unelected institutions: Guardian Council can reject reformist legislation, making elections less meaningful; this hybrid structure is what makes Iran distinctive among the six countries

title: Nigeria — Federal Multi-Party System
subtitle: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments
overview: Political Systems, Regimes, and Governments 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Federal structure with 36 states reflecting ethnic and regional diversity (Hausa-Fulani, Yoruba, Igbo)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: multiple coups creating weak civilian institutions
petroleum wealth creating corruption and conflict rather than development

traps: Treating Nigeria's problems as simply cultural or tribal — AP tests STRUCTURAL explanations: the oil curse (resource wealth reducing government accountability to citizens who don't pay taxes) explains corruption better than ethnicity; the colonial legacy of arbitrary borders creating ethnic tension explains instability; AP rewards explanations that identify institutional and structural causes rather than attributing political problems to culture or character

unitName: Political Culture, Public Opinion, and Participation
title: Political Culture and Legitimacy
subtitle: Political Culture, Public Opinion, and Participation
overview: Political Culture, Public Opinion, and Participation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Political Culture and Legitimacy for the Political Culture, Public Opinion, and Participation unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: shared values about what government should do and how it should operate
right to rule — based on tradition, charisma, or rational-legal authority (Weber)
economic performance and nationalism replacing communist ideology

traps: Treating legitimacy as simply military power — AP tests Weber's three-type distinction: traditional (UK monarchy), charismatic (revolutionary leaders), rational-legal (constitutional governments); the interesting AP question is hybrid legitimacy: China's CCP uses rational-legal (constitution, NPC) AND nationalist-charismatic (revolutionary heritage, Xi's personality cult) simultaneously; identifying legitimacy TYPE for each country is a standard free response task

title: Electoral Systems and Their Consequences
subtitle: Party and Electoral Systems
overview: Party and Electoral Systems 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Electoral Systems and Their Consequences for the Party and Electoral Systems unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: produces two-party systems, strong governments, but wastes votes
produces multi-party systems, coalition governments, minority representation
combining FPTP and PR — Mexico's mixed system after PRI-era reform

traps: Treating electoral systems as neutral vote-counting mechanisms — AP tests their POLITICAL CONSEQUENCES: FPTP systematically overrepresents large parties (UK Conservatives won 80% of seats with 44% of votes in 2019); PR creates more representative but often unstable coalition governments; AP free response asks you to evaluate which system better achieves democratic goals — you must take and defend a position with specific country evidence

unitName: Political and Economic Changes and Development
title: Economic Systems and Development
subtitle: Political and Economic Changes and Development
overview: Political and Economic Changes and Development 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Economic Systems and Development for the Political and Economic Changes and Development unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: privatization, deregulation, free trade — imposed on Mexico, Nigeria by IMF conditions
government directing market economy toward national goals
Nigeria and Iran depending on oil revenue — reducing taxation → reducing accountability

traps: Treating economic liberalism as the only path to development — AP tests China's ALTERNATIVE model: state capitalism directing investment into strategic industries produced rapid growth without democratic politics; neoliberal reforms in Mexico (NAFTA) increased inequality; the comparison challenges simple equations of markets = development = democracy; AP rewards analysis showing that development paths vary and produce different political consequences

title: Maps and Spatial Thinking
subtitle: Thinking Geographically
overview: Thinking Geographically 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Reference maps vs. thematic maps
Isoline maps
Choropleth maps

sections.title: Maps and Spatial Thinking
traps: Distinguish choropleth (shaded areas) from dot-density (individual dots) — FRQs ask you to justify which map type suits the data.

title: Geographic Data and GIS
subtitle: Thinking Geographically
overview: Thinking Geographically 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: GIS layers
Remote sensing
GPS applications

sections.title: Geographic Data and GIS
traps: GIS questions ask what you can COMBINE — overlay population, elevation, and land use; know that GPS is collection, GIS is analysis.

title: Scale and Region
subtitle: Thinking Geographically
overview: Thinking Geographically 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Formal, functional, and vernacular regions
Scale of analysis
Geographic scale effects

sections.title: Scale and Region
traps: Vernacular/perceptual regions (like 'the South') are defined by perception, not data — students confuse these with formal regions.

title: Space, Place, and Landscape
subtitle: Thinking Geographically
overview: Thinking Geographically 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Sense of place vs. space
Cultural landscape
Built environment

sections.title: Space, Place, and Landscape
traps: Cultural landscape = the visible imprint of culture on land; Sequent Occupance describes layers of successive cultures — know both terms with examples.

title: Models of Spatial Interaction
subtitle: Thinking Geographically
overview: Thinking Geographically 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gravity model
Distance decay
Space-time compression

sections.title: Models of Spatial Interaction
traps: Gravity model: interaction ∝ (Pop₁ × Pop₂) / Distance² — larger cities pull more; increasing distance reduces interaction exponentially.

title: Population Distribution and Density
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Arithmetic vs. physiological density
Ecumene
Population clusters

sections.title: Population Distribution and Density
traps: Physiological density = population / arable land — higher than arithmetic in Egypt (most land is desert); always specify which density.

title: Demographic Transition Model
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Stages 1–5
CBR, CDR, NIR
Stage 5 population decline

sections.title: Demographic Transition Model
traps: Stage 5 (sub-replacement fertility) is NOT on all versions of the DTM — know that Japan and Germany are examples; NIR < 0 in Stage 5.

title: Population Pyramids and Structure
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Age-sex pyramids
Dependency ratio
Youth vs. elderly bulges

sections.title: Population Pyramids and Structure
traps: Wide base = Stage 2/3 (high youth, high future growth); narrow base = Stage 4/5 (aging population, strain on social services).

title: Malthus, Boserup, and Population Theory
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Malthusian limits
Boserupian innovation
Neo-Malthusianism

sections.title: Malthus, Boserup, and Population Theory
traps: Malthus said population outruns food (pessimist); Boserup said necessity drives agricultural innovation (optimist) — FRQs ask you to apply both to a scenario.

title: Migration Push and Pull Factors
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Ravenstein's laws
Push-pull model
Intervening obstacles

sections.title: Migration Push and Pull Factors
traps: Intervening opportunity (better option found en route) vs. intervening obstacle (barrier that stops migration) — students mix these up constantly.

title: Types of Migration
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Voluntary vs. forced migration
Transhumance and cyclic movement
Refugees vs. IDPs

sections.title: Types of Migration
traps: Refugees cross international borders; IDPs (Internally Displaced Persons) stay within their country — this distinction matters for FRQ scoring.

title: Migration Patterns and Consequences
subtitle: Population and Migration
overview: Population and Migration 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Brain drain
Remittances
Chain migration

sections.title: Migration Patterns and Consequences
traps: Remittances can exceed foreign aid in developing nations — brain drain and remittances are two sides of the same migration coin.

title: Cultural Traits, Complexes, and Regions
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Material vs. nonmaterial culture
Culture complex
Cultural hearth

sections.title: Cultural Traits, Complexes, and Regions
traps: Cultural hearths are origin points of innovation (Mesopotamia, Nile Valley, Indus Valley) — distinguish hearth from cultural diffusion pathway.

title: Cultural Diffusion
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Relocation diffusion
Expansion diffusion (contagious, hierarchical, stimulus)
Reverse hierarchical

sections.title: Cultural Diffusion
traps: Contagious = spreads like a disease (contact); Hierarchical = jumps city-to-city; Stimulus = idea adopts but adapts (McDonald's goes local) — know all four.

title: Language Distribution
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Language families and branches
Lingua franca
Language extinction

sections.title: Language Distribution
traps: Indo-European is the largest family; within it, Romance vs. Germanic vs. Slavic branches — Swahili is an example of a lingua franca, not a family.

title: Religion and Sacred Space
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Universalizing vs. ethnic religions
Sacred spaces
Religious landscapes

sections.title: Religion and Sacred Space
traps: Universalizing religions (Christianity, Islam, Buddhism) actively seek converts; Ethnic religions (Judaism, Hinduism) are tied to place/ethnicity — this is a key MCQ distinction.

title: Ethnicity, Race, and Cultural Identity
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Ethnic enclaves
Multiculturalism vs. assimilation
Cultural identity and conflict

sections.title: Ethnicity, Race, and Cultural Identity
traps: Ethnic enclaves preserve culture (Little Italy, Chinatown) — distinguish from ghettos (forced segregation); FRQs ask you to identify which and explain why.

title: Gender and Cultural Norms
subtitle: Cultural Patterns and Processes
overview: Cultural Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gender roles across cultures
Female empowerment index
Gendered spaces

sections.title: Gender and Cultural Norms
traps: Gender inequality index and female education rates appear in development-themed FRQs — connect to DTM Stage and fertility rate.

title: Political Geography Concepts
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Nation vs. state vs. nation-state
Stateless nations
Multi-state nations

sections.title: Political Geography Concepts
traps: The Kurds are the classic stateless nation example; the Arab nation spans multiple states — don't confuse 'state' (political unit) with 'nation' (cultural group).

title: Borders and Boundaries
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Geometric vs. natural boundaries
Antecedent, subsequent, superimposed boundaries
Relic boundaries

sections.title: Borders and Boundaries
traps: Superimposed boundaries were drawn by outside powers ignoring cultural groups (Africa's colonial borders) — this is the root cause of many African conflicts.

title: Shape and Size of States
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Compact, elongated, fragmented, prorupted, perforated states
Enclave vs. exclave

sections.title: Shape and Size of States
traps: Prorupted states have a panhandle giving access to resources or sea; Perforated states completely surround another (South Africa surrounds Lesotho).

title: Centripetal and Centrifugal Forces
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: National identity as centripetal
Devolution as centrifugal
Balkanization

sections.title: Centripetal and Centrifugal Forces
traps: Centripetal forces unite (common language, national anthem); centrifugal forces divide (ethnic conflict, regional autonomy demands) — always give a specific example.

title: Supranationalism and International Organizations
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: EU integration and challenges
UN peacekeeping
Trade blocs and sovereignty

sections.title: Supranationalism and International Organizations
traps: Supranationalism = states giving up some sovereignty to a larger body; Brexit is the prime example of a state reasserting sovereignty over supranational membership.

title: Electoral Geography
subtitle: Political Patterns and Processes
overview: Political Patterns and Processes 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gerrymandering
Reapportionment vs. redistricting
Voting patterns and geography

sections.title: Electoral Geography
traps: Gerrymandering involves 'cracking' (split opponent voters) or 'packing' (concentrate opponent voters) — FRQs show district maps and ask you to identify the technique.

title: Origins and Spread of Agriculture
subtitle: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use
overview: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: First Agricultural Revolution
Hearths (Fertile Crescent, SE Asia)
Domestication of plants and animals

sections.title: Origins and Spread of Agriculture
traps: First Ag Revolution = domestication (~10,000 BCE); Second = mechanization (18th c. Britain); Third = Green Revolution (20th c.) — know all three and their geographic hearths.

title: Von Thünen's Model
subtitle: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use
overview: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Concentric rings of land use
Distance from market and intensity
Modern critiques

sections.title: Von Thünen's Model
traps: Von Thünen: intensive farming closest to market (dairy, vegetables), extensive farming farther out (grain, ranching) — the model assumes flat plain and single market.

title: Types of Agriculture
subtitle: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use
overview: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Subsistence vs. commercial
Intensive vs. extensive
Plantation and mixed crop-livestock

sections.title: Types of Agriculture
traps: Shifting cultivation (slash and burn) is subsistence and extensive; market gardening is commercial and intensive — map these terms to Von Thünen rings.

title: Green Revolution and Biotechnology
subtitle: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use
overview: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: High-yield variety seeds
GMOs and food security
Environmental critiques

sections.title: Green Revolution and Biotechnology
traps: Green Revolution increased yields but also increased reliance on fertilizers and water — FRQs ask you to weigh benefits (less hunger) vs. costs (soil degradation, debt).

title: Agriculture and the Environment
subtitle: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use
overview: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Soil degradation and desertification
Water usage in irrigation
Sustainable agriculture

sections.title: Agriculture and the Environment
traps: The Aral Sea shrinkage is the canonical example of unsustainable irrigation — rivers diverted for cotton farming caused an environmental catastrophe.

title: Origins and Growth of Cities
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Site vs. situation
Central place theory (Christaller)
Urban hierarchy

sections.title: Origins and Growth of Cities
traps: Central place theory: threshold (minimum population to support a service) vs. range (maximum distance customers travel) — larger threshold = higher order place.

title: Urban Land-Use Models
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Concentric Zone (Burgess)
Sector (Hoyt)
Multiple Nuclei (Harris & Ullman)

sections.title: Urban Land-Use Models
traps: Concentric Zone = rings from CBD; Sector = pie slices along transportation; Multiple Nuclei = several nodes — FRQs give a city diagram and ask you to identify the model.

title: Latin American, SE Asian, and Sub-Saharan City Models
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Griffin-Ford Latin American model
McGee model (SE Asia)
Sub-Saharan African city structure

sections.title: Latin American, SE Asian, and Sub-Saharan City Models
traps: Griffin-Ford: spine of commercial activity radiating from CBD with elite housing along it, shanty towns (disamenity zones) at periphery — inverse of US model.

title: Suburbanization and Sprawl
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Edge cities
Boomburbs
Urban sprawl consequences

sections.title: Suburbanization and Sprawl
traps: Edge cities (Tyson's Corner, VA) have more jobs than bedrooms — distinguish from bedroom communities (commuter suburbs with no job centers).

title: Challenges of Urban Growth
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Informal settlements/squatter cities
Urban heat island
Environmental justice

sections.title: Challenges of Urban Growth
traps: Squatter settlements (favelas, bustees, bidonvilles) lack legal title and formal services — know regional terms; FRQs ask you to propose a realistic improvement strategy.

title: Urban Renewal and Gentrification
subtitle: Cities and Urban Land-Use
overview: Cities and Urban Land-Use 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Redlining and disinvestment
Gentrification displacement
Smart growth and new urbanism

sections.title: Urban Renewal and Gentrification
traps: Gentrification raises property values, displacing lower-income residents — FRQs ask you to identify winners and losers; New Urbanism advocates walkable, mixed-use design.

title: Economic Development Models
subtitle: Industrial and Economic Development
overview: Industrial and Economic Development 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
