Temperature dependence of spontaneity

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS

traps: Students say a reaction is spontaneous if ΔH < 0 — spontaneity requires ΔG < 0, which depends on BOTH ΔH and ΔS; an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0) can be spontaneous at high T if ΔS > 0

title: How Energy Changes at Phase Boundaries
subtitle: Thermochemistry
overview: Thermochemistry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Heating curves and plateau regions
Heat of fusion vs. heat of vaporization
Why ΔHvap >> ΔHfus for most substances

sections.title: How Energy Changes at Phase Boundaries
traps: Students calculate heat during a phase change using q = mcΔT — during a phase change, TEMPERATURE IS CONSTANT; use q = m × ΔH_fusion or ΔH_vaporization; q = mcΔT applies only when temperature IS changing

title: What Controls How Fast a Reaction Goes
subtitle: Kinetics and Equilibrium
overview: Kinetics and Equilibrium 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Activation energy and transition state

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: energy and orientation requirements
lowering Ea without changing ΔH

traps: Students say a catalyst increases reaction rate by 'providing energy' — catalysts lower ACTIVATION ENERGY by providing an alternative pathway; they are not consumed and do not change the enthalpy of reaction (ΔH stays the same)

title: How to Write Rate Laws from Experiments (Not Equations)
subtitle: Kinetics and Equilibrium
overview: Kinetics and Equilibrium 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Determining order from initial rate data
Integrated rate laws for first and second order

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: rate = k[A]^m[B]^n

traps: Students write rate laws from balanced equations — rate law orders CANNOT be determined from stoichiometry; they must be determined EXPERIMENTALLY by comparing initial rate data when one concentration is varied

title: What Equilibrium Actually Means (Rates, Not Amounts)
subtitle: Kinetics and Equilibrium
overview: Kinetics and Equilibrium 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why pure solids and liquids are excluded from Keq

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: forward rate = reverse rate
products over reactants

traps: Students write Keq including solid and liquid concentrations — pure solids and pure liquids have CONSTANT concentrations (activity = 1) and are excluded from the expression; water in aqueous reactions is excluded

title: How to Predict Which Way a Reaction Will Shift
subtitle: Kinetics and Equilibrium
overview: Kinetics and Equilibrium 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Q vs. K comparison to predict shift direction
Effect of temperature on Keq value (not just shift)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: stress and response

traps: Students say adding a catalyst shifts equilibrium — a catalyst speeds up BOTH forward and reverse reactions equally; it reaches equilibrium faster but does NOT shift the equilibrium position or change Keq

title: Acid-Base Equilibrium: What pH Really Measures
subtitle: Kinetics and Equilibrium
overview: Kinetics and Equilibrium 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Ka and Kb expressions
pH = −log[H⁺], pOH, and Kw = 10⁻¹⁴

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: complete vs. partial dissociation

traps: Students set up weak acid ICE tables then forget to check if the approximation (x << [HA]₀) is valid — if x/[HA]₀ > 5%, the quadratic must be solved; blindly using the approximation when invalid gives wrong pH

title: How to Assign and Track Electron Bookkeeping (Oxidation States)
subtitle: Electrochemistry
overview: Electrochemistry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Identifying oxidation vs. reduction (OIL RIG)
Oxidizing agent vs. reducing agent — which is which

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: O = −2, H = +1, sum rules

traps: Students confuse the oxidizing agent with the species being oxidized — the OXIDIZING AGENT causes oxidation in another species but is ITSELF REDUCED; the reducing agent is oxidized; always identify both the agent and what happens to it

title: How Galvanic Cells Convert Chemistry to Electricity
subtitle: Electrochemistry
overview: Electrochemistry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: maintaining charge neutrality
anode | solution || solution | cathode

traps: Students reverse anode and cathode in galvanic cells — in galvanic (voltaic) cells, ANODE is negative and CATHODE is positive (opposite of electrolytic cells); mnemonic: Red Cat / An Ox (reduction at cathode, oxidation at anode)

title: How to Calculate Cell Voltage and Spontaneity
subtitle: Electrochemistry
overview: Electrochemistry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Standard reduction potentials (E°red)
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode
Relationship between E°cell, ΔG°, and Keq

sections.title: How to Calculate Cell Voltage and Spontaneity
traps: Students multiply E° values by stoichiometric coefficients — standard reduction potentials are INTENSIVE properties (they don't scale with moles); only ΔG° and Keq scale; E°cell stays the same regardless of how many electrons are transferred

title: How Electrolytic Cells Force Non-Spontaneous Reactions
subtitle: Electrochemistry
overview: Electrochemistry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Electrolysis vs. galvanic cells

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: moles of electrons and product mass
electroplating and water electrolysis

traps: Students forget to convert coulombs to moles of electrons in Faraday's law problems — moles of e⁻ = charge(C) / 96,485 (C/mol); then use stoichiometry of the half-reaction; skipping the conversion to moles is the most common error

title: The Difference Between How Fast and How Much (Speed vs. Velocity)
subtitle: Kinematics
overview: Kinematics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Scalar vs. vector quantities
Distance vs. displacement
Average vs. instantaneous velocity

sections.title: The Difference Between How Fast and How Much (Speed vs. Velocity)
traps: Students calculate average speed as (v₁ + v₂)/2 — this only works if acceleration is constant; average velocity = total displacement / total time, which is always correct; these give different answers for non-uniform motion

title: What Constant Acceleration Really Looks Like
subtitle: Kinematics
overview: Kinematics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What Constant Acceleration Really Looks Like for the Kinematics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: v = v₀ + at, x = v₀t + ½at², v² = v₀² + 2ax
slope of x-t is v, slope of v-t is a
a = −9.8 m/s² always downward

traps: Students use g = +9.8 m/s² and then wonder why answers are wrong — pick a consistent positive direction; if upward is positive, acceleration due to gravity is −9.8 m/s²; sign errors on g cause wrong answers on every free-fall problem

title: Why Horizontal and Vertical Motion Are Independent
subtitle: Kinematics
overview: Kinematics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Range, max height, and time of flight equations

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ax = 0, ay = −g
45° maximizes range on level ground

traps: Students think a horizontally launched projectile falls slower because it moves forward — horizontal velocity has NO effect on vertical fall; both a dropped ball and a horizontally thrown ball hit the ground at the same time from the same height

title: How to Add Vectors That Aren't in a Straight Line
subtitle: Kinematics
overview: Kinematics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Adding vectors by components
Resultant magnitude and direction

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Ax = A cos θ, Ay = A sin θ

traps: Students use the angle measured from the wrong reference axis — always specify the angle as measured from the x-axis (or explicitly state from which axis); θ in Ax = A cos θ is measured from the POSITIVE x-axis, not the vertical

title: Why Objects Don't Naturally Stop Moving
subtitle: Dynamics
overview: Dynamics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Identifying inertial vs. non-inertial frames
Friction as an external force, not a natural tendency

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: inertia and reference frames

traps: Students say objects slow down because 'they run out of force' — Newton's 1st Law says objects in motion STAY in motion unless acted on by a net external force; friction is the external force causing deceleration, not nature

title: How Force, Mass, and Acceleration Are Exactly Connected
subtitle: Dynamics
overview: Dynamics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Normal force and tension as constraint forces

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Fnet = ma
all forces on ONE object

traps: Students draw forces on multiple objects in one free body diagram — FBDs must show forces on ONE object only; the normal force on a block on a ramp is perpendicular to the ramp surface, NOT straight up

title: Why Action-Reaction Pairs Never Cancel Each Other
subtitle: Dynamics
overview: Dynamics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why Newton's 3rd law pairs act on DIFFERENT objects
Identifying correct action-reaction pairs

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: equal and opposite force pairs

traps: Students say the book on a table is in equilibrium because 'gravity equals normal force — they're action-reaction pairs' — the normal force and gravity are NOT a Newton's 3rd law pair (they act on the same object); the N3 pair of gravity on book is gravity on Earth from book

title: How Friction Works — and When to Use Which Equation
subtitle: Dynamics
overview: Dynamics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why μs > μk
Friction on inclined planes

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fs ≤ μsN, fk = μkN

traps: Students apply kinetic friction to a stationary object — use STATIC friction (up to maximum fs = μsN) when the object is not moving; kinetic friction applies only WHILE sliding; the maximum static friction is GREATER than kinetic

title: Why Objects Moving in Circles Must Have Inward Force
subtitle: Dynamics
overview: Dynamics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Centripetal force as net inward force (not a new force)
Why 'centrifugal force' is not real in inertial frames

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ac = v²/r toward center

traps: Students add centrifugal force to their free body diagrams — centrifugal force does NOT exist in inertial frames; centripetal force is the NET result of REAL forces (tension, gravity, normal) pointing inward; never draw it as a separate force

title: Why Work Is Not the Same as Effort
subtitle: Energy and Momentum
overview: Energy and Momentum 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Why Work Is Not the Same as Effort for the Energy and Momentum unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: W = Fd cos θ
perpendicular force, no displacement
Wnet = ΔKE

traps: Students say gravity does no work on a pendulum — gravity does positive work on the downswing (force and displacement both downward) and negative work on the upswing; only centripetal force does ZERO work (always perpendicular to motion)

title: How Energy Is Stored and Released in Conservative Systems
subtitle: Energy and Momentum
overview: Energy and Momentum 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Gravitational PE = mgh, Spring PE = ½kx²
Conservation of mechanical energy (no friction)
Energy bar charts and accounting

sections.title: How Energy Is Stored and Released in Conservative Systems
traps: Students use h = 0 inconsistently in the same problem — choose a reference height and KEEP IT; if you set the lowest point as h = 0, then use that same h = 0 for both sides of the energy equation

title: Where Does Energy Go When Friction Is Present?
subtitle: Energy and Momentum
overview: Energy and Momentum 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Energy conservation with nonconservative forces

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Eth = fk × d
P = W/t = Fv

traps: Students forget that the distance in Eth = fkd is the SLIDING distance between surfaces — for a block pulled up a ramp, it's the length of the ramp, not the vertical height; these are different and using the wrong one gives wrong answers

title: Why Momentum Is Harder to Change Than Speed
subtitle: Energy and Momentum
overview: Energy and Momentum 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Conservation of momentum in collisions
Elastic vs. inelastic collisions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: FΔt = Δp

traps: Students think kinetic energy is conserved in all collisions — KE is conserved ONLY in elastic collisions; in inelastic collisions, KE is converted to internal energy (heat, deformation); momentum is ALWAYS conserved if no external forces act

title: What Actually Moves in a Wave (It's Not the Medium)
subtitle: Waves and Sound
overview: Waves and Sound 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Transverse vs. longitudinal waves
v = fλ relationship

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: amplitude, wavelength, frequency, speed

traps: Students say 'the water moves forward in a water wave' — water molecules in a transverse wave move PERPENDICULAR to wave propagation, not forward; a floating duck bobs up and down, not horizontally toward shore

title: Why Waves Interfere and What the Patterns Mean
subtitle: Waves and Sound
overview: Waves and Sound 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Path difference and phase difference

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: constructive and destructive interference
nodes and antinodes

traps: Students think destructive interference destroys energy — energy is REDISTRIBUTED, not destroyed; where destructive interference occurs, the energy reappears at other locations (nodes have zero displacement but the energy is at antinodes)

title: Why Strings and Pipes Produce Only Certain Frequencies
subtitle: Waves and Sound
overview: Waves and Sound 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Open and closed pipe harmonics
Why closed pipes only produce odd harmonics

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fn = nv/2L

traps: Students apply the string formula to closed pipes — a closed pipe (one end open, one closed) has a NODE at the closed end and ANTINODE at the open end; fundamental = v/4L (not v/2L); only odd harmonics are present

title: Why a Moving Source Changes the Pitch You Hear
subtitle: Waves and Sound
overview: Waves and Sound 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why the observer hears higher f as source approaches
Shock waves and sonic booms

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: source approaching vs. receding

traps: Students flip the Doppler formula numerator and denominator — use f' = f × (v ± v_observer)/(v ∓ v_source); upper signs when approaching (increase), lower when receding (decrease); observer motion affects numerator, source motion affects denominator

title: Why Like Charges Repel and What Controls the Force
subtitle: Electricity and Magnetism
overview: Electricity and Magnetism 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Why Like Charges Repel and What Controls the Force for the Electricity and Magnetism unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: F = kq₁q₂/r²
E = F/q (force per unit charge)
direction, density, and interpretation

traps: Students double the force when charge is doubled and distance is also doubled — Coulomb's Law has r², so doubling r DECREASES force by 4×; doubling both charge and distance gives net change of 2/4 = ½ the original force

title: Why Voltage and Energy Are Not the Same Thing
subtitle: Electricity and Magnetism
overview: Electricity and Magnetism 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Electric potential (V) vs. electric potential energy (PE = qV)
Equipotential lines and their relationship to field lines

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: W = qΔV

traps: Students say 'higher voltage means more energy' without specifying the charge — electric potential energy = qV; a proton and an electron at the same potential have equal |PE| but the proton's is positive and the electron's is negative

title: How Resistors Control Current in Circuits
subtitle: Electricity and Magnetism
overview: Electricity and Magnetism 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Series and parallel resistor combinations
Kirchhoff's voltage and current laws

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: V = IR

traps: Students add resistors in parallel using the reciprocal formula but forget to take the final reciprocal — 1/Req = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ gives you 1/Req; you must take the reciprocal of that sum to get Req; the parallel combination is ALWAYS less than the smallest individual resistor

title: How Moving Charges Create Magnetic Fields (and Vice Versa)
subtitle: Electricity and Magnetism
overview: Electricity and Magnetism 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Magnetic field from long straight wire and solenoid

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: F = qv × B (right-hand rule)
F = IL × B

traps: Students apply the right-hand rule without specifying the velocity direction of the charge — for negative charges, use the right-hand rule then REVERSE the direction; the magnetic force on an electron moving right in an upward B field points opposite to the force on a proton

title: What It Means for a Relation to Be a Function
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Vertical line test
Domain, codomain, range distinction

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: f(x) means output, not multiplication

traps: Students write the range as all real numbers by default — the range is the set of ACTUAL OUTPUT values; always determine what y-values are actually achieved, not what's theoretically possible from the formula

title: How Transformations Move and Reshape Graphs
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Transformations Move and Reshape Graphs for the Functions and Graphs unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: f(x±h) and f(x)±k
f(−x) and −f(x)
af(x) and f(bx)

traps: Students shift horizontally in the wrong direction — f(x − 3) shifts RIGHT 3 (not left); the sign inside the function is OPPOSITE to the direction of shift because you're replacing x with x−3, not adding 3 to x

title: Why Inverse Functions Undo Each Other (And How to Find Them)
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Horizontal line test for invertibility

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: swapping input and output
swap x and y, solve

traps: Students confuse f⁻¹(x) with 1/f(x) — f⁻¹(x) is the INVERSE FUNCTION (swap x and y); 1/f(x) is the RECIPROCAL; these are completely different; f(x) = 2x has f⁻¹(x) = x/2 but 1/f(x) = 1/(2x)

title: How to Combine Functions and What That Means
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Domain restrictions in composed functions

sections.title: Key concepts
traps: Students evaluate f(g(x)) in the wrong order — (f∘g)(x) means apply g FIRST, then apply f to that result; they often compute g(f(x)) instead; always substitute the inner function result into the outer function

title: Even, Odd, and Neither: Reading Symmetry Algebraically
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Testing algebraically, not just visually

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: f(−x) = f(x) → y-axis symmetry
f(−x) = −f(x) → origin symmetry

traps: Students test only one x-value to determine even/odd — a function must satisfy f(−x) = f(x) for ALL x in its domain to be even; one counterexample disproves it; always simplify f(−x) fully before concluding

title: What the End Behavior of a Polynomial Tells You Before You Graph
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Functions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Leading term dominates for large |x|
Even/odd degree and positive/negative leading coefficient
Four end behavior cases

sections.title: What the End Behavior of a Polynomial Tells You Before You Graph
traps: Students determine end behavior from the first term written, not the leading term — the leading term is the HIGHEST degree term; if a polynomial is written in non-standard form, identify the highest degree term first

title: How Multiplicity of Zeros Controls Bouncing vs. Crossing
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Functions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Writing polynomial from given zeros

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: graph crosses x-axis
graph touches and bounces

traps: Students think double roots mean the graph barely crosses — a root with EVEN multiplicity means the graph TOUCHES but does not cross the x-axis; odd multiplicity means it CROSSES; multiplicity 1 = simple crossing

title: Why Rational Functions Have Holes and Asymptotes (And Which Is Which)
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Functions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Vertical asymptotes vs. holes from factored form
Horizontal asymptote rules from degree comparison
Oblique asymptotes via polynomial division

sections.title: Why Rational Functions Have Holes and Asymptotes (And Which Is Which)
traps: Students make everything a vertical asymptote — a common factor that cancels creates a HOLE (removable discontinuity), not a vertical asymptote; the vertical asymptote comes from zeros of the denominator that DON'T cancel

title: How to Divide Polynomials and Use the Remainder
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Functions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Polynomial long division
Synthetic division for (x − c) divisors

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: f(c) = remainder

traps: Students apply synthetic division to divisors like (x + 3) without changing the sign — synthetic division uses c where the divisor is (x − c); for (x + 3), c = −3, not +3; entering +3 gives completely wrong results

title: Finding All Zeros: The Full Rational Root Strategy
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Functions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Using synthetic division to test and deflate
Complex conjugate pairs and irreducible quadratics

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: ±p/q candidates

traps: Students stop after finding two real roots — the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra guarantees a degree-n polynomial has EXACTLY n roots (counting multiplicity) in the complex numbers; after finding real roots, check if remaining factor has complex roots

title: Why Exponential Growth Eventually Beats Every Polynomial
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Domain, range, and asymptote of exponential
Comparing linear, polynomial, and exponential growth rates

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: base and growth/decay

traps: Students confuse exponential growth rate with percent increase — if b = 1.08, the growth rate is 8% PER PERIOD; the base directly encodes the growth factor, not the percent; b = 0.92 means 8% decay (1 − 0.92 = 0.08 = 8%)

title: What a Logarithm Is Actually Asking
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: log_b(x) = y means bʸ = x
Common log (base 10) and natural log (base e)
Graph of log as inverse of exponential

sections.title: What a Logarithm Is Actually Asking
traps: Students evaluate log_2(8) by calculating 2×8 or 8/2 — a logarithm asks 'what EXPONENT on the base gives this number?'; log_2(8) = 3 because 2³ = 8; always rewrite as the equivalent exponential equation to solve

title: Logarithm Laws: Breaking Apart and Rebuilding Expressions
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Logarithm Laws: Breaking Apart and Rebuilding Expressions for the Exponential and Logarithmic Functions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: log(AB) = log A + log B
log(A/B) = log A − log B
log(Aⁿ) = n·log A

traps: Students write log(A + B) = log A + log B — there is NO log law for the log of a sum; log(AB) = log A + log B (product rule applies to multiplication, NOT addition); this is the most common logarithm error

title: Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Isolating the exponential, then taking log of both sides
Checking for extraneous solutions in log equations
Change of base formula

sections.title: Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
traps: Students accept extraneous solutions in log equations — after solving, CHECK that the argument of EVERY log in the original equation is POSITIVE; log(negative number) is undefined, so solutions that make the argument ≤ 0 must be rejected

title: Why Radians Are More Useful Than Degrees
subtitle: Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Degree-radian conversions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: arc length / radius

terms.term: Arc length and sector area formulas
terms.def: s = rθ, A = ½r²θ

traps: Students use degree measures in s = rθ — this formula REQUIRES θ in RADIANS; using degrees gives wrong answers; always convert to radians before applying arc length or sector area formulas

title: How the Unit Circle Encodes All Trig Values
subtitle: Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Reference angles and quadrant signs (ASTC)
Exact values at 0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2 and their multiples

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: (cos θ, sin θ) at angle θ

traps: Students memorize unit circle values without understanding reference angles — sin(5π/6) is not sin(5π/6) from scratch; 5π/6 is in Quadrant II with reference angle π/6; sin is positive in Q2, so sin(5π/6) = sin(π/6) = 1/2

title: How Amplitude, Period, and Phase Shift Transform Trig Graphs
subtitle: Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Period = 2π/|B|
Phase shift = −C/B (direction trap)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: identifying each parameter

traps: Students read phase shift as −C when it should be −C/B — for y = sin(2x − π), factor as sin(2(x − π/2)); phase shift is π/2 to the RIGHT, not π; always factor out B before reading the phase shift

title: Why Inverse Trig Functions Have Restricted Ranges
subtitle: Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why restrictions are necessary for invertibility
Solving trig equations on restricted vs. full domains

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: restricted ranges

traps: Students give all solutions when only the principal value is needed (or vice versa) — arcsin(x) returns ONE value in [−π/2, π/2]; when solving sin θ = 0.5 on [0, 2π], there are TWO solutions (π/6 and 5π/6); read the problem carefully for the domain

title: Proving and Applying Trig Identities
subtitle: Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Sum and difference formulas

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: sin²+cos²=1 and derived forms
sin 2θ, cos 2θ

traps: Students 'prove' identities by cross-multiplying both sides — proofs must be one-directional; transform ONE side only until it equals the other; never operate on both sides simultaneously as if it's an equation to solve

title: What Makes a Sequence Arithmetic or Geometric
subtitle: Sequences and Series
overview: Sequences and Series 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Identifying from ratios vs. differences

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: aₙ = a₁ + (n−1)d
aₙ = a₁ · rⁿ⁻¹

traps: Students apply arithmetic formula to geometric sequences — check: constant DIFFERENCE → arithmetic; constant RATIO → geometric; if successive terms multiply by the same factor, the sequence is geometric even if the terms grow rapidly

title: How to Sum a Finite Arithmetic or Geometric Series
subtitle: Sequences and Series
overview: Sequences and Series 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How to Sum a Finite Arithmetic or Geometric Series for the Sequences and Series unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Sₙ = n(a₁+aₙ)/2
Sₙ = a₁(1−rⁿ)/(1−r)
finding n, a₁, aₙ or r

traps: Students confuse n (number of terms) with aₙ (the nth term value) — n is the COUNT of terms; if terms run from a₁ to a₁₀₀, n = 100; to find n when terms are listed as values, use the nth term formula first

title: When an Infinite Geometric Series Has a Finite Sum
subtitle: Sequences and Series
overview: Sequences and Series 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why |r| ≥ 1 diverges

sections.title: Key concepts
traps: Students apply S∞ = a₁/(1−r) when |r| > 1 — this formula is only valid when |r| < 1 (series CONVERGES); for |r| ≥ 1, the series diverges (sum grows without bound); always check |r| before applying the formula

title: What Makes an Argument Persuasive vs. Just Assertive
subtitle: Rhetoric and Argumentation
overview: Rhetoric and Argumentation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Claim, evidence, warrant (Toulmin model)
Thesis that takes a genuine position
Why assertions without support are not arguments

sections.title: What Makes an Argument Persuasive vs. Just Assertive
traps: Students write thesis statements that announce a topic rather than take a position — 'This essay will discuss climate change' is not a thesis; a thesis must be ARGUABLE ('Climate change policy fails because...'); evaluate every thesis: can a reasonable person disagree?

title: How Logos, Ethos, and Pathos Work Together (Not in Isolation)
subtitle: Rhetoric and Argumentation
overview: Rhetoric and Argumentation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Logos, Ethos, and Pathos Work Together (Not in Isolation) for the Rhetoric and Argumentation unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: credibility through expertise, fairness, tone
logical structure and quality of evidence
emotional connection to audience values

traps: Students identify appeals as though they're separate — skilled arguments blend all three simultaneously; a statistic (logos) from a respected expert (ethos) that illustrates human suffering (pathos) does all three at once; label the dominant appeal but acknowledge blending

title: Why Counterarguments Make Your Argument Stronger
subtitle: Rhetoric and Argumentation
overview: Rhetoric and Argumentation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Concession-refutation structure
Steelmanning vs. straw man fallacy
Where to place counterargument for maximum effect

sections.title: Why Counterarguments Make Your Argument Stronger
traps: Students treat counterargument as admitting weakness — a well-handled counterargument INCREASES credibility (ethos) by showing the writer has considered other views; the key is to refute or qualify it, not just acknowledge it and move on

title: Recognizing Logical Fallacies Before They Undermine Your Argument
subtitle: Rhetoric and Argumentation
overview: Rhetoric and Argumentation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Ad hominem, false dichotomy, slippery slope
Hasty generalization and anecdotal evidence
Circular reasoning and appeal to authority

sections.title: Recognizing Logical Fallacies Before They Undermine Your Argument
traps: Students identify the fallacy name but can't explain WHY it undermines the argument — the explanation requires showing what VALID form of reasoning it violates; false dichotomy fails because it ignores the possibility of multiple solutions beyond the two presented

title: Using Evidence Without Letting It Replace Your Voice
subtitle: Rhetoric and Argumentation
overview: Rhetoric and Argumentation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Paraphrase vs. summary vs. direct quote
Commentary as the writer's own analytical voice

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: framing, embedding, explaining

traps: Students drop quotes without analysis ('Quote sandwiching' without the bread) — every piece of evidence needs framing before (context) and analysis after (what it means for your argument); the analysis must advance your claim, not just re-describe the quote

title: What Theme Is (and Why It's Not Just a Topic)
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Theme as a complete statement about human experience
How multiple elements work together to build theme
Distinguishing theme from moral or lesson

sections.title: What Theme Is (and Why It's Not Just a Topic)
traps: Students write theme as a single word ('loyalty') instead of a thematic statement — 'loyalty' is a topic; 'True loyalty sometimes requires betraying what others expect of you' is a theme; it must make a CLAIM about life

title: How Authors Use Structure to Control Meaning
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Linear vs. non-linear narrative
In medias res, flashback, foreshadowing
How structure mirrors or ironizes content

sections.title: How Authors Use Structure to Control Meaning
traps: Students describe structure without explaining its effect — saying 'the story uses flashback' earns no credit; you must explain WHAT the flashback reveals and HOW it changes the reader's understanding of the present-tense events

title: How to Analyze a Character Beyond 'Describe Their Personality'
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Dynamic vs. static and round vs. flat characterization
Foil characters and what contrast reveals
Motivation, internal conflict, and character arc

sections.title: How to Analyze a Character Beyond 'Describe Their Personality'
traps: Students confuse dynamic and round characters — a character can be ROUND (complex, many dimensions) but STATIC (doesn't change); a DYNAMIC character changes; these are independent axes; a flat character can be dynamic if they shift from one simple trait to another

title: Why Point of View Is One of the Most Powerful Authorial Choices
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: First person limitations vs. intimacy
Third person limited vs. omniscient tradeoffs
Unreliable narrator and dramatic irony

sections.title: Why Point of View Is One of the Most Powerful Authorial Choices
traps: Students say 'first person is more relatable' without analyzing limitations — the key analytical move is explaining what the CHOSEN POV RESTRICTS as much as what it enables; first person limits information but creates intimacy; the restriction is often the point

title: How Symbolism Works Without Being Heavy-Handed
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Building symbolic meaning through repetition and context
Conventional vs. contextual symbols
How to distinguish symbolism from coincidence in texts

sections.title: How Symbolism Works Without Being Heavy-Handed
traps: Students assert a symbol without textual support — you must show how the TEXT builds the symbolic meaning through repetition, contrast, or explicit connection; 'the green light represents hope' requires tracing how Fitzgerald develops this meaning throughout, not just stating it

title: How to Write a Literary Analysis That Makes a Real Argument
subtitle: Literary Analysis
overview: Literary Analysis 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Interpretive thesis vs. summary thesis
Close reading as primary evidence
Connecting textual evidence to the larger thematic argument

sections.title: How to Write a Literary Analysis That Makes a Real Argument
traps: Students write plot summaries dressed up as analysis — every body paragraph must advance an ARGUMENT about meaning, not narrate events; the question to ask after each paragraph: 'So what? What does this prove about the author's message?'

title: How to Evaluate Sources Before You Trust Them
subtitle: Research and Writing
overview: Research and Writing 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Primary vs. secondary sources
Bias in sources and how to use biased sources well

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, Purpose

traps: Students dismiss biased sources entirely — a biased source can be used as EVIDENCE OF a perspective or to demonstrate how a group framed an issue; the key is to acknowledge the bias and use it appropriately, not pretend it doesn't exist

title: Why Your Argument Must Drive Your Research (Not the Other Way Around)
subtitle: Research and Writing
overview: Research and Writing 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Working thesis vs. finalized thesis
Research question development
Avoiding confirmation bias in source selection

sections.title: Why Your Argument Must Drive Your Research (Not the Other Way Around)
traps: Students use whatever sources support their pre-existing view — strong research requires actively seeking COUNTER-EVIDENCE and incorporating or refuting it; a paper that ignores opposing scholarship is academically weak regardless of how much support it accumulates

title: Citation: How to Attribute Sources Without Interrupting Your Voice
subtitle: Research and Writing
overview: Research and Writing 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: MLA in-text citation and works cited format
Signal phrases and attribution
Avoiding plagiarism through proper paraphrase

sections.title: Citation: How to Attribute Sources Without Interrupting Your Voice
traps: Students think paraphrasing means changing a few words — a proper paraphrase REPROCESSES the idea in your own sentence structure using your own vocabulary; just swapping synonyms while keeping the sentence structure is still considered plagiarism

title: How to Structure a Long Argument That Doesn't Lose Its Thread
subtitle: Research and Writing
overview: Research and Writing 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Organizing by line of reasoning, not by source
Topic sentences that advance the argument
Transitions that show logical relationships

sections.title: How to Structure a Long Argument That Doesn't Lose Its Thread
traps: Students organize research papers by source (one paragraph per source) — papers must be organized by ARGUMENT; sources should appear wherever they support your claim in the argument structure, not in the order you found them

title: Why Sentence Variety Is About Meaning, Not Just Sound
subtitle: Language and Style
overview: Language and Style 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Periodic vs. cumulative sentences and their effects
Short sentences for emphasis
Syntactic parallelism and its persuasive power

sections.title: Why Sentence Variety Is About Meaning, Not Just Sound
traps: Students vary sentences randomly for 'style' — sentence length and type should serve MEANING; a very short sentence after long ones creates emphasis through contrast; use it where you want the reader to pause and feel the weight of an idea

title: How Diction Shapes the Reader's Entire Experience
subtitle: Language and Style
overview: Language and Style 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Connotation vs. denotation and emotional weight
Formal vs. informal register and context
Precision of word choice in academic writing

sections.title: How Diction Shapes the Reader's Entire Experience
traps: Students use sophisticated vocabulary to 'sound smart' at the cost of clarity — diction should serve PRECISION and TONE, not display vocabulary; a simpler word used precisely is stronger than a complex word used vaguely

title: How Tone Is Created and How to Analyze It Accurately
subtitle: Language and Style
overview: Language and Style 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Tone = author's attitude toward subject or audience
Multiple simultaneous tones
How diction, syntax, and figurative language converge to create tone

sections.title: How Tone Is Created and How to Analyze It Accurately
traps: Students name a single broad tone word ('sad' or 'angry') — effective analysis uses SPECIFIC, nuanced tone words and traces which specific word choices and syntactic decisions CREATE that tone; 'melancholic' is better than 'sad'; showing HOW it's created is the actual skill

title: How Figurative Language Compresses Meaning Into a Single Image
subtitle: Language and Style
overview: Language and Style 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Extended metaphor and conceit development

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: what the comparison reveals
verbal, situational, dramatic

traps: Students identify the device but don't explain what the comparison REVEALS — 'the poet uses a metaphor comparing life to a river' is identification; the analysis must explain what the river comparison specifically says about the nature of life that a direct statement could not

title: What Slope Really Means Beyond 'Rise Over Run'
subtitle: Linear Functions
overview: Linear Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Slope as rate of change
Positive, negative, zero, and undefined slope
Interpreting slope in context (units matter)

sections.title: What Slope Really Means Beyond 'Rise Over Run'
traps: Students calculate slope as Δx/Δy instead of Δy/Δx — slope is always VERTICAL change over HORIZONTAL change (rise/run = Δy/Δx); inverting the fraction gives the slope of the perpendicular line, which is a completely different line

title: Three Forms of a Line — When to Use Which
subtitle: Linear Functions
overview: Linear Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Three Forms of a Line — When to Use Which for the Linear Functions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: y = mx + b
Ax + By = C
y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

traps: Students always convert to slope-intercept even when point-slope is faster — when given a point and a slope, point-slope form is directly applicable without solving for b; converting first wastes time and introduces arithmetic errors

title: How Parallel and Perpendicular Lines Are Related
subtitle: Linear Functions
overview: Linear Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Writing equations of parallel and perpendicular lines

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: equal slopes
slopes are negative reciprocals

traps: Students negate the slope instead of taking the negative reciprocal for perpendicular lines — perpendicular slope = −1/m; for slope 2, perpendicular slope is −1/2, not −2; students who only negate get the sign right but still have the wrong answer

title: Solving Systems by the Method That Fits the Problem
subtitle: Linear Functions
overview: Linear Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Graphing, substitution, and elimination methods
When each method is most efficient
No solution vs. infinitely many solutions

sections.title: Solving Systems by the Method That Fits the Problem
traps: Students always use substitution regardless of the equations — elimination is faster when coefficients are already equal or easily scaled; substitution requires extra algebra when both equations are in Ax + By = C form; choose method based on structure

title: How to Solve and Graph Linear Inequalities
subtitle: Linear Functions
overview: Linear Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How to Solve and Graph Linear Inequalities for the Linear Functions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: same as equations except flip sign when dividing by negative
dashed vs. solid line
feasible region

traps: Students forget to flip the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a NEGATIVE number — this is the single rule that makes inequalities different from equations; −2x > 6 gives x < −3, not x > −3; always check this when the variable has a negative coefficient

title: What the Vertex Form Actually Tells You About the Parabola
subtitle: Quadratic Functions
overview: Quadratic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: How 'a' controls width and direction of opening

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: y = a(x − h)² + k
h has sign flip

traps: Students read the vertex from y = a(x − h)² + k as (−h, k) without checking the sign — in y = (x − 3)² + 2, the vertex is (3, 2) because h = 3; in y = (x + 3)² + 2, the vertex is (−3, 2); the sign inside the parenthesis is OPPOSITE to the h-coordinate

title: How to Factor Quadratics When the Leading Coefficient Isn't 1
subtitle: Quadratic Functions
overview: Quadratic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: AC method for ax² + bx + c
Factoring by grouping
Checking factored form by expanding

sections.title: How to Factor Quadratics When the Leading Coefficient Isn't 1
traps: Students apply trial-and-error factoring to ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 1 — the AC method is systematic: multiply a × c, find factors that add to b, split the middle term, then factor by grouping; random guessing is slow and misses answers

title: The Quadratic Formula: When to Use It and How Not to Mess Up
subtitle: Quadratic Functions
overview: Quadratic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Setting quadratic = 0 before applying the formula

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: b² − 4ac and what it predicts

traps: Students forget to set the equation equal to zero before applying the formula — the quadratic formula requires the form ax² + bx + c = 0; if the equation is x² + 3x = 4, rewrite as x² + 3x − 4 = 0 first, then identify a, b, c

title: Completing the Square: The Technique Behind Everything
subtitle: Quadratic Functions
overview: Quadratic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Converting standard to vertex form
Why it works (creating a perfect square trinomial)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: isolate x² term, add (b/2)² to both sides

traps: Students forget to add (b/2)² to BOTH sides — when completing the square, the value added to one side must also be added to the other; if a ≠ 1, divide through by a first before completing the square; skipping this step breaks the equation

title: What the Discriminant Tells You Without Solving
subtitle: Quadratic Functions
overview: Quadratic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What the Discriminant Tells You Without Solving for the Quadratic Functions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: two real roots
one real (repeated) root
no real roots (complex roots)

traps: Students compute the discriminant but interpret a negative result as 'no answer' — b² − 4ac < 0 means no REAL roots; the quadratic has two COMPLEX (imaginary) conjugate roots; for Honors, these are ±i√|discriminant|/2a

title: How to Add, Subtract, and Multiply Polynomials Without Losing Terms
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Expressions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Expressions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How to Add, Subtract, and Multiply Polynomials Without Losing Terms for the Polynomial and Rational Expressions unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: matching degree and variable
FOIL and beyond
(a+b)², (a−b)², (a+b)(a−b)

traps: Students use FOIL for polynomials with more than two terms — FOIL only works for BINOMIAL × BINOMIAL; for trinomials, distribute each term of the first polynomial to every term of the second; using FOIL for (x²+x+1)(x+2) gives wrong answers

title: Why Factoring Is Just Multiplication in Reverse
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Expressions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Expressions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: GCF factoring first
Sum and difference of cubes

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b)

traps: Students skip GCF factoring and proceed to more complex methods — always factor out the GCF FIRST; 2x² − 8 = 2(x² − 4) = 2(x+2)(x−2); students who skip GCF may not recognize the difference of squares pattern underneath

title: How to Simplify Rational Expressions Without Canceling Too Much
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Expressions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Expressions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Factor completely before canceling
Domain restrictions from the original denominator
Simplifying vs. evaluating

sections.title: How to Simplify Rational Expressions Without Canceling Too Much
traps: Students cancel individual terms instead of factors — (x² + 3x) / x = x(x+3)/x = x+3; but (x + 3) / (x + 3) can ONLY be canceled as a unit; you cannot cancel part of a sum: (x+3)/(x+5) ≠ 3/5 even though students often do this

title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
subtitle: Polynomial and Rational Expressions
overview: Polynomial and Rational Expressions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Simplifying before multiplying reduces errors

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: factor all, then cancel across numerators and denominators
multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor

traps: Students forget to find the reciprocal when dividing rational expressions — division is multiplication by the RECIPROCAL of the second fraction; flip the second fraction, then multiply; taking the reciprocal of the entire expression, not just the numerator or denominator, is essential

title: How Exponential Growth and Decay Models Work in Context
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Growth (b > 1) vs. decay (0 < b < 1)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: initial value a, growth/decay factor b

terms.term: Finding b from a percent rate
terms.def: b = 1 + r or 1 − r

traps: Students write b = r (the rate) instead of b = 1 + r — for 6% annual growth, b = 1.06, not 0.06; writing y = a(0.06)ˣ gives a decay function; the base encodes the FACTOR, not the rate of change

title: What Logarithms Ask and How to Evaluate Them
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: log_b(x) = y ↔ bʸ = x
Common log (log₁₀) and natural log (ln)
Evaluating simple logarithms by asking 'what exponent?'

sections.title: What Logarithms Ask and How to Evaluate Them
traps: Students try to compute log₂(8) as 2÷8 or 2×8 — a logarithm asks 'what power of the base gives this number?'; rewrite as an exponential equation: 2? = 8 → ? = 3; this conversion is the only reliable method

title: Solving Exponential Equations Using Logarithms
subtitle: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
overview: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Taking log of both sides when bases can't be matched
Isolating the exponential before logging

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: log_b(x) = log(x)/log(b)

traps: Students log both sides before isolating the exponential — solve 3·2ˣ = 48 by dividing both sides by 3 first to get 2ˣ = 16, THEN take the log; logging too early creates log(3·2ˣ) = log(48) which requires additional log rules to separate

title: How to Describe a Data Set: Center and Spread
subtitle: Statistics and Probability
overview: Statistics and Probability 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Range, IQR, standard deviation as spread measures
Effect of outliers on mean vs. median

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: when each is appropriate

traps: Students report the mean for skewed data — mean is pulled toward outliers; for skewed distributions, the MEDIAN better represents the 'typical' value; always check the shape of the data before choosing a measure of center

title: How Probability Rules Work Together
subtitle: Statistics and Probability
overview: Statistics and Probability 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A)
Independent vs. mutually exclusive events (not the same)

sections.title: How Probability Rules Work Together
traps: Students confuse mutually exclusive and independent events — mutually exclusive events CANNOT both happen (P(A and B) = 0); independent events DON'T AFFECT each other (P(A|B) = P(A)); these are different properties and a set of events can be one without being the other

title: Counting Strategies: When to Multiply, Permute, or Combine
subtitle: Statistics and Probability
overview: Statistics and Probability 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Fundamental counting principle

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: order matters
order doesn't matter

traps: Students use permutations when order doesn't matter (or vice versa) — ask: 'Does swapping two choices create a DIFFERENT outcome?' If yes, use permutation; if no, use combination; choosing a committee of 3 from 10 = combination (same people regardless of order)

title: How Scatter Plots and Correlation Tell a Story
subtitle: Statistics and Probability
overview: Statistics and Probability 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Positive vs. negative vs. no correlation
Correlation ≠ causation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: strength and direction

traps: Students say a strong r-value means one variable CAUSES the other — correlation measures LINEAR ASSOCIATION, not causation; ice cream sales and drowning rates are correlated (both increase in summer) but neither causes the other; always ask about a lurking variable

title: Why Three Distinct Colonial Regions Developed Different Societies
subtitle: Colonial America to Revolution
overview: Colonial America to Revolution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Why Three Distinct Colonial Regions Developed Different Societies for the Colonial America to Revolution unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Puritan compact, town meetings, subsistence farming
diversity and commerce
plantation economy and indentured servitude to slavery

traps: Students describe colonies as uniformly agricultural — the key regional distinction is ECONOMIC FOUNDATION; New England developed trade and manufacturing because rocky soil limited farming; this shapes later sectional conflict in ways that are heavily tested

title: How Salutary Neglect Created the Conditions for Revolution
subtitle: Colonial America to Revolution
overview: Colonial America to Revolution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Colonial self-governance through assemblies
Why colonists felt British interference post-1763 was tyranny

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: British non-enforcement of trade laws pre-1763

traps: Students say colonists rebelled only over taxes — the deeper grievance was loss of SELF-GOVERNANCE; decades of running their own affairs meant colonists saw post-1763 enforcement as a violation of established rights, not just new taxation

title: What 'No Taxation Without Representation' Really Meant
subtitle: Colonial America to Revolution
overview: Colonial America to Revolution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Virtual vs. actual representation debate
Stamp Act, Townshend Acts, and colonial responses
Boston Massacre and Tea Party as escalation

sections.title: What 'No Taxation Without Representation' Really Meant
traps: Students say the Revolution was purely about taxes being too high — it was about the PRINCIPLE of parliamentary authority over the colonies; colonists often paid lower taxes than British citizens; the issue was legitimacy of Parliament's right to tax, not the amount

title: What the Declaration of Independence Actually Argued (It's More Than a List of Grievances)
subtitle: Colonial America to Revolution
overview: Colonial America to Revolution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Lockean natural rights foundation
Social contract theory and right to revolution

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: philosophy → evidence → conclusion

traps: Students treat the Declaration as primarily listing British abuses — the first two paragraphs establish the PHILOSOPHICAL JUSTIFICATION; the grievances come after to PROVE the contract was broken; Jefferson's logical structure is what essay questions target

title: Why the Articles of Confederation Failed on Purpose
subtitle: Colonial America to Revolution
overview: Colonial America to Revolution 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Shays' Rebellion as catalyst for Constitution

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: fear of centralized power
Land Ordinance of 1785, Northwest Ordinance of 1787

traps: Students say the Articles were just poorly designed — they were DELIBERATELY WEAK because the founders feared a powerful central government like Britain's; recognizing this intent explains why the Constitution required a political revolution in thinking, not just a technical fix

title: What the Constitution's Framework Actually Created (and What It Left Unresolved)
subtitle: Early Republic to Civil War
overview: Early Republic to Civil War 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Bill of Rights as Anti-Federalist compromise
What the Constitution deliberately left ambiguous

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: concurrent and enumerated powers

traps: Students treat ratification as the end of debate — the Constitution's AMBIGUITIES (necessary and proper clause, commerce clause) became the source of ongoing conflict; the founders' failure to resolve slavery is the most consequential omission

title: How Political Parties Emerged Despite the Founders' Wishes
subtitle: Early Republic to Civil War
overview: Early Republic to Civil War 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Elastic clause vs. strict construction debate
Washington's Farewell Address warning about factions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Hamilton vs. Jefferson

traps: Students say Hamilton and Jefferson disagreed only on economic policy — their disagreement was PHILOSOPHICAL; Hamilton believed in active government as a force for prosperity; Jefferson feared concentrated power as a threat to liberty; this tension defines US political history

title: How Manifest Destiny Was Used to Justify Expansion (and at Whose Expense)
subtitle: Early Republic to Civil War
overview: Early Republic to Civil War 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Mexican-American War and territorial acquisition

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: providential destiny and Anglo-Saxon superiority
Trail of Tears, Indian Removal Act

traps: Students treat westward expansion as unambiguously positive — Honors-level analysis requires examining WHOSE COSTS paid for whose gains; Manifest Destiny was simultaneously nation-building and ethnic cleansing; both must appear in any analytical response

title: Why Compromise Over Slavery Failed and What That Reveals
subtitle: Early Republic to Civil War
overview: Early Republic to Civil War 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Missouri Compromise, Compromise of 1850, Kansas-Nebraska Act
How each compromise pushed the crisis forward
Bleeding Kansas and the collapse of compromise

sections.title: Why Compromise Over Slavery Failed and What That Reveals
traps: Students memorize the compromises as a list — the analytical point is that EACH COMPROMISE delayed rather than resolved the fundamental contradiction; each successive compromise required greater concessions from the North, making future agreement less likely, not more

title: What the Civil War Decided — and What It Left Open
subtitle: Early Republic to Civil War
overview: Early Republic to Civil War 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: 13th Amendment's scope and limits
Competing visions of Reconstruction as indicator of unresolved questions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: preserved union, ended slavery as institution

traps: Students say the Civil War 'ended' the slavery issue — the war ended slavery as a LEGAL INSTITUTION but left unanswered questions about the status, rights, and economic position of formerly enslaved people; Reconstruction debates show how much remained contested

title: Why Reconstruction Was Both a Revolutionary Moment and a Failed Promise
subtitle: Reconstruction to Progressive Era
overview: Reconstruction to Progressive Era 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Black political participation in the South 1867–1877
Compromise of 1877 and withdrawal of federal troops

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 14th and 15th Amendments, Freedmen's Bureau

traps: Students say Reconstruction simply 'failed' — it had SIGNIFICANT achievements (Black officeholders, schools built, constitutional amendments passed); the failure was in DEFENDING those gains; the question is not whether it worked but why federal commitment collapsed

title: How Industrialization Concentrated Power and Created Opposition
subtitle: Reconstruction to Progressive Era
overview: Reconstruction to Progressive Era 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Robber barons vs. captains of industry framing
Vertical and horizontal integration (Carnegie, Rockefeller)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Knights of Labor, AFL, Pullman Strike

traps: Students describe Gilded Age business leaders as purely villainous or purely heroic — both framings are too simple; the analytical task is explaining HOW their business practices SIMULTANEOUSLY created national prosperity and concentrated power in ways that undermined democracy

title: What the Progressive Movement Actually Reformed (and Who It Excluded)
subtitle: Reconstruction to Progressive Era
overview: Reconstruction to Progressive Era 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Muckrakers and investigative journalism as political force
Trust-busting, food safety, conservation under TR

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: race, women's suffrage, immigration

traps: Students present Progressivism as broadly reformist — a critical analysis notes that most Progressive reforms were SEGREGATED or explicitly EXCLUDED Black Americans; many Progressives shared eugenic beliefs; 'progress' was defined by and for middle-class white Americans

title: How WWI and Its Aftermath Changed American Foreign Policy
subtitle: 20th Century America
overview: 20th Century America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Wilson's Fourteen Points and failed idealism
Senate rejection of League of Nations
Return to isolationism in the 1920s

sections.title: How WWI and Its Aftermath Changed American Foreign Policy

title: What Caused the Great Depression and Why the New Deal Was Controversial
subtitle: 20th Century America
overview: 20th Century America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What Caused the Great Depression and Why the New Deal Was Controversial for the 20th Century America unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: bank failures, Smoot-Hawley, credit collapse, speculation
relief, recovery, reform — 3 Rs
government overreach and debt

traps: Students say Hoover 'did nothing' during the Depression — Hoover actually tried interventions (Reconstruction Finance Corporation, tariffs) but believed they were insufficient to act further; the more accurate critique is that his interventions were INADEQUATE and ideologically constrained

title: How WWII Transformed the United States Domestically
subtitle: 20th Century America
overview: 20th Century America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: War production ending the Depression
Japanese American internment as civil liberties failure

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: democracy abroad, democracy at home

traps: Students describe the home front as uniformly patriotic — Honors analysis requires examining CONTRADICTIONS: the US fought fascist racism abroad while maintaining Jim Crow at home; the Double V campaign shows Black Americans' awareness of this hypocrisy; it sets up the civil rights movement

title: How Cold War Logic Shaped Every Domestic and Foreign Decision
subtitle: 20th Century America
overview: 20th Century America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Containment doctrine and Truman Doctrine
McCarthyism as domestic Cold War
Korea, Cuba, and Vietnam as containment in practice

sections.title: How Cold War Logic Shaped Every Domestic and Foreign Decision
traps: Students treat Cold War foreign policy decisions as responses to specific events — Cold War decisions were driven by the DOCTRINE OF CONTAINMENT which shaped interpretation of every event; policymakers saw Vietnam, Korea, and Cuba through the lens of domino theory, not just their local context

title: What the Civil Rights Movement Achieved and How It Did It
subtitle: 20th Century America
overview: 20th Century America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What the Civil Rights Movement Achieved and How It Did It for the 20th Century America unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: boycotts, sit-ins, freedom rides
Civil Rights Act 1964, VRA 1965
SNCC, CORE, SCLC, Black Power

traps: Students present the civil rights movement as monolithic — the movement had SIGNIFICANT internal disagreements about tactics, goals, and leadership; the tension between nonviolent gradualism (SCLC/MLK) and direct confrontation (SNCC) and Black Power (later) reflects genuine strategic debates

title: How the 1970s Crisis Reshaped American Politics
subtitle: Modern America
overview: Modern America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: credibility gap and War Powers Act
executive power and its limits

title: What the Reagan Revolution Actually Changed

objectives: Cold War escalation vs. détente
Cultural conservatism and the New Right coalition

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: tax cuts, deregulation, cutting social programs

traps: Students evaluate Reagan purely as partisan liberals or conservatives do — the analytical task is explaining HOW Reaganism SHIFTED the ideological center of American politics; even Democrats moved rightward in the 1990s, showing the lasting structural impact of the Reagan coalition

title: How Globalization and Technology Rewired American Society After the Cold War
subtitle: Modern America
overview: Modern America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
