Internet economy and wealth concentration
9/11 and the transformation of national security state

sections.title: How Globalization and Technology Rewired American Society After the Cold War
traps: Students treat 9/11 as a purely foreign policy story — 9/11 transformed DOMESTIC governance (Patriot Act, DHS, surveillance state); the tension between security and civil liberties that defines modern America begins here; connect to long-term debates about government power

title: What Scientists Actually Do (It's Not a Checklist)
subtitle: Scientific Method and Tools
overview: Scientific Method and Tools 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Observation vs. inference
Scientific question vs. testable hypothesis
Why science is iterative, not linear

sections.title: What Scientists Actually Do (It's Not a Checklist)
traps: Students write hypotheses as questions — a hypothesis must be a TESTABLE STATEMENT in 'if...then...' form; 'Does sunlight affect plant growth?' is a question, not a hypothesis; 'If a plant receives more sunlight, then it will grow taller' is a testable prediction

title: The Difference Between a Good Experiment and a Guess
subtitle: Scientific Method and Tools
overview: Scientific Method and Tools 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Independent variable (what you change), dependent variable (what you measure)
Control group and controlled variables
Why you can only change ONE variable at a time

sections.title: The Difference Between a Good Experiment and a Guess
traps: Students confuse the control group with the controlled variables — the CONTROL GROUP is the untreated baseline for comparison; CONTROLLED VARIABLES are factors kept constant throughout; both are required for a valid experiment

title: How Scientists Measure Things Accurately
subtitle: Scientific Method and Tools
overview: Scientific Method and Tools 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Accuracy vs. precision
Significant figures basics

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: kilo-, centi-, milli-, conversions

traps: Students use 'accurate' and 'precise' as synonyms — a dartboard analogy clarifies it: precise = clustered together (reproducible); accurate = close to the bullseye (correct); you can be precise and wrong, or accurate but inconsistent

title: How to Read Data and Tell If It Supports Your Hypothesis
subtitle: Scientific Method and Tools
overview: Scientific Method and Tools 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How to Read Data and Tell If It Supports Your Hypothesis for the Scientific Method and Tools unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: when to use which
trends and outliers
patterns in data without claiming cause

traps: Students say data 'proves' a hypothesis — science never proves; data SUPPORTS or REFUTES a hypothesis; the correct language is 'the data is consistent with' or 'the data does not support'; one experiment never gives final proof

title: What Matter Is Made Of and How We Know
subtitle: Physical Science Basics
overview: Physical Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Atoms, elements, compounds, mixtures
Physical vs. chemical properties
States of matter and particle motion

sections.title: What Matter Is Made Of and How We Know
traps: Students confuse compounds and mixtures — in a COMPOUND, elements are chemically bonded in fixed ratios (water is always H₂O); in a MIXTURE, substances are physically combined and can be separated without a chemical reaction

title: What a Chemical Reaction Is (and Isn't)
subtitle: Physical Science Basics
overview: Physical Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Conservation of mass
Physical change vs. chemical change

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: gas, precipitate, color change, heat

traps: Students say ice melting is a chemical change because 'it looks different' — a physical change alters form but NOT chemical identity; melting, dissolving, and cutting are physical; burning, rusting, and digesting are chemical; the substance identity either changes or it doesn't

title: How Forces Change Motion (Newton's Laws in Plain Language)
subtitle: Physical Science Basics
overview: Physical Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Balanced vs. unbalanced forces
Friction and gravity as everyday forces

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: F = ma concept

traps: Students say an object moving at constant speed has no forces on it — constant speed means forces are BALANCED (net force = 0), not absent; a car cruising requires engine force to balance friction; zero net force ≠ no forces

title: What Energy Is and Why It Can't Disappear
subtitle: Physical Science Basics
overview: Physical Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Kinetic vs. potential energy
Law of conservation of energy
Energy transformations in everyday systems

sections.title: What Energy Is and Why It Can't Disappear
traps: Students say energy is 'lost' in a system — energy is TRANSFORMED, not destroyed; a roller coaster converts PE to KE to heat (friction); 'lost' energy became thermal energy; asking where the energy WENT is the correct scientific framing

title: What Makes Something Alive
subtitle: Life Science Basics
overview: Life Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Cell as basic unit of life
Unicellular vs. multicellular organisms

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: MRS GREN

traps: Students say fire and cars are alive because they grow and use energy — life requires ALL characteristics (reproduction, response to environment, homeostasis, cells); fire lacks cells and cannot reproduce; applying all criteria simultaneously is essential

title: How Cells Get Energy: The Short Version
subtitle: Life Science Basics
overview: Life Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why both processes are essential to life on Earth

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: light + CO₂ + water → glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen → CO₂ + water + energy

traps: Students say only plants do photosynthesis and only animals do respiration — ALL living cells perform cellular respiration; plants do BOTH photosynthesis AND respiration; in darkness, a plant only respires and actually releases CO₂

title: How Traits Are Passed From Parents to Offspring
subtitle: Life Science Basics
overview: Life Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: DNA as hereditary molecule
Dominant and recessive alleles
Simple Punnett square predictions

sections.title: How Traits Are Passed From Parents to Offspring
traps: Students say a dominant trait is more common in a population — dominant means it's expressed when present, NOT that it's more frequent; a dominant disease allele can be rare; frequency in a population has nothing to do with dominance

title: Why Living Things Are Classified Into Groups
subtitle: Life Science Basics
overview: Life Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Binomial nomenclature (genus species)
Why shared characteristics drive classification

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: domain, kingdom, phylum...species

traps: Students write binomial nomenclature with both words capitalized — only the GENUS is capitalized; the species epithet is lowercase: Homo sapiens, not Homo Sapiens; when handwritten, both words are underlined; when typed, both are italicized

title: What the Rock Cycle Tells Us About Earth's History
subtitle: Earth Science Basics
overview: Earth Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: How each type forms and transforms
Reading rock layers (strata) as a timeline

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic

traps: Students say rocks always follow the cycle in one direction — the rock cycle has NO fixed order; igneous rock can become metamorphic directly under heat/pressure without becoming sedimentary first; arrows go multiple directions

title: How Plate Tectonics Explains Earthquakes, Volcanoes, and Mountains
subtitle: Earth Science Basics
overview: Earth Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries
Why plate boundaries are where action happens

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: seafloor spreading, fossil distribution

traps: Students say earthquakes only occur at plate boundaries — MOST earthquakes occur at boundaries, but intraplate earthquakes exist; the New Madrid Seismic Zone in the US interior is a tested example; 'most' and 'only' are different claims

title: What Weather vs. Climate Actually Means
subtitle: Earth Science Basics
overview: Earth Science Basics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Weather = short-term atmospheric conditions; climate = long-term patterns
Why 'it's cold today' doesn't disprove climate change

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: latitude, altitude, ocean currents

traps: Students use weather events as evidence for or against climate change — weather is day-to-day; climate is 30+ year patterns; a cold snap is a weather event; climate change refers to shifts in the GLOBAL AVERAGE over decades, not individual days

title: The Building Blocks: Points, Lines, and Planes Have Rules
subtitle: Foundations and Proof
overview: Foundations and Proof 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Postulates vs. theorems
Segment and angle notation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: point, line, plane

traps: Students treat a postulate and a theorem as the same thing — a POSTULATE is assumed true without proof (a starting rule); a THEOREM is proved using postulates and other theorems; the difference matters when writing proofs

title: How to Write a Two-Column Proof Without Getting Stuck
subtitle: Foundations and Proof
overview: Foundations and Proof 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Statement-reason format
Properties of equality and congruence

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: given, definition, postulate, theorem

traps: Students write 'because it looks equal' or 'obvious' as reasons — every reason must be a named DEFINITION, POSTULATE, or THEOREM; acceptable reasons are formal mathematical names; informal observations earn no credit in a proof

title: What Congruence Actually Means (Not Just 'Same Size')
subtitle: Foundations and Proof
overview: Foundations and Proof 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Congruence vs. equality (≅ vs. =)
Midpoint and angle bisector definitions

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: exact same measure

traps: Students write AB = CD when they mean AB ≅ CD — segments and angles are CONGRUENT (≅); their MEASURES are equal (=); 'AB = CD' means the lengths are equal numbers; '∠A = ∠B' should be '∠A ≅ ∠B' unless referring to degree measures

title: Why Triangles Always Add Up to 180° (and How to Use That)
subtitle: Triangles
overview: Triangles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Triangle angle sum theorem
Exterior angle theorem
Finding missing angles in multi-triangle figures

sections.title: Why Triangles Always Add Up to 180° (and How to Use That)
traps: Students apply the 180° rule to quadrilaterals — the interior angle sum is 180° only for TRIANGLES; for any polygon, sum = (n−2) × 180°; a quadrilateral sums to 360°, not 180°

title: How to Prove Two Triangles Are Congruent (All Five Shortcuts)
subtitle: Triangles
overview: Triangles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL congruence shortcuts
Why SSA and AAA do NOT guarantee congruence
CPCTC as a reason after proving congruence

sections.title: How to Prove Two Triangles Are Congruent (All Five Shortcuts)
traps: Students use SSA (Side-Side-Angle) as a congruence shortcut — SSA is NOT valid and can produce two different triangles (the ambiguous case); HL (Hypotenuse-Leg) is valid ONLY for right triangles; SSA for non-right triangles does not prove congruence

title: What's Special About Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
subtitle: Triangles
overview: Triangles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Equilateral = equiangular = 60° each

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: base angles are equal
equal angles means equal sides

traps: Students identify the 'base' of an isosceles triangle as the bottom side regardless of orientation — the BASE is the NON-EQUAL side (between the two equal sides); the figure can be rotated; always identify which two sides are equal first

title: How the Pythagorean Theorem Works and When to Use It
subtitle: Triangles
overview: Triangles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: if a²+b²=c², then it's a right triangle

traps: Students assign c to any side — c is ALWAYS the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle); assigning c to a leg and solving gives a wrong answer every time; identify the right angle first, then c is the side opposite it

title: Special Right Triangles: The Two Shortcuts Worth Memorizing
subtitle: Triangles
overview: Triangles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Recognizing when to apply each

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: legs = x, hypotenuse = x√2
short leg = x, long leg = x√3, hypotenuse = 2x

traps: Students multiply the SHORT leg by 2 to get the hypotenuse in a 30-60-90 — this is correct ONLY when the SHORT LEG is x; if given the hypotenuse or long leg, divide first to find x, then multiply; starting from the wrong side cascades into wrong answers

title: The Hierarchy of Quadrilaterals (Every Square Is a Rectangle — Not Vice Versa)
subtitle: Quadrilaterals and Polygons
overview: Quadrilaterals and Polygons 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Quadrilateral → parallelogram → rectangle/rhombus → square
Properties of each type
Trapezoid and isosceles trapezoid

sections.title: The Hierarchy of Quadrilaterals (Every Square Is a Rectangle — Not Vice Versa)
traps: Students say 'a rectangle is a square' — a square IS a rectangle (all squares have 4 right angles) but a rectangle is NOT necessarily a square (it doesn't need equal sides); the hierarchy flows one way; Venn diagram thinking prevents this error

title: What Parallelogram Properties Let You Solve Problems
subtitle: Quadrilaterals and Polygons
overview: Quadrilaterals and Polygons 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Opposite sides equal and parallel; opposite angles equal
Consecutive angles supplementary
Diagonals bisect each other

sections.title: What Parallelogram Properties Let You Solve Problems
traps: Students say diagonals of a parallelogram are equal — diagonals bisect each other in ALL parallelograms, but they are only EQUAL in a rectangle; only PERPENDICULAR in a rhombus; only BOTH in a square; don't over-apply properties

title: How to Find Interior and Exterior Angles of Any Polygon
subtitle: Quadrilaterals and Polygons
overview: Quadrilaterals and Polygons 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Interior angle sum = (n−2) × 180°
Each interior angle of regular polygon = (n−2)×180°/n
Each exterior angle of regular polygon = 360°/n

sections.title: How to Find Interior and Exterior Angles of Any Polygon
traps: Students confuse interior and exterior angle formulas — for a REGULAR polygon: each EXTERIOR angle = 360°/n (always); each INTERIOR angle = 180° − exterior angle; students frequently apply the 360°/n formula to find interior angles, getting the wrong answer

title: All the Parts of a Circle and What They're Called
subtitle: Circles
overview: Circles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Radius, diameter, chord, secant, tangent
Central angle, inscribed angle, arc
Arc measure vs. arc length

sections.title: All the Parts of a Circle and What They're Called
traps: Students confuse arc MEASURE (in degrees) and arc LENGTH (in linear units) — arc measure equals the central angle in degrees; arc length = (arc measure/360) × 2πr; these require different formulas and are frequently mixed up

title: The Inscribed Angle Theorem: Half the Central Angle
subtitle: Circles
overview: Circles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Inscribed angle = half the intercepted arc
Inscribed angle in a semicircle = 90°
Two inscribed angles intercepting the same arc are equal

sections.title: The Inscribed Angle Theorem: Half the Central Angle
traps: Students set inscribed angle equal to the arc instead of half the arc — the inscribed angle is HALF the intercepted arc; the central angle EQUALS the intercepted arc; confusing which is which produces exactly the wrong answer

title: How Tangent Lines and the Radius Are Always Related
subtitle: Circles
overview: Circles 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Tangent perpendicular to radius at point of tangency
Two tangents from external point are equal length
Tangent-chord angle = half intercepted arc

sections.title: How Tangent Lines and the Radius Are Always Related
traps: Students forget the 90° angle at the point of tangency — when a tangent meets a radius, they form a RIGHT ANGLE; this creates right triangles in problems where none seem obvious; most tangent-line problems are secretly Pythagorean theorem problems

title: How Distance and Midpoint Formulas Come From Pythagorean Theorem
subtitle: Coordinate Geometry
overview: Coordinate Geometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Applying to prove geometric properties

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: d = √[(x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²]

traps: Students average the x-coordinates but subtract the y-coordinates in midpoint (or vice versa) — midpoint takes the AVERAGE of BOTH x AND y; both coordinates use the same averaging operation; students sometimes apply the distance formula operation to midpoint

title: How to Prove a Shape Is What You Say It Is Using Coordinates
subtitle: Coordinate Geometry
overview: Coordinate Geometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Using distance and slope together

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: equal and parallel opposite sides
perpendicular adjacent sides (slopes are negative reciprocals)

traps: Students prove a rectangle by showing all four sides equal — equal sides proves a RHOMBUS, not a rectangle; to prove rectangle, show right angles using PERPENDICULAR SLOPES (negative reciprocal slopes); these two proofs are completely different

title: What the Equation of a Circle Means Geometrically
subtitle: Coordinate Geometry
overview: Coordinate Geometry 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Identifying center (h,k) and radius from equation
Completing the square to convert general form

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: (x−h)² + (y−k)² = r²

traps: Students read center from (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² as (−h, −k) — the center is (h, k) with the OPPOSITE signs of what appears in the equation; (x−3)²+(y+2)²=25 has center (3, −2), not (−3, 2); the sign flip is the same trap as vertex form of a parabola

title: How Surface Area and Volume Are Different Problems
subtitle: 3D Geometry and Volume
overview: 3D Geometry and Volume 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Surface Area and Volume Are Different Problems for the 3D Geometry and Volume unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: sum of all face areas
space inside the figure
SA in square units, V in cubic units

traps: Students use volume formula when asked for surface area (and vice versa) — SURFACE AREA measures the OUTSIDE wrapping (square units); VOLUME measures what it holds (cubic units); re-read the question to identify which is asked before selecting a formula

title: The Formula Patterns for Prisms, Cylinders, Pyramids, and Cones
subtitle: 3D Geometry and Volume
overview: 3D Geometry and Volume 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master The Formula Patterns for Prisms, Cylinders, Pyramids, and Cones for the 3D Geometry and Volume unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: V = Bh (base area × height)
V = ⅓Bh
V = (4/3)πr³, SA = 4πr²

traps: Students forget the ⅓ in pyramid and cone volume — pyramids and cones hold EXACTLY one-third the volume of the corresponding prism or cylinder with the same base and height; physically, three conical fills equal one cylinder; forgetting this gives volume 3× too large

title: How Scale Factor Changes Size, Area, and Volume
subtitle: 3D Geometry and Volume
overview: 3D Geometry and Volume 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Area scale factor: k²
Volume scale factor: k³

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: lengths multiply by k

traps: Students apply the linear scale factor to area and volume — if a figure is scaled by k, LENGTHS multiply by k, AREAS by k², VOLUMES by k³; doubling all dimensions of a box makes it 8× the volume (2³), not 2× or 4×; students consistently under-apply the exponent

title: What a Variable Actually Means (And Why x Isn't Scary)
subtitle: Foundations of Algebra
overview: Foundations of Algebra 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Variable as a placeholder for an unknown number
Evaluating expressions by substitution
Difference between an expression and an equation

sections.title: What a Variable Actually Means (And Why x Isn't Scary)
traps: Students add variables and numbers: 3x + 4 = 7x — you CANNOT combine 3x and 4 because they are unlike terms (different kinds); 3x + 4 is already fully simplified; only LIKE TERMS (same variable, same exponent) can be combined

title: The Order of Operations Is Not Optional
subtitle: Foundations of Algebra
overview: Foundations of Algebra 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Left-to-right for equal priority operations
Common mistakes with subtraction and division

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiply/Divide, Add/Subtract

traps: Students do addition before subtraction because 'A comes before S' in PEMDAS — addition and subtraction have EQUAL priority; work LEFT TO RIGHT; 10 − 3 + 2 = 9 (not 5); the same applies to multiplication and division

title: How to Combine Like Terms Without Losing Anything
subtitle: Foundations of Algebra
overview: Foundations of Algebra 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Simplifying expressions step by step

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: same variable, same exponent
a(b+c) = ab+ac

traps: Students distribute only to the first term in parentheses: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 4 — the 3 must multiply EVERY term inside: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12; forgetting to distribute to the constant is the most common distributive property error

title: How to Solve an Equation by Undoing What Was Done to x
subtitle: Linear Equations and Inequalities
overview: Linear Equations and Inequalities 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Inverse operations to isolate the variable
Two-step and multi-step equations
Checking solutions by substituting back

sections.title: How to Solve an Equation by Undoing What Was Done to x
traps: Students perform operations in PEMDAS order when solving — solving equations reverses PEMDAS; undo addition/subtraction FIRST (outermost operations), then multiplication/division (innermost); doing it in PEMDAS order locks the variable inside instead of isolating it

title: What Happens When You Solve an Equation With Variables on Both Sides
subtitle: Linear Equations and Inequalities
overview: Linear Equations and Inequalities 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Moving all variable terms to one side
Combining like terms across the equals sign
Equations with no solution or infinitely many solutions

sections.title: What Happens When You Solve an Equation With Variables on Both Sides
traps: Students get 0 = 0 or 5 = 3 and say there's no solution in both cases — 0 = 0 (always true) means INFINITELY MANY solutions (all values work); 5 = 3 (always false) means NO solution; these are opposite conclusions from similar-looking steps

title: The One Rule That Makes Inequalities Different from Equations
subtitle: Linear Equations and Inequalities
overview: Linear Equations and Inequalities 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Solving inequalities like equations — except one rule
Flip the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.term: Graphing solutions on a number line
terms.def: open vs. closed circle

traps: Students flip the inequality sign every time they touch a negative number — only flip when MULTIPLYING or DIVIDING both sides by a negative; subtracting a negative (adding) does NOT flip the sign; the sign flip rule is specifically about the operation, not the presence of negatives

title: How to Write and Solve Equations From Word Problems
subtitle: Linear Equations and Inequalities
overview: Linear Equations and Inequalities 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Defining the variable before writing an equation
Translating verbal phrases to algebraic expressions
Checking that your answer makes sense in context

sections.title: How to Write and Solve Equations From Word Problems
traps: Students define x as 'the problem' rather than a specific quantity — define x precisely: 'let x = the number of apples Sarah bought'; vague definitions lead to equations that solve for the wrong thing; the definition determines what your answer means

title: What Makes a Relationship a Function (The Rule Every Graph Must Follow)
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Vertical line test on graphs

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: each input has exactly one output
f(x) means output when input is x

traps: Students say x = 3 is a function because 'it's just a line' — a VERTICAL line fails the vertical line test and is NOT a function; every x must map to exactly one y; x = 3 maps one x-value to infinitely many y-values, violating the definition

title: How to Graph a Line from an Equation Without Making a Table
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Plotting y-intercept, then using slope to find next point

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: y = mx + b
y = k and x = h

traps: Students plot the slope as a single point instead of a ratio — slope is RISE OVER RUN, meaning 'go up rise units, then right run units'; a slope of 3/4 means up 3 RIGHT 4 from any point; treating slope as just another coordinate to plot gives a random point, not the next point on the line

title: How Domain and Range Describe What a Function Can Do
subtitle: Functions and Graphs
overview: Functions and Graphs 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Domain and Range Describe What a Function Can Do for the Functions and Graphs unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: all valid inputs (x-values)
all resulting outputs (y-values)
no division by zero, no square root of negative

traps: Students give range as all real numbers for y = x² — the RANGE of y = x² is y ≥ 0 because squaring any real number gives a non-negative result; the graph only exists at and above the x-axis; always consider what output values are actually achievable

title: How to Add, Subtract, and Multiply Polynomials
subtitle: Polynomials
overview: Polynomials 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Combining like terms (same variable, same degree)
FOIL for binomial multiplication

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: multiply each term

traps: Students add exponents when adding like terms: x² + x² = x⁴ — adding like terms ADDS the coefficients, not the exponents: x² + x² = 2x²; MULTIPLYING terms adds exponents: x² · x² = x⁴; addition and multiplication are completely different operations

title: How to Factor Out the GCF (The First Thing You Always Try)
subtitle: Polynomials
overview: Polynomials 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Finding the greatest common factor of all terms
Factoring GCF from a polynomial
Why factoring is the reverse of distributing

sections.title: How to Factor Out the GCF (The First Thing You Always Try)
traps: Students factor out a number that doesn't divide all terms evenly — the GCF must divide INTO every single term; to find it, list the factors of each coefficient and each variable, then pick the highest common value; after factoring, check by distributing back

title: How to Factor a Trinomial x² + bx + c
subtitle: Polynomials
overview: Polynomials 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Finding two numbers that multiply to c and add to b
Writing as (x + p)(x + q)

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: when both positive, both negative, or mixed

traps: Students guess factors without checking the signs systematically — for x² − 5x + 6: multiply to +6 and add to −5 means BOTH numbers must be negative (−2 × −3 = +6, −2 + −3 = −5); drawing a small table of factor pairs and their sums is faster than guessing

title: What a Parabola's Vertex and Axis of Symmetry Tell You
subtitle: Quadratics
overview: Quadratics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Opening direction from sign of a

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: minimum or maximum point
x = −b/2a

traps: Students find the axis of symmetry as −b/a instead of −b/2a — the axis of symmetry formula is x = −b/(2a), where 2a is in the denominator; forgetting the 2 gives an axis that's off by a factor of 2; write the full formula before substituting

title: How to Solve a Quadratic Equation Three Different Ways
subtitle: Quadratics
overview: Quadratics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How to Solve a Quadratic Equation Three Different Ways for the Quadratics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: set each factor = 0 (Zero Product Property)
when no bx term
always works

traps: Students apply the quadratic formula to every problem before trying to factor — factoring is faster and less error-prone when the quadratic factors nicely; use the discriminant (b²−4ac) first: if it's a perfect square, factor; if not, use the formula

title: What the Discriminant Predicts Before You Solve
subtitle: Quadratics
overview: Quadratics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What the Discriminant Predicts Before You Solve for the Quadratics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: two real solutions
one real solution
no real solutions

traps: Students compute the discriminant as b² − 4c (omitting a) — the discriminant is b² − 4AC, where ALL THREE of a, b, and c must be identified from ax² + bx + c = 0; omitting a (or using the unset equation) gives wrong discrimination results

title: How to Find What the Author Is Really Saying
subtitle: Reading Comprehension
overview: Reading Comprehension 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Main idea vs. topic
Explicit vs. implicit meaning
Distinguishing major details from minor ones

sections.title: How to Find What the Author Is Really Saying
traps: Students confuse the topic with the main idea — the TOPIC is what it's about ('dogs'); the MAIN IDEA is what the author says about it ('Dogs make better companions than cats because...'); the main idea must be a STATEMENT, not just a label

title: How Authors Use Evidence to Support Their Points
subtitle: Reading Comprehension
overview: Reading Comprehension 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Facts vs. opinions
How supporting details connect to the main idea
Evaluating whether evidence is relevant and sufficient

sections.title: How Authors Use Evidence to Support Their Points
traps: Students accept any statement as a fact if it sounds authoritative — a FACT is verifiable and can be proven true or false; an OPINION is a belief or judgment ('this is the best policy'); statements using 'should,' 'best,' 'worst,' or 'I believe' signal opinions

title: How to Infer What the Author Didn't Say Directly
subtitle: Reading Comprehension
overview: Reading Comprehension 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: What 'reading between the lines' actually means
Avoiding inferences that go beyond the text

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: using evidence + background knowledge

traps: Students make inferences that the text doesn't support — a valid inference must be SUPPORTED BY TEXTUAL EVIDENCE; it's not a guess about anything beyond what the text implies; if no evidence points to your inference, it's speculation, not inference

title: How Vocabulary Context Clues Help You Figure Out Unknown Words
subtitle: Reading Comprehension
overview: Reading Comprehension 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Vocabulary Context Clues Help You Figure Out Unknown Words for the Reading Comprehension unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: the word is explained nearby
antonym signals
lists and illustrations

traps: Students look up words in their head without checking context — the CONTEXT meaning may differ from the dictionary definition; a word like 'draft' or 'charge' has multiple meanings; always use the surrounding sentences to determine which meaning fits

title: How to Write a Thesis That Actually Takes a Position
subtitle: Writing Fundamentals
overview: Writing Fundamentals 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Thesis = one arguable claim, not a topic announcement
The difference between a topic sentence and a thesis

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: end of introduction

traps: Students write 'In this essay I will discuss...' as a thesis — this announces a topic, not an argument; a thesis must make a CLAIM that can be agreed with or disagreed with; 'Social media harms teenagers because it disrupts sleep and amplifies anxiety' is a thesis

title: What a Strong Body Paragraph Must Include
subtitle: Writing Fundamentals
overview: Writing Fundamentals 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Topic sentence that supports the thesis
Commentary explaining what the evidence proves

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: quote, example, or data

traps: Students end paragraphs after a quote — a quote needs COMMENTARY explaining what it means and how it proves the topic sentence; 'This quote shows...' followed by real explanation; ending with evidence alone leaves the reader to make the connection for you

title: Common Grammar Mistakes That Change Your Meaning
subtitle: Writing Fundamentals
overview: Writing Fundamentals 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Run-on sentences and comma splices
Subject-verb agreement with tricky subjects

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: missing subject or verb

traps: Students fix comma splices by adding a comma before 'however' — 'however' is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction; joining two independent clauses requires either a SEMICOLON before 'however' or a period; 'I tried, however I failed' is still a comma splice

title: How Transitions Connect Ideas (Not Just Fill Space)
subtitle: Writing Fundamentals
overview: Writing Fundamentals 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Transitions showing addition, contrast, cause-effect, example
Using transitions to signal logical relationships
Overused transitions to replace

sections.title: How Transitions Connect Ideas (Not Just Fill Space)
traps: Students start every paragraph with 'Also' or 'Additionally' — these only show ADDITION; use transitions that reflect the actual logical relationship: contrast (however, although), cause-effect (therefore, as a result), emphasis (indeed, above all); 'also' for every paragraph suggests no logical structure

title: How to Identify What a Story Is Really About (Theme vs. Plot)
subtitle: Literature
overview: Literature 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Plot = what happens; theme = what it means
Universal themes across different stories
How multiple elements contribute to theme

sections.title: How to Identify What a Story Is Really About (Theme vs. Plot)
traps: Students write theme as one word ('friendship') — theme is a SENTENCE that makes a claim: 'True friendship requires accepting someone's flaws, not just their strengths'; the one-word version is a topic, not a theme; always push from the topic word to a full thematic statement

title: How to Analyze a Character as More Than Just Their Traits
subtitle: Literature
overview: Literature 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: How characters are revealed through actions, speech, thoughts
Dynamic vs. static characters
How characters change in response to conflict

sections.title: How to Analyze a Character as More Than Just Their Traits
traps: Students list personality traits rather than analyzing them — describing a character as 'brave' earns no credit; analyzing HOW the author shows bravery through specific actions, what the bravery COSTS the character, and what it REVEALS about the theme is the actual analytical task

title: How Figurative Language Creates Meaning Beyond Literal Words
subtitle: Literature
overview: Literature 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Figurative Language Creates Meaning Beyond Literal Words for the Literature unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: comparison and what it reveals
giving human qualities to nonhuman things
objects that represent larger ideas

traps: Students identify the device but stop there — 'The author uses a metaphor' earns minimal credit; the analysis must explain WHAT IS BEING COMPARED and WHAT THE COMPARISON REVEALS about the character, mood, or theme; identification is just step one

title: How to Build an Argument That Actually Persuades Someone
subtitle: Argument and Research
overview: Argument and Research 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Claim supported by reasons and evidence
Acknowledging the other side
Why a counterargument makes your argument stronger

sections.title: How to Build an Argument That Actually Persuades Someone
traps: Students skip the counterargument because they think it weakens their position — addressing the opposing view and REFUTING it shows the reader you've thought carefully; ignoring it makes readers think you haven't considered it; concession + refutation builds credibility

title: How to Use Sources Without Letting Them Take Over
subtitle: Argument and Research
overview: Argument and Research 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Introducing sources with signal phrases
Quoting vs. paraphrasing
Explaining what the source proves

sections.title: How to Use Sources Without Letting Them Take Over
traps: Students drop in a quote and move on — every source needs: (1) introduction (who said it and why they're credible), (2) the quote or paraphrase, (3) explanation of what it proves for YOUR argument; skipping the explanation makes the source do all the work for you

title: How to Tell If a Source Is Trustworthy
subtitle: Argument and Research
overview: Argument and Research 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Author credentials and purpose
Publication date and relevance

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: perspective vs. misinformation

traps: Students accept any website as a source — evaluate AUTHOR expertise (does this person know the subject?), PURPOSE (is it trying to inform or sell/persuade?), and DATE (is it current enough for your topic?); a .org or .edu domain is not an automatic guarantee of accuracy

title: Why Colonists Came to America (And Who Was Already There)
subtitle: Founding America
overview: Founding America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Push-pull factors for European colonization
Native American cultures and early contact
Three main colonial regions and their differences

sections.title: Why Colonists Came to America (And Who Was Already There)
traps: Students describe colonization as if America were empty — Native American nations were DISPLACED by colonization, not simply absent; the impact on indigenous peoples (disease, land loss, warfare) must be part of any account of colonial settlement

title: Why the Colonists Decided to Break Away From Britain
subtitle: Founding America
overview: Founding America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Growing self-governance through colonial assemblies
Boston Massacre and Tea Party as turning points

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Stamp Act, Townshend Acts

traps: Students say the Revolution was only about taxes — the deeper issue was SELF-GOVERNANCE; colonists had run their own assemblies for decades and saw Parliament's new assertiveness as an attack on rights they already had; taxes were the symptom, not the root cause

title: What the Constitution Set Up and Why It Was Designed That Way
subtitle: Founding America
overview: Founding America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Three branches and separation of powers

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: each branch limiting the others
national vs. state power

traps: Students describe checks and balances as 'three equal branches' — the branches are equal in STATUS but not in every POWER; Congress overrides vetoes (2/3), the president nominates judges, Congress confirms them; each branch has specific powers OVER specific other branches

title: How the North and South Became Two Different Economies
subtitle: Building a Nation
overview: Building a Nation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Northern industrialization and wage labor
Southern plantation economy and slavery
How economic differences created political conflict

sections.title: How the North and South Became Two Different Economies
traps: Students describe slavery as 'just a Southern issue' — slavery was economically connected to the ENTIRE country; Northern textile mills depended on Southern cotton; banks in New York financed plantations; slavery's reach was national, not regional, which made abolition politically explosive

title: What Manifest Destiny Was and Who It Hurt
subtitle: Building a Nation
overview: Building a Nation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Idea that westward expansion was America's destiny
Mexican-American War and territorial expansion

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Indian Removal Act, Trail of Tears

traps: Students describe westward expansion only through the pioneers' perspective — a complete answer includes the COST paid by Native American nations and Mexicans; Manifest Destiny required taking land from people already living there; both perspectives must appear in analysis

title: Why the Civil War Was Ultimately About Slavery
subtitle: Building a Nation
overview: Building a Nation 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: States' rights debate centered on slavery specifically
Confederate Constitution explicitly protected slavery
Emancipation Proclamation's strategic purpose

sections.title: Why the Civil War Was Ultimately About Slavery
traps: Students say the Civil War was 'really about states' rights, not slavery' — the SPECIFIC right being claimed was the right to keep slavery; Confederate documents explicitly name slavery as the cause of secession; 'states' rights' is not a neutral term in this context

title: How Big Business Changed American Life After the Civil War
subtitle: Industrial America
overview: Industrial America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Railroads connecting national markets
Why monopolies worried Americans

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: vertical and horizontal integration

traps: Students describe big business as purely negative — industrialization created jobs, lowered consumer prices, and connected the nation; the problem was CONCENTRATION OF POWER without accountability; both the benefits and the dangers are required for a complete answer

title: What Immigrants and Workers Did to Shape American Society
subtitle: Industrial America
overview: Industrial America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: New immigration waves from Southern and Eastern Europe

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: hours, pay, child labor
strikes, collective bargaining, Pullman Strike

traps: Students say unions immediately improved conditions — unions faced violent opposition (Homestead Strike, Pullman Strike) and won gains slowly over decades; the government often sided with business owners; early labor movement history is a story of struggle and setback, not quick victory

title: How the Progressive Movement Tried to Fix the Problems of Industry
subtitle: Industrial America
overview: Industrial America 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Muckrakers exposing corruption and unsafe conditions
Theodore Roosevelt's trust-busting and conservation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Progressivism often excluded Black Americans

traps: Students present Progressivism as solving all industrial problems — many Progressive reforms were LIMITED to white Americans; segregation intensified during the Progressive Era (Wilson re-segregated federal buildings); 'progressive' didn't mean equal rights for all

title: How WWI and WWII Made America a World Power

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: Zimmermann Telegram, unrestricted submarine warfare
from isolation to global war after Pearl Harbor

traps: Students say the US was always willing to enter both wars — the US maintained ISOLATIONISM until specific events forced entry (Zimmermann Telegram for WWI, Pearl Harbor for WWII); Congress and the public strongly opposed involvement before these events; entry was not inevitable

title: What the Cold War Was (It Wasn't Just About Nuclear Weapons)

Space race and arms race as competition beyond military

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: stopping Soviet expansion

traps: Students say the Cold War was a military conflict between the US and USSR — it was a POLITICAL, ECONOMIC, and IDEOLOGICAL competition that rarely involved direct combat; 'hot' wars in Korea and Vietnam were proxy conflicts; the two superpowers never directly fought each other

title: How the Civil Rights Movement Changed America
subtitle: America in the World
overview: America in the World 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why legal equality and economic equality are different challenges

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: sit-ins, boycotts, freedom rides
Civil Rights Act 1964, Voting Rights Act 1965

traps: Students say the Civil Rights Act 'solved' racism — the legislation ended LEGAL discrimination but did not eliminate economic inequality or social racism; the movement's ongoing challenges (poverty, housing discrimination, police violence) show that legal rights and lived equality are different goals

title: Everything Around You Is Matter — Here's How to Describe It

objectives: Physical vs. chemical properties
Pure substance vs. mixture
Homogeneous vs. heterogeneous mixtures

sections.title: Everything Around You Is Matter — Here's How to Describe It
traps: Students classify solutions as pure substances because they look uniform — a solution is a HOMOGENEOUS MIXTURE, not a pure substance; saltwater looks uniform but can be separated by evaporation; pure substances (elements and compounds) cannot be physically separated

title: How Scientists Measure Things in Chemistry
subtitle: Matter and Measurement
overview: Matter and Measurement 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.

terms.def: mass (g), volume (mL or L), temperature (K)
what they mean and how to count them
D = m/V and its uses

traps: Students count ALL digits as significant — zeros are TRICKY: leading zeros are NOT significant (0.0045 has 2 sig figs); trailing zeros after a decimal ARE significant (2.50 has 3 sig figs); trailing zeros without a decimal are ambiguous; use scientific notation to be clear

title: How to Convert Units Without Getting Confused
subtitle: Matter and Measurement
overview: Matter and Measurement 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Dimensional analysis (factor-label method)
Setting up conversion factors
Multi-step conversions

sections.title: How to Convert Units Without Getting Confused
traps: Students multiply by conversion factors without canceling units — in dimensional analysis, write units in EVERY step and cancel them like fractions; if you can't cancel the unit you want to eliminate, the conversion factor is upside down; units that remain are your answer's units

title: What an Atom Is Made Of and Where Those Parts Are
subtitle: Atomic Structure
overview: Atomic Structure 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus; electrons in orbitals
Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: gaining or losing electrons changes charge, not identity

traps: Students say an ion is a different ELEMENT — gaining or losing electrons changes the CHARGE, not the number of protons; an atom's IDENTITY is determined by proton count (atomic number); Na⁺ is still sodium; only changing protons creates a different element

title: How the Periodic Table Organizes Every Element
subtitle: Atomic Structure
overview: Atomic Structure 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Periods (rows) and groups (columns)
Metals, nonmetals, metalloids location

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity

traps: Students say ionization energy and atomic radius increase in the same direction — they move in OPPOSITE TRENDS across a period; as you go right, atomic radius DECREASES (more protons pull electrons closer); ionization energy INCREASES (harder to remove electrons held tighter)

title: How Electrons Are Arranged and Why It Matters
subtitle: Atomic Structure
overview: Atomic Structure 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Valence electrons determine reactivity
Why noble gases are unreactive

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: filling order by energy level

traps: Students say all elements want to have 8 electrons — the octet rule applies to most main group elements, but EXCEPTIONS exist; hydrogen follows the duet rule (2 electrons); some elements like phosphorus and sulfur can expand beyond 8; hydrogen and helium are the key exceptions

title: How to Read and Write Chemical Equations
subtitle: Chemical Reactions
overview: Chemical Reactions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Reactants → products format

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: atoms balanced on both sides

traps: Students change subscripts to balance equations — NEVER change subscripts to balance; H₂O₂ ≠ H₂O; subscripts define the substance; only change COEFFICIENTS in front of formulas; changing a subscript creates an entirely different chemical

title: The Five Types of Chemical Reactions and How to Recognize Them
subtitle: Chemical Reactions
overview: Chemical Reactions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Synthesis (A+B→AB), decomposition (AB→A+B)
Single replacement, double replacement, combustion
Predicting products from reaction type

sections.title: The Five Types of Chemical Reactions and How to Recognize Them
traps: Students confuse single and double replacement — SINGLE: one element displaces another in a compound (A + BC → AC + B); DOUBLE: the cations of two compounds switch partners (AB + CD → AD + CB); identifying whether one or two elements are switching determines the type

title: How to Use Moles to Predict How Much Product You Make
subtitle: Chemical Reactions
overview: Chemical Reactions 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Molar mass from periodic table
Mole ratio from balanced equation

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: 1 mol = 6.02×10²³ particles

traps: Students convert grams directly to grams of product — stoichiometry requires going THROUGH MOLES: grams A → moles A → moles B → grams B; skipping the mole conversion and just using a mass ratio gives wrong answers except by coincidence

title: What 'Dissolving' Actually Means at the Particle Level
subtitle: Solutions and Acids/Bases
overview: Solutions and Acids/Bases 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Solute and solvent roles

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: polarity matching
molarity = moles/liter

traps: Students say 'water dissolves everything' — water only dissolves POLAR and IONIC substances ('like dissolves like'); oil doesn't dissolve in water because oil is nonpolar; this principle predicts what will dissolve before any experiment is run

title: What Acids and Bases Actually Are
subtitle: Solutions and Acids/Bases
overview: Solutions and Acids/Bases 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master What Acids and Bases Actually Are for the Solutions and Acids/Bases unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: donate H⁺; bases: accept H⁺ (Brønsted-Lowry)
0–14, neutral at 7
complete vs. partial dissociation

traps: Students say a low pH means 'a little acidic' — pH 2 is EXTREMELY acidic; each pH unit represents a 10× change in H⁺ concentration; pH 2 has 100× more H⁺ than pH 4; students confuse the magnitude of the number with the intensity of acidity

title: What Happens When an Acid and a Base Are Mixed
subtitle: Solutions and Acids/Bases
overview: Solutions and Acids/Bases 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Net ionic equations

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: acid + base → salt + water
using a known concentration to find an unknown

traps: Students say neutralization means the products are neutral — a neutralization REACTION produces a salt and water, but the resulting solution is not necessarily pH 7; strong acid + weak base → acidic salt; weak acid + strong base → basic salt; the product's pH depends on which reactant is stronger

title: Why Every Living Thing Is Made of Cells
subtitle: Cell Biology
overview: Cell Biology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Prokaryotic vs. eukaryotic cells
Why cell size has limits

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: all life made of cells

traps: Students say plant cells have all the same organelles as animal cells — plants have CELL WALLS, CHLOROPLASTS, and a LARGE CENTRAL VACUOLE that animal cells lack; animal cells have CENTRIOLES that plant cells lack; the differences are directly tied to each cell's unique functions

title: What Each Organelle Does and Why It Matters
subtitle: Cell Biology
overview: Cell Biology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Nucleus, mitochondria, ribosome functions
Chloroplasts and cell wall in plant cells

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: protein production line

traps: Students say the nucleus makes proteins — the NUCLEUS contains the DNA instructions; RIBOSOMES make proteins using those instructions; the rough ER processes proteins, the Golgi modifies and ships them; this is a multi-step assembly line, not a single organelle job

title: How Materials Get In and Out of Cells
subtitle: Cell Biology
overview: Cell Biology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How Materials Get In and Out of Cells for the Cell Biology unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: passive transport
energy required
crenation and lysis in different solutions

traps: Students say a cell placed in salt water will swell — a cell in HIGH SALT (hypertonic) solution loses water by osmosis and SHRINKS (crenation in animal cells, plasmolysis in plant cells); a cell in PURE WATER (hypotonic) gains water and swells; water moves toward MORE solute

title: How Traits Are Inherited From Parents
subtitle: Genetics
overview: Genetics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Dominant and recessive alleles
Genotype vs. phenotype
Homozygous vs. heterozygous

sections.title: How Traits Are Inherited From Parents
traps: Students say a dominant trait is 'stronger' or 'better' — dominant simply means it's expressed when present; it has NO relationship to being beneficial or common; a harmful dominant allele (like Huntington's disease) is expressed even with one copy

title: How to Predict Offspring Using a Punnett Square
subtitle: Genetics
overview: Genetics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Setting up monohybrid crosses
Reading probability from Punnett squares
Phenotype ratios vs. genotype ratios

sections.title: How to Predict Offspring Using a Punnett Square
traps: Students report Punnett square results as exact numbers instead of probabilities — a 3:1 phenotype ratio means a 75% chance of the dominant phenotype per offspring, not that exactly 3 out of 4 offspring will show it; probability applies to EACH individual offspring, not a guaranteed count

title: How DNA Carries the Instructions for Making You
subtitle: Genetics
overview: Genetics 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master How DNA Carries the Instructions for Making You for the Genetics unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: double helix, base pairing (A-T, G-C)
section of DNA coding for a protein
copying before cell division

traps: Students say A pairs with G and T pairs with C — base pairing is A-T and G-C (in DNA); A pairs with T, not G; G pairs with C, not A; this rule is called complementary base pairing and determines both DNA replication and transcription accuracy

title: What Natural Selection Actually Is (Evolution Explained Simply)
subtitle: Evolution and Classification
overview: Evolution and Classification 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Variation exists in populations
Traits that improve survival are inherited more
Natural selection acts on individuals; evolution happens to populations

sections.title: What Natural Selection Actually Is (Evolution Explained Simply)
traps: Students say 'organisms evolve to survive' — organisms don't CHOOSE to evolve; individuals with EXISTING helpful traits survive and reproduce more; the population's allele frequencies shift over generations; no intentionality is involved; 'organisms develop traits they need' is Lamarckism, which is incorrect

title: The Evidence That Evolution Happened
subtitle: Evolution and Classification
overview: Evolution and Classification 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Fossil record showing change over time
Homologous structures in related species
DNA similarity as molecular evidence

sections.title: The Evidence That Evolution Happened
traps: Students say 'evolution is just a theory' as if theory means a guess — in science, a THEORY is an explanation supported by extensive evidence and testing; scientific theories explain HOW things happen (evolution, gravity, germ theory); a hypothesis is the guess; a theory is the tested explanation

title: How Scientists Organize and Name All Living Things
subtitle: Evolution and Classification
overview: Evolution and Classification 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Binomial nomenclature rules
Phylogenetic trees and common ancestry

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: domain to species

traps: Students say species that look similar must be closely related — convergent evolution produces similar-looking organisms with NO close relationship (dolphins and fish look similar but are not closely related); classification must be based on EVOLUTIONARY HISTORY (genetics), not appearance

title: How Energy Moves Through an Ecosystem
subtitle: Ecology
overview: Ecology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Producers, consumers, decomposers roles
Food chains and food webs
10% energy transfer rule between trophic levels

sections.title: How Energy Moves Through an Ecosystem
traps: Students say 50% of energy passes between trophic levels — only about 10% of energy transfers to the next level; 90% is LOST as heat through cellular respiration; this is why food chains are short and why there are more producers than top predators in any ecosystem

title: How Populations Grow and What Controls Their Size
subtitle: Ecology
overview: Ecology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Biotic and abiotic factors
Carrying capacity and population limits
Predator-prey relationships

sections.title: How Populations Grow and What Controls Their Size
traps: Students say populations grow until 'there's no more room' — populations are limited by RESOURCES (food, water, space), PREDATION, and DISEASE, not just physical space; a meadow might have room for more rabbits but not enough food; food is usually the limiting resource before space

title: How Human Activities Change Ecosystems
subtitle: Ecology
overview: Ecology 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Habitat destruction as leading cause of species loss
Pollution and its effects on food chains
Climate change and ecosystem shifts

sections.title: How Human Activities Change Ecosystems
traps: Students list many causes of extinction as equally important — HABITAT DESTRUCTION is the SINGLE LARGEST cause of species extinction globally; pollution, invasive species, and climate change are significant but secondary; when asked to rank causes, habitat loss is the answer

title: What Speed, Velocity, and Acceleration Are (They're Not the Same)
subtitle: Motion
overview: Motion 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Calculating average speed and velocity

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: speed + direction)
change in velocity, not just speeding up

traps: Students say an object isn't accelerating if it's moving at constant speed in a curve — CHANGING DIRECTION is a change in velocity (direction changed), so it IS accelerating; a car going around a circular track at constant speed is constantly accelerating toward the center

title: How to Read Distance-Time and Speed-Time Graphs
subtitle: Motion
overview: Motion 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Slope of distance-time graph = speed
Slope of speed-time graph = acceleration
Area under speed-time graph = distance

sections.title: How to Read Distance-Time and Speed-Time Graphs
traps: Students read a horizontal line on a speed-time graph as 'stopped' — a HORIZONTAL LINE on a speed-time graph means CONSTANT SPEED (not zero speed); the object is only stopped if the line is on the x-axis (speed = 0); a flat line at v = 5 m/s means moving steadily at 5 m/s

title: How Gravity Pulls Everything Down the Same Way
subtitle: Motion
overview: Motion 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why mass doesn't affect fall time (ignoring air resistance)
Terminal velocity from air resistance

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: all objects accelerate at g = 9.8 m/s²

traps: Students say heavier objects fall faster — in a VACUUM, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of mass (Galileo's experiment); air resistance makes a feather fall slower than a hammer in atmosphere; on the moon (no air), both hit the ground simultaneously

title: What Work and Power Mean in Physics (Not in Life)
subtitle: Energy
overview: Energy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Work = force × distance in direction of force
Power = work / time

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: perpendicular force or no movement

traps: Students say holding a heavy box is 'hard work' in physics — physics work requires DISPLACEMENT in the direction of force; holding a box with no movement does ZERO WORK no matter how tiring it is; work requires both force AND movement in the force's direction

title: How Kinetic and Potential Energy Trade Off in Moving Objects
subtitle: Energy
overview: Energy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: KE = ½mv², PE = mgh
Conservation of mechanical energy (no friction)
Energy transformations on a roller coaster or pendulum

sections.title: How Kinetic and Potential Energy Trade Off in Moving Objects
traps: Students say a roller coaster has the most speed at the highest point — speed is maximum at the LOWEST point where KE is maximum (all PE converted to KE); at the highest point, PE is maximum and KE is minimum; height and speed are inversely related in a frictionless system

title: Why Energy Is Never Actually Lost (It Just Changes Form)
subtitle: Energy
overview: Energy 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Law of conservation of energy
Thermal energy as the destination of 'lost' energy

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: useful energy output vs. total input

traps: Students say friction 'destroys' energy — friction CONVERTS mechanical energy to THERMAL energy; total energy is conserved; the energy isn't gone, it's just in a less useful form; efficiency measures how much of the input energy becomes useful output

title: What Waves Actually Are and How They Move
subtitle: Waves and Light
overview: Waves and Light 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Transverse vs. longitudinal waves

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: v = fλ
more amplitude = more energy

traps: Students say faster waves have higher frequency — wave speed, frequency, and wavelength are related by v = fλ; if SPEED increases and frequency stays the same, WAVELENGTH increases; only frequency changes if you change the source, not the medium; medium changes speed and wavelength together

title: How Light Behaves When It Hits Different Materials
subtitle: Waves and Light
overview: Waves and Light 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Total internal reflection and critical angle

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
light bends when changing medium

traps: Students say light bends TOWARD normal when going from fast to slow medium — light bends TOWARD the normal when entering a denser medium (slowing down); it bends AWAY when entering a less dense medium (speeding up); this is why a straw appears bent in water

title: Why White Light Contains All Colors
subtitle: Waves and Light
overview: Waves and Light 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Master Why White Light Contains All Colors for the Waves and Light unit.

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: radio to gamma
ROY G BIV and frequency order
prism separating white light

traps: Students say red light has the highest frequency — RED has the LOWEST frequency and LONGEST wavelength in visible light; VIOLET has the highest frequency and shortest wavelength; energy increases with frequency: gamma rays have more energy than radio waves

title: What Electric Charge Is and How It Creates Force
subtitle: Electricity
overview: Electricity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Positive and negative charges; like charges repel
Static electricity and charge transfer
Insulators vs. conductors

sections.title: What Electric Charge Is and How It Creates Force
traps: Students say only electrons move when charging objects — in solids, only ELECTRONS (negative charges) move; protons are fixed in the nucleus; when a rod becomes positively charged, it LOST electrons, not GAINED protons; charging is always about electron transfer in solids

title: How Voltage, Current, and Resistance Work Together (Ohm's Law)
subtitle: Electricity
overview: Electricity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Voltage (V) = electric pressure; current (I) = flow rate

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: opposition to current
V = IR

traps: Students say higher voltage always means higher current — current depends on BOTH voltage and resistance: I = V/R; doubling voltage while also doubling resistance keeps current the SAME; you must consider both before predicting what happens to current

title: What Happens to Current and Voltage in Series vs. Parallel Circuits
subtitle: Electricity
overview: Electricity 단원의 핵심 주제예요. 아래 개념을 정확히 잡고, 빨간 함정을 피하는 데 집중하세요.
objectives: Why parallel is used in home wiring

sections.title: Key concepts

terms.def: same current everywhere, voltage divides
same voltage across branches, current divides

traps: Students say voltage divides in parallel circuits — in PARALLEL, each branch has the SAME voltage as the source; voltage DIVIDES in SERIES; this is why household circuits are parallel: every device gets the full voltage regardless of how many devices are on
